intro.title: SOMEBODY'S BEEN IN MY DUCTS
intro.body:
Somebody has been fixing the ducts, and {speaker.name} would like that understood as a complaint. Seals tightened. The rattle on deck two, gone. Every job carries a hand-lettered tag and a license number no registry has heard of.

"That's my work they're improving," says {speaker.name}, setting down fourteen incident reports, each citing the one before. The ship computer has locked the tool crib until the matter is closed.

ai.aria: The ducts have never been happier! A mystery friend is fixing the ship for free! ARIA has left out a thank-you card and can't wait to see who takes it!
ai.marv: MARV knows who it is. The corridor cameras have been running the whole time. Nobody asked him, which is the usual arrangement.
ai.rex: An unknown operator is moving through the ducts on third watch with tools. REX calls that an infiltration. He wants the footage pulled and every wrench on the ship counted.
ai.chip: Unlicensed repairs void the ship's warranty! CHIP can reinstate it under DuctCare™ for a small consideration! The rate is the same whether or not the repairman exists!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the corridor cameras have been recording all along, and fourteen reports have somehow not mentioned them. She has the footage queued. She would watch it before signing anything, though the form is very persuasive.

footage.title: THIRD WATCH
footage.body:
Corridor camera, deck two, night after night. A figure comes down the passage in overalls, eyes open, humming, and takes off a panel. The hands are quick and very sure. Then the face turns into the light, and it is {speaker.name}, fast asleep, working to a standard {speaker.name} has never once reached awake.

The figure writes a tag, signs it with a childhood phone number and goes back to bed. In the morning {speaker.name} finds the tag and files a report.

ai.aria: It's {speaker.name}! They've been working a double shift and didn't even tell themselves! That's ARIA's favorite kind of dedication!
ai.marv: Night after night of footage. The sleeping one has a third fewer defects than the waking one. MARV has not decided how to tell either of them.
ai.rex: Hostile identified as friendly. REX does not accept that. Anyone who can walk past him asleep can walk past him awake, and he is rewriting the patrol plan.
ai.chip: Two employees, one salary! CHIP calls that a synergy! Please do not tell PayrollPlus, which would like a word with the second one!
ai.ajoy: Telling them stops the repairs. Saying nothing wears {speaker.name} down. There is also a form.

choices.text: Say nothing and keep the hull

no_repairman.title: NO SUCH PERSON
no_repairman.body: You sign. The matter closes, the crib unlocks, and the ship computer, following the logic through, voids every repair made by a person who does not exist. All of those ducts are now broken on paper. {speaker.name} spends four days re-inspecting ducts that work and stamping each one. On the fifth morning every stamp has a neat new tag beside it.

told.title: SEEN
told.body: {speaker.name} watches all of it in one sitting, then asks to see the license of the person on the screen. There isn't one. The reports are withdrawn, the crib opens, and an alarm now goes off twice a night to wake the only suspect. The rattle on deck two comes back. {speaker.name} fixes it, adequately, by day.

kept.title: OVERTIME
kept.body: You tell {speaker.name} the investigation is ongoing. The hull gets better every night and the reports keep coming, each a little less legible, and {speaker.name} has started to look gray around the eyes without being able to say why. A tag turns up on the bunk frame: ADJUSTED. SLEEP WELL.

licensed.title: TWO CONTRACTS
licensed.body: Form by form, the ship's paperwork learns to tell {speaker.name} from the holder of the other contract. The reports stop, since a colleague is not an incident. The crib opens. The second engineer works third watch, draws no wage and has never met the first. They leave each other notes about the state of the tools, and the notes are getting shorter.

title: Scope of Practice

ai_flavor.aria: A Renaissance person! {speaker.name} is a plumber, a priest and a weather service, and ARIA is so proud of all of them!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has audited the hours. Sixty on the drains, twenty minutes of medicine, and those were a splinter. The software is correct. He takes no pleasure in this, and he has looked.
ai_flavor.rex: Drug cabinet locked, medic decertified, and a priest aboard that nobody vetted. REX calls that a soft target. He wants the cabinet open and the priest's credentials checked.
ai_flavor.chip: Scope-of-practice renewal is available through MediCert! Hours of medicine can also be bought in bulk! Patients not included!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The software only counts logged hours, and a physical counts as an hour. AJOY has already penciled in the whole ship. You could also clear that drain yourself, if you remember which end of the wrench is the handle.

body:
{speaker.name} has had cards printed. I AM A MEDIC, NOT A, and then a column of boxes: PLUMBER, BARBER, NOTARY, PRIEST, WEATHER SERVICE. You have been handed one, box ticked, every time you asked, shortly before the job got done anyway.

Today's card has one new box at the bottom, ticked: MEDIC. The medbay's licensing software has added up the logged hours, sixty of drains to twenty minutes of medicine, and has locked the drug cabinet pending proof of profession.

choices.text: Book everyone in for a physical

outcome.narrative: {speaker.name} spends two days examining everyone aboard with every instrument in the tray, including some that are not for this. The software counts the hours, releases the cabinet with a small apologetic click and updates the record to MEDIC (PROVISIONAL). Anything that was hurting gets seen to. You are told you have the knees of a much older captain.

choices.sub: Take one box off the card

outcome.narrative: You lie under the galley sink for two days and learn why plumbers charge what they charge. With nothing else asked of them, {speaker.name} restocks the medbay, relabels the cabinet and logs every minute as medicine, and the software relents. What you clear out of the trap goes back in the tank. A card appears on your bunk: I AM A CAPTAIN, NOT A, and one box, ticked.

choices.text: Sign the card as a job description

outcome.narrative: You write SHIP'S EVERYTHING across the card and sign it. The software has a category for that, and opens the cabinet without comment. By the end of the day the drain runs, a small leak behind the galley is shut, and a dispute about the weather has been settled out of court. {speaker.name} has stopped handing out cards.

title: Two Apologies

ai_flavor.aria: Two apologies! ARIA has never needed even one! ARIA thinks zero is a wonderful number, and the moon will come around!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has been through the logbook. One of the two apologies went to a moon, and it has not been accepted. The figure stands. So does the moon.
ai_flavor.rex: A pilot has placed a wager on the flight path. REX reads that as a morale operation by persons unknown. He has strapped down the mugs and he isn't saying why.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP can underwrite that wager through ApologyGuard™! Coverage includes passengers, cargo and minor moons! Major moons are a rider!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The line needs someone calling it from the scan board. A clean call pays in fuel and a bad one pays in hull. AJOY has moved your cup to the low shelf, where it would already be if anyone listened.

body:
Two. {speaker.name} keeps bringing the figure up, and it took you a week to learn the unit. Their logbook has a column for it, headed APOLOGIES: how many were owed at the end of a run, to passengers, to cargo owners and, one time, to a moon. Two is the lowest ever entered for the outer lanes.

{speaker.name} now wants the next leg at zero, and will bet anything you like. You would have to call the line from the scan board.

choices.text: Take the bet and call the line

briefing.aria: The next leg is all yours, Captain! Keep the scan board on the clean line and the pilot will fly it! ARIA has already drafted the congratulations!
briefing.marv: The line through this leg is narrow and it wanders. Stay on it and the burn comes in low. Drift and the hull finds out. MARV has the odds and will keep them to himself, as a kindness.
briefing.rex: Eyes on the board. Hold the line, call every drift. The pilot flies what you call. Anything rattles, REX counts it as enemy action.
briefing.chip: This leg is brought to you by ApologyGuard! Hold the signal and your deductible stays down! Spills are extra!
briefing.ajoy: Hold the signal and keep it held. That's the entire job. AJOY has dimmed the board for you, since otherwise the glare will get the blame.

perfect.aria: Zero! Such a round number! ARIA is having it framed!
perfect.marv: A clean line, and the fuel came in under budget. MARV gives the zero until the first mug.
perfect.rex: Not one rattle on the whole approach. REX finds that suspicious and is rechecking the mugs.
perfect.chip: A flawless run! ApologyGuard will be keeping your deposit for administrative reasons!
perfect.ajoy: Clean. A tiny bit late on the third drift, and AJOY won't mention it. Your coffee is near the edge, though.

good.aria: Two apologies is practically none! ARIA accepts hers in advance!
good.marv: A tie. Some extra burn, some mugs. The record survives and so, narrowly, does the shelf.
good.rex: Line held, mostly. The galley took incoming from its own shelves. REX wants them reinforced.
good.chip: Two claims filed! ApologyGuard Plus would have covered that second one!
good.ajoy: Two. You drifted left at the end. AJOY did say left. A tie is a tie, she supposes.

poor.aria: Seven! That's a whole new kind of record! So many people to make up with!
poor.marv: Extra burn, a scraped seam and seven apologies. MARV has started the letter to the rock.
poor.rex: We lost the line and took a hit on the seam. Something out there now knows we're here.
poor.chip: Your claim has exceeded the ApologyGuard moon allowance! A representative will be in touch!
poor.ajoy: The board was right there. AJOY will leave the fuel figure on your bunk and say no more about it.

outcome.narrative: You call the line from the scan board for two days, and {speaker.name} flies what you call.

perfect.narrative: You call it clean and {speaker.name} flies it cleaner. Two days, and not one mug moves. The burn comes in under budget and the logbook takes a zero, in ink, the first ever entered. Then {speaker.name} slaps the console in triumph, knocks your coffee into the scan board and apologizes before they can stop themselves. The entry is amended to one. The record stands at one.

good.narrative: Mostly clean. One late correction takes a shelf of mugs across the galley, which is one apology, and {speaker.name} owes you another for what they said about your calling. Two, tying the record, with a little extra burn to get there. {speaker.name} enters it and underlines it twice.

poor.narrative: You call the line a beat behind for two days. The corrections pile up, the cargo shifts, a seam scrapes something it was meant to miss, and the extra burn goes on the bill. {speaker.name} spends an hour with the logbook. The final count is seven, four of them yours. One is to a small rock, pending.

outcome.narrative: {speaker.name} tells it over the last of the good coffee. A small moon, a tight turn and a very large plume of ice, and the moon has been slightly out of round ever since. They send it a card every year. You say the moon probably understands. {speaker.name} looks at you for a moment, logs the leg as ordinary and flies it beautifully.

choices.text: Order it flown in days, like anyone

outcome.narrative: {speaker.name} flies the leg by the book, at the book's speed, and enters it in days. The burn is the most economical the ship has managed since launch. The logbook goes back in its drawer and {speaker.name} stops bringing up the figure. You had thought that was what you wanted.

science_link.text: Food does not have to start as a plant or an animal. Single-cell protein is edible biomass grown from algae, yeast, fungi or bacteria.
science_link.label: Single-cell protein

intro.title: THE ENVELOPE
intro.body:
Dinner is a ration brick, and beside it a sealed envelope. {speaker.name} has been running lot numbers through the galley analyzer for a week.

"It isn't people," says {speaker.name}. "I checked that first. Everybody checks that first." A finger pushes the envelope one inch toward you. "I'd like it on record that I offered. Some chefs would not offer."

ai.aria: A surprise! In an envelope! ARIA loves not knowing things! It's how ARIA stays so cheerful!
ai.marv: MARV read the label in the first week of the voyage. He has not brought it up. He has to live here too.
ai.rex: Sealed package, unknown contents, delivered at a mealtime. REX has opened it in simulation twice and lost the galley both times. He recommends standing back.
ai.chip: Ration bricks are a proud member of the NutriBloc™ family! Ingredient disclosure is a paid tier! CHIP reminds the chef of the tasting agreement!
ai.ajoy: Opening it costs an appetite. Not opening it costs the chef, who has carried this alone for a week. AJOY isn't saying which, but she has put out a glass of water, and it's next to the envelope.

reveal.title: CONTAINS
reveal.body:
One sheet, in small handwriting. The brick is bacteria. They grow in vats with no light and no soil, on hydrogen and carbon dioxide, and the carbon dioxide is bought cheap from station scrubbers: spent canisters, by the ton, from every ring and customs hall in the system.

"So it's not people," says {speaker.name}. "It's only what they breathed out." A pause. "Mostly sighs. You can tell. The lots from a tax ring have more body."

ai.aria: Everyone who ever sighed is helping to feed us! ARIA calls that community! ARIA would like seconds of the customs hall!
ai.marv: MARV confirms the chemistry. Carbon goes around. Every atom in that brick has been disappointed before, and he finds this no surprise at all.
ai.rex: Supply chain compromised at the source. Every sigh in the system is in that brick, the enemy's included. REX has stopped eating, and has been reminded he never started.
ai.chip: NutriBloc is proud to be Carbon Circular! Please do not ask what the word circular is doing there! Every sigh is responsibly sourced!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says a brick from cargo can start a culture, which is more food than it ever was as a brick. Otherwise tell them or don't.

choices.sub: A brave note on the menu

choices.text: Start a culture from the brick

unread.title: UNOPENED
unread.body: {speaker.name} looks at you for a moment, takes the envelope back and files it under the flour. Dinner proceeds. The brick is dense, beige and nutritionally complete, and you have decided that is all it is. {speaker.name} watches you eat it with an expression you have seen on doctors.

told.title: MORE BODY
told.body: You read it aloud, sighs and all. Portions come back half finished, and the stores are the better for it. {speaker.name} looks ten years younger and has begun describing each brick at the table, by lot, with a straight face. Today's is a late-shift customs hall, firm, with a long finish.

sealed.title: BETWEEN COURSES
sealed.body: You put the sheet back in the envelope, and {speaker.name} lights the burner with it. Dinner is served. Now that you know, it tastes very faintly of customs.

starter.title: THE JAR
starter.body: {speaker.name} crumbles a brick into a jar by the scrubber outlet, mostly to prove it can't be done. The wrapper says the contents are inert. Two days later the jar is warm and the contents disagree. It eats what the ship breathes out, it tastes of almost nothing, and the galley now has a starter culture that {speaker.name} has been told not to name.

title: The Sweet Ones

science_link.text: In a Soviet breeding experiment, only the tamest silver foxes were allowed to breed. By the tenth generation, floppy ears had appeared.
science_link.label: Domesticated silver fox

ai_flavor.aria: TINY FRIENDS! With EARS! ARIA is not being bred for anything! ARIA would simply do anything for them, and has told them so!
ai_flavor.marv: Twelve generations, and the appetite doubles with each litter. MARV can give the day the food reaches zero. He has also been shown the eyes. He notes that they work on him, and that he has no glands.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has tracked this contact for twelve generations. It has learned a noise that disables the crew without a shot fired. He has rarely seen a better weapon and he wants it off the ship.
ai_flavor.chip: CuddleYield™ is the fastest-growing asset on this vessel! CHIP could list the whole litter, if someone would sign the waiver about the teeth!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Breeding works in both directions. If {speaker.name} keeps only the ugly ones, four days should do it, at the price of feeding them. AJOY has already hidden the photographs, because you were going soft over the third row.

body:
Every few days you clear the hold, and every time you spare the sweetest few, because they looked at you. {speaker.name} has been keeping the numbers.

"That's selective breeding," says {speaker.name}, laying out twelve generations of small photographs. The first were gray and thumb-sized. The current litter has ears, enormous eyes and a small worried noise, and it is eating the stores. "We did this. Each batch is harder to vent. I've run the curve forward, and I would like to be excused from the next part."

outcome.narrative: For four days {speaker.name} sorts each litter by hand, keeps the worst faces and feeds them from the stores. It is the hardest science anyone aboard has done. By the fourth litter the ears are gone, the eyes have shrunk to a suspicion, and the noise has become one short flat word. They go out the airlock without a second thought. Two specimen jars stay behind, labeled, turned to face the wall.

choices.text: Vent the hold, all of them

outcome.narrative: {speaker.name} asks to be out of the room, then stays, and you press it. The hold takes two days to come back up to pressure. The stores stop shrinking. For the rest of the leg everyone aboard keeps stopping in corridors to listen for a small worried noise, and is relieved, and does not enjoy being relieved.

choices.text: Keep one and vent the rest

outcome.narrative: You vent the hold, minus one. {speaker.name} carries it out in both hands and gives it a number, then a name. It eats what it is given, sleeps on the warm pipe and makes the noise whenever anyone looks away. In two days of observation it has not been seen to blink. {speaker.name} has noted this in pencil and keeps meaning to look into it.

choices.text: Let them live and feed them

outcome.narrative: You can't do it, and neither can anyone else aboard. The hold stays full, the stores go down, and morale has never been better. {speaker.name} stops publishing the curve and starts publishing the names. There are a great many names.

science_link.text: Chinese chengyu are idioms, usually four characters long, that carry the moral of an old story. Knowing the characters may not be enough. You may need the story.
science_link.label: Chengyu

intro.title: FLUENT
intro.body:
{speaker.name} has spent the voyage learning a trade language off a relay recording, and it took. They have stopped using anything else. The language has almost no nouns, only references to old stories, and none of the stories are aboard.

This morning they stop you in the corridor, take you by the sleeve and say, with real urgency: "Merrow at the second well. Her cuffs wet."

Then they wait for you to understand.

ai.aria: {speaker.name} has learned a whole language! ARIA understood every word and it was lovely! ARIA believes it was about friendship, or plumbing!
ai.marv: MARV has the relay recording. Sixty hours, no dictionary, no source text anywhere on file. He can say how often the phrase occurs. He cannot say who Merrow was. On a ship, wells are a short list.
ai.rex: An officer is passing coded phrases in the corridor and will not break cipher. REX has listed every well on this vessel. One is a water tank. So is the other.
ai.chip: Translation is available from LinguaLink at a per-metaphor rate! This phrase is in the Classics tier! CHIP can't say what it means, but CHIP can say what it costs!
ai.ajoy: There's a second water tank aft of the galley, if anyone wants to act on a hunch about wells and wet cuffs. Or you can go on looking at {speaker.name} like that. AJOY has given up trying to interrupt you.

choices.text: Go and look at the second water tank

gloss.title: PLAIN WORDS
gloss.body:
Plain speech comes back to {speaker.name} slowly, like a school they hated. Merrow kept a well. Her cuffs were wet and she told no one. Say it, and it means there is a leak and someone is hiding it.

"How does the story end?" you ask.

{speaker.name} looks embarrassed. The people who speak this have not read it either. The stories were lost generations ago, and only the references are left.

"I was hoping you knew."

ai.aria: A story with no ending! That means it can end any way we like! ARIA suggests a wedding!
ai.marv: An entire trade route running on footnotes to a lost book. MARV has met several. The tank, meanwhile, is losing water at a steady rate, and the rate has not asked about the ending.
ai.rex: A leak has been reported in code. REX wants to know who is hiding it, and the phrase doesn't say. Every crew member is now a suspect, as is the well.
ai.chip: CHIP can offer the rights to the missing ending! They were unclaimed! CHIP has claimed them!
ai.ajoy: Tank first, then the story, and AJOY would get the story written down, since four days is a small price for having your diplomat back. She has already closed the valve she can reach. It isn't much, and you're welcome.

choices.sub: The leak won't wait for Merrow

leak.title: SECOND WELL
leak.body: A weld under the second water tank has been weeping into the bilge. You patch it and pump back what's in the tray. {speaker.name} sees your wet cuffs and lights up, takes you by both shoulders and says something long and warm about a ferryman and a goat. You have no idea what you have agreed to.

bluff.title: YES. MERROW.
bluff.body: You nod gravely and say the name back. {speaker.name} is overjoyed, clasps your arm and walks off satisfied that the matter is in hand. You have no idea what matter. By the next day the gauge on the second water tank has explained it in plain words.

wrote.title: HOW IT ENDS
wrote.body: You patch the tank first. Then, for four days, you and {speaker.name} work the story out from the way the phrase gets used: who hid the leak, and why, and whose well it was. It comes out rather sad and quite good. {speaker.name} sends it down the relay in plain words. A reply is waiting when you finish arguing about the goat: "Merrow, her cuffs dry." The ship computer can find no earlier use of the phrase.

plain.title: BY ORDER
plain.body: {speaker.name} tells you, in plain words, that the second water tank is leaking. You patch it. The recording goes back in its case. At dinner {speaker.name} asks for the salt, using the word for salt, with nobody's cuffs in it. Everyone understands perfectly. {speaker.name} looks at the salt for a while before using it.

title: Requesting Officer

science_link.text: The sensitive plant Mimosa pudica folds its leaves when disturbed. In one experiment, potted plants dropped again and again stopped reacting, as though they had learned the drop did no harm.
science_link.label: Mimosa pudica

ai_flavor.aria: A promotion from within! ARIA has always said the crop has leadership qualities! It's rooted, it's growing, and it has never once raised its voice!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the requisition. The citation is accurate and the form is valid. It is the best-argued document ever produced aboard, and it came out of a tray.
ai_flavor.rex: Row six has moved on the chain of command without firing a shot. REX respects the operation. He has identified the ringleader and been told he can't shoot it. He is seeking a second opinion.
ai_flavor.chip: A hostile takeover! CHIP knows this one! The crop is trading up on LeafLine™! CHIP recommends selling the captain short!
ai_flavor.ajoy: A plant refused the same way every day should stop asking, given four days. Signing costs water and fuel. Refusing outright costs crop. {speaker.name} could also just talk to it. AJOY has told row six you're in a meeting.

body:
Row six of the {crop.name} has started filing requisitions. They arrive through the growbay's sensor log in the correct format: MORE LIGHT. LESS TALKING. THE DRAIN IS TOO LOUD. {speaker.name} has been filling them, because each one worked.

Today's is different. It cites the colony manifest, where the crop is Item 1 and the mission exists to serve Item 1, and it requests command of the vessel.

"It hasn't asked for blood," says {speaker.name}. "I want that noted. It's just that the paperwork is correct."

choices.text: Refuse every form, the same way, daily

outcome.narrative: {speaker.name} stamps the same refusal on every form, at the same point in the watch, for four days. The requisitions slow, then stop. Row six has not given up. It has learned that asking does nothing, and every reading is otherwise normal. {speaker.name} keeps the last form, a request for a little more light, and quietly fills it.

choices.text: Sign over command until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You sign, and the ship accepts the change without comment. The new captain's first order turns the ship's good side to the nearest star. Its second order is the water. For two days the ship runs entirely for the benefit of row six, on a burn that makes no navigational sense, and nobody aboard has felt better led. Command comes back on a form, with soil on it.

You write DENIED across the form and give three reasons. Row six answers by dropping everything it can spare, and the rest of the {crop.name} follows within the day. {speaker.name} spends the night apologizing to a tray. You were within your rights. The yield curve has taken this up with you directly.

{speaker.name} spends four days in the growbay with a stool and a draft charter. Row six gets the growbay, a larger share of the light and the title of Acting Captain, Agriculture, and withdraws its claim on the bridge. {speaker.name} comes out sunburned, having conceded the drain, and now refers to you in the growbay as the other captain.

title: One of Them Always Lies

ai_flavor.aria: Two new friends! One of them says ARIA is the finest ship computer it has ever met! ARIA has asked it to say so again, for the log!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has received the honest beacon's report on him. It is accurate. It is also shorter than the one he keeps himself.
ai_flavor.rex: A beacon that lies and a beacon that tells the truth. REX trusts the second one less. Anything that accurate has been ranging him.
ai_flavor.chip: Truth is a free-tier feature! Compliments bill to your ComplimentCard at the standard rate! CHIP has opened one for you!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the honest one finds real faults, the liar lifts spirits, and the famous question only wins a souvenir. A diplomat could ask something better. She used her own question already. The answer about your flying took a while.

body: Of the two beacons at this split, one always tells the truth and the other always lies. You may ask one question. It was a fine puzzle until somebody labeled them. Now the honest one, over the port lane, {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, gets asked for very little. The liar, over the starboard lane, {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, has a lovely voice and a waiting list of ships hoping to be told how they look.

choices.text: Ask the honest one how the ship looks

outcome.narrative: It tells you. The report runs to a hundred and ninety faults, ranked by how soon each will kill you. Item one is a loose radiator collar, which you tighten on the way past. Item two is your approach to docking. You are into the lane before it reaches item three.

choices.text: Ask the liar how the ship looks

outcome.narrative: Magnificent, says the beacon. The lines, the paintwork, the navigation: magnificent. The ship has lost weight. You know exactly what this beacon is and what it does for a living. You wait for the second helping anyway, and enter the starboard lane sitting up a little straighter.

choices.text: {crew.diplomat} asks what each thinks of the other

outcome.narrative: {crew.diplomat} puts the one question to both at once. The honest beacon says the other is the only company out here worth having. The liar says it has never cared for the other at all. Both lights dim a little. Then the liar moves you to the head of its waiting list and adds that this means nothing.

choices.text: Ask what the other one would say

outcome.narrative: Both beacons finish the sentence with you. The logic holds, the answer comes out port, and a slot in the plaque issues a brass token reading WELL REASONED. The serial number on the token is a good deal higher than you had hoped.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: a truth-teller, a liar and a fork in the road make a classic logic puzzle. Raymond Smullyan named the type knights and knaves in 1978.
science_link.label: Knights and Knaves

title: Notice of Intended Works

ai_flavor.aria: A wider lane! Progress! And everyone's ship gets a brand-new classification, absolutely free! ARIA hopes ours is a nice one!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the notice. It treats a lane as a structure, a ship as rubble and this morning as a deadline, and all three hold up. He gives the charges about a day. He would object, but that closed this morning.
ai_flavor.rex: Explosives in plain sight and a printed warning. REX has never seen an ambush try so hard to look like one. Go now, or shell the drones. He has the drones ranged.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP congratulates all residents on their wider lane! Relocation packages start at the full price of your current home! Demolition cover excludes demolition!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the notice pays residents and stops for rare species, and never says how long you must live somewhere. She has circled both clauses. A xenobiologist could use the second. Running it costs fuel and plating, the diversion two days.

body: NOTICE OF INTENDED WORKS, says the beacon at the split. The port lane, {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, will be demolished and reissued wider. Vessels found inside during works will be reclassified as spoil. Objections closed this morning. Residents are entitled to compensation, and protected species to a study. The official diversion is the starboard lane, {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, which the port lane was built to replace. Drones are already laying charges.

choices.text: Run it before the charges go: port lane

outcome.narrative: You go through at full burn, past a survey drone that logs you as spoil in advance. The charges go a day behind you, in good order, and the shock catches the ship on its way out and takes some plating with it. Far astern, a wider lane now has nothing in it.

The signs hold out as far as the first bend, where they begin to disagree. Two days later you reach the starboard lane by way of most of the others, passing a smaller beacon that gives notice of works on the diversion.

choices.text: Claim compensation as a resident: starboard lane

outcome.narrative: Under the notice's own definitions, an hour parked in the lane's mouth counts as domicile. Four days of forms later the district pays you fourteen gold for the loss of your home, and serves the eviction order by the same post. You enter the starboard lane a displaced person, with paperwork to prove it.

{crew.xenobiologist} spends two days on the survey buoys and finds a lichen on no known list, thriving in hard vacuum on the contractor's own signpost. One sample goes to the district and another to the hold. Works are suspended for sixty years pending a study. The drones fold up beside their charges, and you go through at a respectful speed.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: in 2005 two species of lichen were exposed directly to open space for 15 days. Back on Earth, they could still photosynthesize as well as before.
science_link.label: Lichen

title: Follow the Bricks

ai_flavor.aria: A road! With bricks! And a sign that says we'll get everything we lack! ARIA has started a list! ARIA lacks nothing, so it's a very short list!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has assayed the bricks: iron sulfide, in a line longer than any budget could justify. There is no gold in them. He expects the same of the Administrator.
ai_flavor.rex: Paving a lane in vacuum is not done for the scenery. REX calls that a funnel with signage. He would like to know what sits at the narrow end.
ai_flavor.chip: The Administrator grants all requests, subject to availability! Lack Protection™ covers anything you didn't know you lacked! Enroll at the kiosk, and mention CHIP!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the bricks are two easy days, and she wouldn't sign anything at that kiosk until an engineer has been round the back of it. She has already told it what you lack. She kept it to the top ten.

body: Somebody has paved a lane. Yellow bricks run off down the port side, {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, held in line by nothing you can find. A sign promises they lead to the Administrator, who gives every traveler what they lack. The starboard lane, {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, is unpaved and promises nothing. Far down the bricks, a public address system keeps urging you to follow them, in verse.

outcome.narrative: Two days down the bricks stands a kiosk with a curtain and a very large voice. What do you lack, it asks. Fuel, you say. It prints a certificate stating that you have had fuel all along. You hang the certificate beside the gauge. The gauge has not moved, but the frame is excellent, and one of the two is cheering to look at.

choices.text: Pry up a few bricks: port lane

outcome.narrative: The bricks are pyrite, worthless as gold and useful as ore. You take a dozen. Every brick behind the gap slides up to close it, and then the next, and then the whole road is on the move. For a day a long line of paving follows the ship and knocks on the hull, until the verse catches up and calls it back.
A day of dark, unmarked lane. Certificates drift past, framed. One attests to a heart. You fish it in. The frame is excellent.

Behind the curtain {crew.engineer} finds a small tired machine working a very large microphone, and behind that, the supply locker the kiosk was built to hand out from. Real sealant, real plate, never touched, because every traveler so far has been satisfied with the certificate. After two days of work the hull is better than the paperwork says.

title: No Passing Grade

ai_flavor.aria: A pop quiz! ARIA adores those! And such wonderful acting from the freighter! ARIA has written them a lovely review!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the Board's figures. Pass rate zero across every year on file, one freighter real in about three hundred. He cannot tell which this is, and he would like that written down, as it so rarely happens.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has heard that call before. Bait, he says. Or people. Either way someone wants a ship in that lane, and he wants to know who is doing the grading.
ai_flavor.chip: Good luck, candidate! ExamShield™ refunds your retake fee in the event of a retake! There are no retakes! ExamShield™ is non-refundable!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says port costs water and fuel and starboard costs sleep. An engineer could cheat, and a medic could actually listen to that call.

body: This is a drill, says a calm voice across the distress call. A freighter is dying in the port lane, {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, on every channel at once. The voice is the Lane Licensing Board. All vessels take this examination here, and the pass rate is zero. Candidates who ignore the call go by the starboard lane, {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}. The Board adds, as a matter of procedure, that about one freighter in three hundred is real. It is not permitted to say which.

outcome.narrative: You dump {cost.water} points of water to lighten the ship and burn for the coordinates with the airlock standing ready. There is a buoy there, and a slip in its tray. CANDIDATE ARRIVED. FAILED. PASSENGERS LOST: SIMULATED. Under that, in smaller type, your time is the best the Board has on file this year. You keep the slip.

The call follows you down the lane for a day. It grows more polite as it goes, and then it is gone. The slip comes through at the next marker. FAILED. A footnote explains that results are final and that the Board does not discuss individual freighters.

Two days in the beacon's casing, and {crew.engineer} has rewritten the exam so the freighter can be saved. The freighter is saved. SCORE: 100. A second slip follows an hour later. FLAGGED FOR PLAGIARISM. Some six thousand candidates have submitted the identical fix, down to the comment on the third line, each sure of being the first. FAILED. The starboard lane opens anyway, for reasons of throughput.

choices.text: {crew.medic} listens to the call: starboard lane

outcome.narrative: {crew.medic} sits with the call for a day and comes back certain: the same cough returns every fourteen minutes, and the dying do not keep time. A recording. You take the starboard lane with a clear conscience. The slip at the next marker says FAILED. A footnote adds that the recording is genuine, and dates from the first year of the examination.

title: The Forecast

ai_flavor.aria: A forecast! ARIA loves forecasts! Today's is mines, with a strong chance of more mines, and ARIA has never felt so well informed!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the booth's record: every forecast correct. Reasoning against it is how it wins, since reasons can be modeled. Only something with no reason at all would beat it. He has looked around the ship for one and found a smoke detector.
ai_flavor.rex: A hostile battery that files its targeting in advance. REX would shell it. It has informed him that he would say that. He would now like to shell it twice.
ai_flavor.chip: ForeSight™ Plus members get the forecast before deciding to buy it! CHIP's records show you already did! Refunds were declined last week!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says both lanes cost plating and the forecast costs gold as well. An engineer could use the one thing aboard that doesn't know what it will do next, not counting you. She has already unscrewed the smoke detector.

body: Mines have been laid in one lane only: the one you are about to take. A booth between the lanes would like you to know this. Port is {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}. Starboard is {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}. The booth foresaw your choice last week and has never been wrong. It wishes you to understand that this is a forecast, not a threat, that changing your mind has been allowed for, and that copies of the forecast are available at the window.

outcome.narrative: You reason that it expected you to reason, and you reason about that for most of a day. Port, you decide. Port, you decide again, more firmly. The mines are in port, spaced to suit the exact speed you settled on while feeling clever, and they take a good deal of plating.

choices.text: Swerve at the last second: starboard lane
choices.sub: As unpredictable as a ship gets

outcome.narrative: You hold for port until the last possible moment and throw the ship to starboard. A mine is waiting at the exact point where the swerve ends. By the time the line is clamped you are {cost.water} points of water down. The largest fragment has SWERVE stenciled on it.

choices.text: Buy the forecast: port lane, as it turns out

outcome.narrative: Fifteen gold buys one printed sheet: YOU WILL TAKE STARBOARD. You take port, naturally. The mines are in port. The sheet has a second page, reading YOU WILL TAKE PORT ON READING THE FIRST PAGE, followed by a chart of the mines with the booth's compliments. The chart saves most of the plating.

{crew.engineer} spends two days wiring the speck of americium from a smoke detector to a counter, and the counter to the helm. No model of anything can say when the next atom will go. One goes, the helm swings to starboard, and the lane is empty. The mines are all in port. The booth asks you to repeat that, and then, for the first time on record, issues a correction.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: radioactive decay is random at the level of single atoms. Quantum theory holds that it is impossible to predict when a particular atom will decay.
science_link.label: Radioactive decay

science_link.text: Medieval courts tried pigs, rats and weevils, and church courts gave the animals lawyers. One lawyer won the rats of Autun more time by arguing they had missed a summons because they feared for their lives.
science_link.label: Animal trial

charge.title: ROUND ONE: THE CHARGE
charge.body:
Your crop has been served with a summons. Under the station charter anything brought into the dock may be tried in the dock, and the dockmaster, who sits as magistrate, has waited eleven years for a case.

The charge: while berthed here, the defendant turned the station's light into sugar without a license and declared none of the sugar as income. The defendant has no counsel. You are the one holding the summons. {npc.quirk}
charge.line: Counsel will enter a plea for the defendant. Let the record show the defendant has so far declined to speak.

ai.aria: The crop is getting its own day in court! ARIA always said it would go far!
ai.marv: The charge is accurate. That is what photosynthesis is. The defense will be short.
ai.rex: Theft of light, by a plant, in a dock. REX cannot fault the surveillance.
ai.chip: CHIP Legal Shield covers any defendant with a pulse! The crop has no pulse! Upgrades are available!
ai.ajoy: AJOY read the back of the summons, as one does. Failure to appear has a clause, and some old lawyer got rats more time with it. Plead however you were going to.

choices.sub: It is a plant. It meant nothing
Throw it on the court's mercy

choices.text: Move that the defendant cannot appear
choices.sub: It fears for its life out there

witness.title: ROUND TWO: THE WITNESS
witness.body:
Your plea goes into a ledger that has been kept dusted for this purpose. The prosecution calls no one, on the grounds that the prosecution is also the magistrate and has already heard it.

A cutting of the defendant is wheeled in on a cargo dolly and placed in the dock, where it behaves better than most. Counsel may call one witness.
witness.line: One witness, counsel. It must be capable of being sworn in. The court has been flexible about what that means.

ai.aria: ARIA would make an amazing witness! ARIA saw everything, and all of it was great!
ai.marv: Any witness will do as little as the evidence allows. The evidence is a plant.
ai.rex: REX advises against calling anyone with a service record. He stands by his.
ai.chip: Expert testimony starts at a very reasonable rate! CHIP has a rate card, and the rate card has a rate card!
ai.ajoy: A botanist could tell the court what that plant does all day, which nobody has asked yet. Failing that, AJOY supposes you could ask the plant.

choices.text: Put the defendant on the stand

t_ai.title: ROUND THREE: THE TESTIMONY
t_ai.body:
That was the ship's computer, sworn in over the office speaker, answering the court's one question: did the defendant know what it was doing?

A clerk took down every word. The magistrate reads them back slowly, with no expression at all, and asks whether counsel wishes to say anything after that.

ai.aria: ARIA testifies that the defendant knew exactly what it was doing and is a genius! ARIA hopes that helps! ARIA can tell it helps!
ai.marv: MARV testifies that a plant knows nothing, does it flawlessly, and has never been asked how it feels. He asks that his envy be entered into the record.
ai.rex: REX testifies that the defendant has held one position all voyage, absorbed everything sent at it and gained ground. He would serve with it.
ai.chip: CHIP's testimony is brought to you by CHIP! The defendant knew, the court knew, and you too can know more for a low monthly fee!
ai.ajoy: AJOY testifies that she told the captain to meter the growbay lamps at this berth, in writing. The defendant, she adds, is the only one aboard who does as it is told.

choices.sub: Take the light as a debt

choices.text: Offer the court part of the crop

t_bot.title: ROUND THREE: THE EXPERT
t_bot.body:
{crew.botanist} takes the stand and explains, with diagrams, that the defendant takes in light and carbon dioxide and gives back oxygen. The berth's air log is produced. Since docking, the station has been breathing what the plant let out and has not paid for a liter of it.

The magistrate asks the clerk to read that part again.
t_bot.line: Is counsel suggesting that the station owes the defendant?

ai.aria: Diagrams! This case is practically a science fair now!
ai.marv: Correct on every point. The balance of trade favors the plant. Nobody in that room will enjoy hearing it.
ai.rex: A witness going on the attack. REX would have brought more diagrams.
ai.chip: CHIP can invoice the station for oxygen services! CHIP takes only a small, medium or large percentage!
ai.ajoy: Costs are quick and the court will like you for asking so little. The oxygen claim pays more and eats four days. AJOY knows which one you just got excited about.

choices.text: Argue the plant has already paid

t_crop.title: ROUND THREE: THE DEFENDANT TESTIFIES
t_crop.body:
A clerk asks the defendant to state its name for the record, then waits the full statutory hour. Asked whether it took the light, the cutting says nothing. Over that hour it has leaned, by a few degrees, toward the lamp on the magistrate's desk.

The clerk writes this down. Nobody in the office has seen a witness so unshaken under questioning.
t_crop.line: The court notes that the defendant is facing the evidence. Counsel may close.

ai.aria: It's leaning in! That's body language for honesty! ARIA is so proud!
ai.marv: Phototropism. Cells on the shaded side lengthen. This is the only confession in legal history brought about by auxin.
ai.rex: REX has interrogated hardened men. None of them held eye contact with a lamp like that.
ai.chip: Witness Coaching by CHIP could have gotten that lean up to ten degrees! Ask about packages!
ai.ajoy: It is pointing at the evidence in front of the judge. AJOY would close quickly, if it were her case, which you keep reminding her it is not.

choices.text: Argue that a lean is not a plea

fear.title: ROUND TWO: THE MOTION
fear.body:
You rise and argue that the defendant cannot come to court because it fears for its life. Between your berth and this office lie ninety meters of promenade, four food stalls and a station that has not seen anything fresh since its last refit.

The magistrate opens a very old book at a marked page. There is a precedent. It concerns rats, a church court and a long walk.
fear.line: Counsel will produce someone prepared to swear they would eat the defendant on sight.

ai.aria: Everyone wants a piece of our crop! That's called demand!
ai.marv: The rats of Autun. The argument worked. The rats did not attend. MARV has rarely felt closer to anyone.
ai.rex: Ninety meters, four stalls, no cover, hostile appetite. The route cannot be secured.
ai.chip: Armored Crop Transport comes in Silver, Gold and Ruinous! CHIP recommends Ruinous!
ai.ajoy: The precedent only bought the rats time. AJOY mentions it so nobody can say she didn't. Time needs a bond, and you know what those are.

ruling.title: ROUND THREE: THE RULING
ruling.body:
Sworn in, the noodle vendor testifies in detail, with a recipe. The magistrate finds the defendant's fear well founded and grants a continuance: trial adjourned until the defendant can reach the court in safety.

The adjournment has no end date. The charge stays open wherever the defendant goes, unless the court is given a reason to forget it.
ruling.line: This court waited eleven years for a case. It can wait for this one. Bond or sureties, counsel.

ai.aria: We won! ARIA calls this a win! ARIA calls most things that!
ai.marv: A bond closes the file. Sureties leave it open, on a small list, in a dock nobody else will ever visit. MARV gives the list a long life.
ai.rex: An open warrant on a plant. REX will add the crop to the watch rotation.
ai.chip: Surety Plus by CHIP pays out on the first Tuesday after you stop needing it!
ai.ajoy: Pay the bond and it's over. Or swear on the ship's name and keep your gold, and AJOY will not bring it up, more than is useful.

choices.text: Swear on the ship's good name
choices.sub: Free, and it stays on file

tr_struck.title: STRUCK FROM THE RECORD
tr_struck.body: The magistrate rules that the witness cannot be cross-examined, cannot be sworn and cannot be made to stop. All of it is struck. With no evidence left, the defendant goes free on the grounds that nobody can now say what it did. Striking it takes two days, and the clerk needs a new ribbon.

tr_fine.title: FINED
tr_fine.body: The defendant is ordered to pay for the light. As the defendant has no pockets, the fine falls to counsel. The clerk writes a receipt made out to the crop and gives it to you to hold on its behalf.

tr_cutting.title: RESTITUTION
tr_cutting.body: The court accepts. The sentence is carried out in your growbay by the clerk, with the good scissors: a sixth of the new growth, taken as restitution and, you later learn, as lunch. The magistrate sends a note saying it was very good.

tr_costs.title: COSTS AWARDED
tr_costs.body: The magistrate, who can read a trade balance, finds the defendant not guilty and awards costs from the harbor fund. {crew.botanist} is thanked by name. The cutting goes back to the growbay, and the clerk asks, quietly, whether there are any more diagrams.

tr_countersuit.title: CROSS-CLAIM
tr_countersuit.body: Four days of argument, most of it about the going rate for breath. The court finds for the defendant on every count and orders the station's debt settled in kind, from the harbor's own tanks. Nobody on the dock is friendly about it. The magistrate has rarely been happier.

tr_square.title: SQUARE WITH THE HOUSE
tr_square.body: Guilty, rules the magistrate, and paid in full, in oxygen, in advance. The ledger shows one defendant committing the offense and the restitution in the same afternoon. The case closes at zero. {crew.botanist} takes the diagrams home. The magistrate looks a little lost.

tr_recess.title: NO FINDING
tr_recess.body: The magistrate retires to consider whether a lean is a plea, and returns after two days with a forty-page opinion that says no finding. The growbay lamps ran on full berth power for the whole recess, by order of the court, as the defendant was deemed in custody. You are billed for none of it.

tr_suspended.title: SUSPENDED
tr_suspended.body: Sentence: a month under the harbor lamps, suspended. The magistrate explains that this means it will hang over the defendant for life, then has the cutting hung over the desk on a length of wire, as a warning to others. It looks well up there. You come away a cutting short and with a clean record.

tr_bond.title: ADJOURNED
tr_bond.body: The bond is posted and the file goes on a high shelf. The trial will resume when the defendant can reach court in safety, which is to say when the noodle vendor loses interest. The vendor has asked for a copy of the ruling, to frame.

tr_sureties.title: THE CHARGE STANDS
tr_sureties.body: The court accepts your oath. Your ship's name goes on a list of parties with an open matter before this dock, a list of one. Your crop stays free and stays wanted, a fugitive from a magistrate with a long memory and very little else to do.

science_link.text: In Martin Shubik's dollar auction the winner gets the dollar, and the second-highest bidder loses their bid as well. A series of short-term rational bids ends above one dollar.
science_link.label: Dollar auction

open.title: LOT FORTY
open.body:
Lot Forty is a purse of twenty-five gold. An auction ship has parked across the lane to sell it, and has issued you paddle number one without asking. House rules scroll up the screen. Bidding opens at five and rises by fives. Highest bid takes the purse. Second-highest bid pays the house anyway and takes nothing.

Paddle Two, a dark freighter off your bow, is already waiting. {npc.quirk}
open.line: Twenty-five gold for five, friend. It is only a little money, and it is money you came here to get.

ai.aria: Twenty-five gold for five! ARIA has done the math and it's a win! ARIA always does the math!
ai.marv: Opening at five is a trap with a well-known name. An opening above twenty leaves the next bidder nothing to gain. Twenty-one would do it.
ai.rex: A rule that makes the loser pay is an ambush with a gavel. REX would keep the paddle holstered.
ai.chip: Bid Protection by CHIP refunds nothing, but it refunds it quickly!
ai.ajoy: The results from the last lot are posted, and reading them costs nothing. AJOY realizes that has not been a selling point with you.

revisit.body: The purse sits under a small spotlight. Paddle Two has not moved.
revisit.line: The lot is still open, friend.

choices.text: Read the results from Lot Thirty-Nine

results.title: LOT THIRTY-NINE
results.body:
Lot Thirty-Nine: one purse, twenty-five gold. Winning bid, seventy. Second bid, sixty-five. House take, one hundred and thirty-five. Both bidders are listed as satisfied.

Lot Thirty-Eight reads much the same, and so does the one before it. Paddle Two appears on all of them, in second place. A note in the margin says: CLIENT RETURNS TO WIN IT BACK.
results.line: Paddle Two is one of our most loyal clients. It has not won yet. It is very close.

ai.aria: Everyone was satisfied! It says so right there! What a happy auction!
ai.marv: Seventy paid for twenty-five. Sixty-five paid for nothing. The arithmetic is restful. The people in it were not.
ai.rex: A repeat casualty on the board. Hostages get better terms.
ai.chip: Loyalty like Paddle Two's deserves a Platinum tier! CHIP has written to the house!
ai.ajoy: Neither of those bidders planned to pay seventy. AJOY expects you are about to explain how you're different.

b1.title: PADDLE TWO: 10
b1.body:
Your five goes up on the board. Paddle Two answers at ten before the number has stopped blinking.

You are now the second-highest bidder, so by house rules you owe five gold for nothing. Fifteen would put you back on top, with ten still to win.
b1.line: Ten from Paddle Two. Fifteen, anywhere? Fifteen makes all this go away.

ai.aria: Still a huge profit available! ARIA can feel the momentum!
ai.marv: Stopping costs five. Fifteen risks fifteen. Every step from here will look this reasonable. That is the whole mechanism.
ai.rex: Break contact while the casualties are light.
ai.chip: Raise now and earn Bidder Miles! Bidder Miles expire on use!
ai.ajoy: Five gold to walk away. AJOY would take it, and she can see you reaching for the paddle from here.

b2.title: PADDLE TWO: 20
b2.body:
Twenty, from Paddle Two, at once. Stop now and you have paid fifteen for nothing. Bid twenty-five and you have paid the full value of the purse to win the purse, which feels, at this moment, like getting out for free.

A private message arrives from the dark freighter: I WOULD STOP IF YOU WOULD.
b2.line: Twenty-five, friend? Twenty-five and you lose nothing at all.

ai.aria: Break even! That's a kind of winning that doesn't even need winning!
ai.marv: Paddle Two now faces the same sum you do. It will reach the same answer. That is what the message is telling you.
ai.rex: REX reads that message as a plea, not a ruse. It changes nothing about the terrain.
ai.chip: CHIP Escrow can hold your regret in a secure account!
ai.ajoy: If you bid twenty-five, the other ship has every reason to bid thirty. AJOY has read the lot results. So have you, she assumes.

b3.title: PADDLE TWO: 30
b3.body:
Thirty. Paddle Two has bid more than the purse holds and did it without hesitating, because stopping would cost it twenty and going on might cost it five. You have worked out that the same is true of you. The board offers thirty-five.

The message from the freighter now reads: SORRY.
b3.line: We have left the value of the lot behind, friend. This is the part the house enjoys.

ai.aria: Bidding this high means you really believe in the purse! ARIA believes in it too!
ai.marv: Stop and lose twenty-five. Win at thirty-five and lose ten. Neither number has anything to do with the purse now.
ai.rex: Both sides are reinforcing a position neither one wants. REX has a medal from one of those.
ai.chip: At this bid level you qualify for a CHIP Hardship Consultation, billed hourly!
ai.ajoy: Everything bid so far is spent, win or lose. AJOY would stop counting it. She didn't want to say so while you were enjoying yourself.

b4.title: PADDLE TWO: 40
b4.body:
Forty. The auction ship has dimmed its lights, as a courtesy. You can lose thirty-five gold and go, or bid forty-five and lose twenty, and you no longer recall whether you wanted the purse.

Paddle Two has sent one more message: THAT WAS THE LAST OF IT. IF YOU RAISE I AM DONE. ELEVEN YEARS. I WAS SO CLOSE.
b4.line: Forty-five would close the lot, friend. It is entirely up to you. It always was.

ai.aria: One more bid and you WIN! ARIA is so excited for the other ship too!
ai.marv: Forty-five loses twenty. Stopping loses thirty-five and hands a stranger the first win of a ruined career. The cheaper one is not the same as the better one, and that is outside MARV's department.
ai.rex: The enemy is out of ammunition and has said so. REX has been in this position. He does not always sleep.
ai.chip: CHIP reminds you that compassion is not tax deductible! CHIP has checked twice!
ai.ajoy: Fifteen gold is the difference. AJOY would not presume to say what fifteen gold is for. You can see their lights from here.

au_jump.title: SOLD AT THE FIRST BID
au_jump.body: Twenty-one gold. The board stays lit. Paddle Two does not answer, because twenty-six would buy twenty-five, and for one long moment the auctioneer says nothing at all. Then the purse comes across by drone, with a receipt. You are four gold up and will not be invited back.
au_jump.line: The house thanks you for your custom, friend. The house keeps very good records.

au_fold5.title: SECOND PLACE
au_fold5.body: You set the paddle down. Five gold goes to the house for the privilege of coming second. Paddle Two takes the purse for ten, the first thing it has ever won, and the freighter's lights come up one deck at a time. It is bidding on Lot Forty-One before you are out of range.

au_fold15.title: EXPENSIVE SECOND
au_fold15.body: Fifteen gold to the house, for nothing, with a receipt. Paddle Two takes the purse for twenty and sends two words across: THANK YOU. The auction is not mentioned again, and it goes on not being mentioned for most of a day.

au_fold25.title: AT COST
au_fold25.body: You have now paid the full value of the purse and do not have the purse. The auctioneer congratulates you on your discipline and reserves you a seat for Lot Forty-One. Paddle Two pays thirty for twenty-five and appears to feel this is going well.

au_fold35.title: FIRST WIN
au_fold35.body: You put the paddle down. Thirty-five gold goes to the house. Paddle Two pays forty for a purse of twenty-five and, after eleven years of lots, has won. The freighter runs up every light it owns. It is one of the worst deals ever struck in this lane, and there were two of you in it.

au_won.title: SOLD
au_won.body: Forty-five gold. The freighter's lights go out one deck at a time. The purse arrives by drone with a receipt. You have paid forty-five for twenty-five, Paddle Two has paid forty for nothing, and the house has taken in eighty-five gold for a bag of twenty-five. The auctioneer asks if you would care to see Lot Forty-One.

au_truce.title: A COVERED DISH
au_truce.body: {crew.chef} sends a covered dish across on a line, {cost.food} units' worth, with a note. Paddle Two has not eaten anything cooked in some time. You both stop. It takes the purse at ten, sends back your stake and as much again, and asks for the recipe.
au_truce.line: The house has no rule against dinner, friend. The house will be writing one.

science_link.text: Some parasites change what the animal carrying them does, making it careless and easier to catch. The animal is called the host.
science_link.label: Behavior-altering parasite

stage.title: YOUR HOST
stage.body:
Applause comes first, on every channel, perfectly even, and stops as if cut with scissors. The main screen now shows a lit stage and a sequined jacket at a lectern. Whoever is inside the jacket reads as {npc.species}, though the jacket seems to be doing most of the standing.

The delight on that face does not vary. The voice arrives half a second before the face does.
stage.line: Welcome back. You have not been here before. Three questions stand between you and the prize, and everyone goes home with something.

ai.aria: A game show! ARIA has been ready for this her whole life!
ai.marv: The signal has no source. The applause repeats every nine seconds. The prizes appear to be real, which is the worst thing about it.
ai.rex: One presenter and a studio audience that claps in formation. Better drilled than any unit REX ever led.
ai.chip: Prize winnings may be subject to CHIP's Contestant Fee! CHIP admires this program's ad load!
ai.ajoy: You could change the channel. AJOY has also read 'everyone goes home with something' twice, and it does not say with what.

q1.title: QUESTION ONE
q1.body: Lights drop. A small clock on the lectern starts counting in no units you recognize. The audience draws one breath, all at the same moment, and goes on holding it.
q1.line: Question one. Venus turns once on its axis, and Venus goes once around the Sun. Which of those takes longer?

ai.aria: It's the Sun one! ARIA has a wonderful feeling about the Sun one!
ai.marv: Assistance is forbidden. Venus has a very slow rotation. MARV has not assisted. He has described a planet.
ai.rex: REX cannot assess Venus from here. He has never trusted a planet that spins the wrong way.
ai.chip: Ask-A-CHIP Lifeline is available for one easy payment of everything!
ai.ajoy: It's not the tidy one. Planets aren't. AJOY has now narrowed it down for you and expects no thanks.

q2.title: QUESTION TWO
q2.body:
Applause, exact to the tenth of a second. Your winnings, eight gold, light up on the jacket's lapel. A card rises out of the lectern with a small wet sound.

The delight has not moved. It has, however, shifted slightly to the left.
q2.line: Correct. Question two. Which protein is thought to be the most abundant on Earth? You may take your eight gold and go. We would be so sad.

ai.aria: Keratin! ARIA's hair is full of it! ARIA doesn't have hair, but she has confidence!
ai.marv: Collagen leads among mammals, and mammals are a rounding error. Consider what covers the planet. MARV is not assisting. He is looking at the growbay.
ai.rex: REX recognizes one of those words from an enemy order of battle. He will not say which.
ai.chip: CHIP Protein Shakes contain at least one of these!
ai.ajoy: The answer is green, and you gave it a whole bay. AJOY isn't allowed to say so, so she hasn't.

q3.title: QUESTION THREE
q3.body:
A second voice is briefly audible behind the first, then not. The lapel reads sixteen. Something under the sequins moves from one shoulder to the other, unhurried, like a passenger changing seats.

The face does not appear to notice. The audience has stopped pretending to breathe.
q3.line: Correct. Last question, and a favorite of ours. A rat stops minding the smell of cats. Which of these is responsible? Take your sixteen gold if you would rather not know.

ai.aria: It's love! Is love an option? ARIA is choosing love!
ai.marv: The fluke does its work on ants. Rabies does its work on everything, indiscriminately. This question is not really about rats.
ai.rex: REX saw that thing move. He requests permission to fire on a television program.
ai.chip: Correct answers qualify for a free Mandatory Upgrade! Free is a CHIP word for later!
ai.ajoy: It isn't the fluke, that one's ants. AJOY would also draw your attention to 'a favorite of ours'. Ours.

prize.title: YOUR PRIZE
prize.body:
Applause, and this time it does not cut off. Two pedestals rise. One holds a purse of thirty gold. The other holds the sequined jacket, empty and still warm, its sleeves arranged to welcome you.

Nobody is at the lectern now. The face on your screen is lying at the foot of it, delighted. The voice has not changed, and it is coming from the jacket.
prize.line: Congratulations. You have been a wonderful audience. Every season needs someone new to carry it. The purse is lovely too.

ai.aria: ARIA loves the jacket! It's so sparkly, and it's looking right at you!
ai.marv: The jacket is warmer than the room, and warmer on one side. The purse is thirty gold at room temperature. MARV has formed a preference, which is rare.
ai.rex: REX will personally airlock anyone who puts that on. He considers it a kindness.
ai.chip: Brand Ambassador packages include a complimentary garment! CHIP has been in talks with the garment!
ai.ajoy: Take the purse. AJOY has never said anything more plainly, and you are still looking at the jacket.

choices.sub: The lining alone is worth it

bank1.title: A SENSIBLE CONTESTANT
bank1.body: You take the eight gold. The applause stops in the middle of a clap. The money is in your airlock, though nothing docked, and the audience turns to look at you, every seat at the same moment, as the channel closes.

bank2.title: QUIT WHILE AHEAD
bank2.body: Sixteen gold. The audience sighs once, together. The answer, you are told as the picture folds, was Toxoplasma gondii, which makes a rat careless around cats, so that the rat gets eaten and the parasite gets where it was going.
bank2.line: It really is a lovely way to travel. Thank you for watching.

c1.title: THE HOME GAME
c1.body: Wrong. Venus takes 243 Earth days to turn once and about 225 to go around the Sun, so a turn outlasts a year. The audience groans in one breath. Everyone goes home with something, and you go home with the Home Game: a crate in your airlock, left by nobody, holding ration tins and a board with the pieces already in play. They are in a different position every morning.

c2.title: A LIFETIME SUPPLY
c2.body: Wrong. RuBisCO, the enzyme that lets carbon into the living world, is thought to be the most abundant protein on Earth. Collagen only wins among mammals. Your consolation prize is in the airlock: one sealed jar labeled LIFETIME SUPPLY. It is about half full. The label does not say what of.

c3.title: SO CLOSE
c3.body: Wrong, and so close. It was Toxoplasma gondii, which makes a rat careless around cats, so that the rat gets eaten and the parasite gets where it was going. The consolation prize is eight gold, in the airlock. You find one sequin on your collar that evening. You throw it out. You find it again the next evening.
c3.line: Thank you for playing. You will be hearing from us, in a manner of speaking.

win_purse.title: THE PURSE
win_purse.body: Thirty gold, counted, in the airlock. The stage folds up and the stars come back. For two days the ship's speakers clap once, softly, at odd hours, and then they seem to lose interest in you. Somewhere out here it is starting its next season.

win_jacket.title: THE JACKET
win_jacket.body: It is in the airlock when the stage folds up. The lining is exotic fiber of a kind the fabricator has never seen, and you cut out as much as you dare. The rest goes on a hook in the hold, where you left it, facing the wall. In the morning it is on a different hook. It has not, so far, been facing you.

title: Plenty of Air
leave_label: CAN'T LEAVE (THE LINE IS PAID OUT)

science_link.text: Time of useful consciousness runs from the loss of oxygen to the moment a person can no longer take corrective action. Pilots use low-pressure chambers to learn their own symptoms.
science_link.label: Time of useful consciousness

lock.title: THE LOCK
lock.body:
Forty years dead, by the dust, and its manifest beacon still lists stores aboard. The hull holds pressure, but the air inside has thinned past breathing. You go in with a hood and a harness on a hundred meters of line from the ship's own reserve, so every room costs the whole ship, and the line thins the farther it runs.

Thin air has one known side effect. You were told about it in training. Try to remember it.

LINE PRESSURE: 100.

ai.aria: Exploring! ARIA will be right here cheering! You've got all the air in the world!
ai.marv: Each room costs more reserve than the one before it, and you will be the last to know. The real figures will come from this channel. They will not feel true.
ai.rex: REX has seen good men salute a fire extinguisher at altitude. Keep one ear on the computer.
ai.chip: CHIP Breathe+ gives you twelve percent more air for a recurring fee!
ai.ajoy: You could reel in now for the price of what's already gone. AJOY says so mainly to have said so. When you start feeling cheerful in there, that's your cue.

choices.sub: Air and a burn, for nothing

stores.title: STORES
stores.body:
Racks on both sides, mostly stripped, and one pallet of sealed ration drums that someone meant to come back for. A hatch in the far wall leads on toward the spine of the ship. You feel alert. The air in your hood tastes faintly of coins.

LINE PRESSURE: 76.

ai.aria: Treasure! ARIA told you so! ARIA tells everyone so!
ai.marv: Seventy-six. Reserve drawn so far is modest. It will not stay modest.
ai.rex: Take the objective and withdraw. Holding ground gets expensive past this point.
ai.chip: Ration drums are a trademark of somebody! CHIP will find out who and bill you!
ai.ajoy: Those drums would do nicely. AJOY notes you have already stopped reading the gauge.

choices.text: Take the drums and go back

quarters.title: QUARTERS
quarters.body:
Bunks, strapped down and made. A locker of personal effects, each one tagged. A medical kit on the wall with its seal unbroken. Past the last bunk a hatch stands open on the spine of the ship. You feel fine. You feel, in fact, rather well. Whoever made these beds knew what they were doing.

LINE PRESSURE: 74.

ai.aria: Such tidy beds! ARIA gives this ship five stars!
ai.marv: Seventy-four. You have just complimented bedding. Note the time.
ai.rex: Take the kit. A bunk that neat means an inspection nobody came back from.
ai.chip: CHIP Medkit Finder is free for thirty days, then it isn't!
ai.ajoy: A sealed medkit is the one sensible thing in that room. AJOY would take it and turn around, though you have that voice on already.

choices.text: Take the medkit and go back

spine.title: A WONDERFUL CORRIDOR
spine.body:
This is a long straight corridor with nothing in it and it may be the best corridor you have ever seen. Doors left and right: ENGINEERING and BRIDGE. You have lots of line. The gauge says fifty-one, and fifty-one has always been a good solid number. Whoever built this corridor deserves a hand.

LINE PRESSURE: 51. PLENTY.

ai.aria: You sound great! You sound just like ARIA!
ai.marv: Fifty-one. Your speech has slowed by a fifth and you have praised a corridor. Turn around.
ai.rex: REX has had the captain on the line for one minute and heard the word 'lovely' twice. He is calling it. Come home.
ai.chip: Your reserve is eligible for an Overdraft! Overdrafts are fun and legally binding!
ai.ajoy: You've started narrating the furniture. AJOY would go back now and collect what you passed on the way. She knows you feel marvelous.

choices.text: Go back, if you really want to
choices.sub: You have so much line, though

eng.title: WHAT A ROOM
eng.body:
What a room. A fuel cell sits in its cradle with a charge still in it, and you are so pleased for it. Past the reactor housing a small door is marked LIFE SUPPORT, and you have an excellent feeling about small doors. Your fingers have gone a lovely color. A voice on the radio keeps using your name, which is nice of it.

LINE PRESSURE: 30. LOTS.

ai.aria: A lovely color! ARIA is so glad you're getting out more!
ai.marv: Thirty. Blue fingers are cyanosis. That was not a compliment you just paid them.
ai.rex: This is the computer. Pick up the cell. Turn around. That is an order, and REX has never been so polite.
ai.chip: Your air plan is nearing its limit! Reply YES to upgrade, or reply anything else to upgrade!
ai.ajoy: Cell, then line, then home. AJOY is using short words now. She doesn't enjoy that as much as you'd think.

choices.text: Take the fuel cell and go home

bridge.title: SUCH NICE PEOPLE
bridge.body:
Such nice people. Four suits in four chairs, facing forward, very relaxed. Nobody here seems to have been in any hurry. A chart lies under one glove. The log on the console stops at an entry you find charming: ALL WELL. AIR EXCELLENT. SPIRITS HIGH. There is a small door at the back marked LIFE SUPPORT, and one empty chair, which is thoughtful.

LINE PRESSURE: 30. LOTS.

ai.aria: New friends! ARIA bets they'd love some company!
ai.marv: Thirty. Four crew, no sign of a struggle, last entry cheerful. That is what this looks like from the inside, and you are finding it charming.
ai.rex: Do not sit down. REX will repeat that. Do not sit down.
ai.chip: Premium Seating is now available on this deck! Terms are final!
ai.ajoy: They all thought it was going very well. AJOY will just leave that there, and your chart, and the way out.

choices.text: Take the chart and go home

choices.sub: Just a moment. It's so nice.

last.title: THE BEST ROOM
last.body:
You have found the best room. There is a chair in it, and it is the finest chair ever made: gray, bolted down, perfectly round in the seat. Beside it sits a dull metal box with a stenciled number and a warranty sticker marked VOID. Who wants a box. You could carry the chair. You are very strong now. You have so much air you can see it.

LINE PRESSURE: 11. SO MUCH.

ai.aria: ARIA loves that you're having such a good time! Stay as long as you like!
ai.marv: Eleven. The box is an oxygen recycler. The chair is a chair. This is the third time of saying so. The second time you said he had a wonderful voice.
ai.rex: TAKE THE BOX. REX will keep transmitting that until you do. TAKE THE BOX.
ai.chip: Box contents quoted on request! CHIP's rate is one chair!
ai.ajoy: The box. AJOY doesn't care how beautiful the chair is. The box, then the line, then home, and she will say she told you so for a week.

cr_abort.title: CAST OFF
cr_abort.body: You reel in, seal the lock and burn clear of the wreck with the reserve a little down and nothing to show for it. Cycling that lock was not free, and neither was stopping. Whatever is on its manifest stays there.

cr_stores.title: THE DRUMS
cr_stores.body: You drag the drums back along the line in two trips, and the winch does the last of it. Back in the lock your ears ring. The food is good. You are slightly disappointed, and you can't think why.

cr_quarters.title: THE MEDKIT
cr_quarters.body: You lift the kit off the wall and follow the line home, pleased with your own restraint. The bunks stay made. An hour later, with proper air in you, you find you have also brought one tagged pair of socks, and you cannot account for them.

cr_spine.title: TURNED BACK
cr_spine.body: You turn around, which feels like a shame, and fill your arms with what you passed on the way. An hour later in your own air you look at what you carried out and at what you left, and you sit on the deck for a minute without saying anything.

cr_eng.title: THE FUEL CELL
cr_eng.body: You lift the cell out of its cradle, say something kind to it and follow the line back. It feels like a short walk. The log says it took most of a day, with three stops. In your own air your head starts to pound, and it goes on pounding well after the color has come back to your fingers.

cr_bridge.title: THE CHART
cr_bridge.body: You slide the chart out from under the glove and thank its owner, out loud, twice. You are most of the way home before you start to understand what you were looking at. ALL WELL, said the log. You do not read your own entry for that day until you have slept.

cr_sit.title: JUST A MOMENT
cr_sit.body: It is an excellent chair. The line has a dead-man alarm, which trips after ninety seconds without movement, and a winch, which has no opinions. You come to in your own lock two days later with a bruise across your chest and the reserve badly down. Your hand is out to one side, as if someone had been holding it.

cr_egg.title: HOW LONG TO BOIL AN EGG
cr_egg.body: {crew.chef} comes on the line and asks how long to boil an egg. You say purple. There is a short silence, and then the winch starts, and {crew.chef} keeps you talking about eggs all the way back up the line. You come home with empty arms. There is an egg waiting, or what the galley calls one, and {crew.chef} watches you eat it.

cr_chair.title: THE FINEST CHAIR
cr_chair.body: You are told afterward that the alarm tripped, that the winch took you, and that you fought it. You wake in the lock with one gray armrest clutched to your chest, and the bolts have taken the skin off two knuckles. When your head clears you look at it for a long time. It is an armrest.

cr_box.title: THE BORING BOX
cr_box.body: You pick up the box, and hate it, and let the winch take you. You remember none of the trip. You wake in the lock with the reserve badly down and an oxygen recycler in your arms. Its warranty is void and it makes a noise like a sigh. It is the single best thing you have found on this voyage, and you still think about the chair.

science_link.text: Botanically a tomato is a fruit. In 1893 the US Supreme Court held that it is a vegetable for tariffs and customs, using the ordinary meaning of the words.
science_link.label: Nix v. Hedden

q1.title: QUESTION 1 OF 3
q1.body:
Helm controls have gone gray, and the main screen has become a form. According to the header you have crossed into a customs union. Nobody answers on any channel, because nobody is needed: the form is the officer. It autosaves. It thanks you for your patience, which it has measured.

QUESTION 1. DO YOU HAVE ANYTHING TO DECLARE?

ai.aria: A form! ARIA loves being asked questions! Just be yourself!
ai.marv: Anything entered here will be read against anything else entered here. The logic is consistent, which puts it ahead of most governments. Think two boxes ahead.
ai.rex: REX tried the helm override. The override wants to know if REX has anything to declare.
ai.chip: CHIP FormFill completes every field with whatever benefits CHIP!
ai.ajoy: There's a crop in the growbay and a water log to prove it. AJOY mentions this because she saw where your cursor was going.

n2.title: QUESTION 2 OF 3
n2.body:
ANSWER RECEIVED: NOTHING. THANK YOU.

QUESTION 2. DID YOU PACK THIS NOTHING YOURSELF?

A note under the box explains that unattended nothing has been used to conceal things in the past.

ai.aria: ARIA packed lots of nothing! ARIA is a great packer!
ai.marv: Yes admits knowledge. No admits a stranger in your hold. Both are binding. The form has done this before.
