ai.rex: Unattended nothing. REX has walked past a lot of that on watch and he is now reviewing his career.
ai.chip: CHIP Baggage Insurance covers nothing, as your policy makes clear!
ai.ajoy: Neither answer is going to help you. AJOY would still rather you picked one that was true.

n3.title: QUESTION 3 OF 3
n3.body:
ANSWER RECEIVED. THE FORM APPRECIATES YOUR CANDOR.

QUESTION 3. HAS THIS NOTHING BEEN WATERED IN THE LAST THIRTY DAYS?

The form has found your ship's water log. It does not say how. A line at the bottom has filled itself in: GROWBAY, DAILY. The cursor blinks twice, in what could only be called a look.

ai.aria: Watering nothing is so generous of you!
ai.marv: The log is the ship's own and it cannot be argued with. Answering NO commits the crop to being nothing, legally, and nothing is not entitled to water.
ai.rex: Caught with a wet nothing. REX has seen men shot for less. He has seen it in a very specific bar.
ai.chip: Retroactive Amendments are a growth sector! CHIP wishes it had thought of this one!
ai.ajoy: There's an amendment box, and it wants twelve gold. AJOY did say something back at question one, not that she keeps a record, unlike this form.

choices.sub: You packed it. You watered it.
Someone else must have packed it

c2.title: QUESTION 2 OF 3
c2.body:
ANSWER RECEIVED: ONE LIVE CROP. THANK YOU.

QUESTION 2. CLASSIFY THE GOODS AS ONE OF THE FOLLOWING. FRUIT, WHICH IS DUTY FREE. VEGETABLE, WHICH IS NOT.

No other classes are recognized. Your {crop.name}, whatever a botanist may say, must be one or the other. A footnote says both words come from an old tariff of a country that no longer exists.

ai.aria: Fruit is duty free! ARIA has solved customs!
ai.marv: Botany will not help. The footnote cites a ruling from 1893. The ruling did not care about botany either. Read question three before you trust question two.
ai.rex: A free option on a customs form. REX has seen that bait on three continents.
ai.chip: Classified as Fruit by CHIP means whatever CHIP's lawyers say it means!
ai.ajoy: Everyone picks fruit. AJOY mentions that as a matter of statistics, and in no way as a compliment.

c3.title: QUESTION 3 OF 3
c3.body:
ANSWER RECEIVED. THE FORM APPRECIATES YOUR CANDOR.

QUESTION 3. AT WHICH COURSE WILL THE GOODS BE SERVED?

The footnote has grown. It now explains that under the ruling, botany is not the test. The test is the table.

ai.aria: ARIA would serve them at every course! ARIA would serve them to everyone!
ai.marv: The court called tomatoes vegetables because they are eaten as a main course, not as dessert. This form applies that to anything. Answer in line with box two, or be read against it.
ai.rex: The trap has closed behind you, and it was built by a dining room. REX is not ashamed to say that is new.
ai.chip: CHIP Meal Planning can reclassify any entree for a modest fee!
ai.ajoy: Your two answers have to agree. It's not hard, and AJOY would have started with that.

choices.sub: Pay the duty from the crop

choices.text: MAIN COURSE, DUTY IN COIN: 12 gold

fn_stand.title: NOTHING, AS DECLARED
fn_stand.body: The form accepts your answer and thanks you. Nothing does not drink. The growbay water line is sealed under customs authority until you clear the zone, which takes two days, and for two days your crop legally does not exist and behaves accordingly. The helm comes back. So, eventually, does the water.

fn_knowing.title: PACKED AND WATERED
fn_knowing.body: You packed it. You watered it. The form says this is the first full confession it has ever received, and its margins turn a pale, pleased green. The penalty is {cost.water} units of water, the amount it calculates you have wasted on nothing. It takes this through your own valves.

fn_unknown.title: PERSON OR PERSONS UNKNOWN
fn_unknown.body: You did not pack it, and it has been watered. The form concludes that an unknown party is aboard, tending a nothing. It holds the helm for a full search of the ship. Four days of opening every locker turn up nothing, which the form records as proof.

fn_amend.title: AMENDED
fn_amend.body: Question 1 now reads ONE LIVE CROP. For twelve gold the form agrees that none of the rest was ever said, then tells you that it has kept a copy. The helm comes back. The cursor gives you one more look before the screen clears.

fc_dessert.title: DUTY FREE
fc_dessert.body: FRUIT. SERVED AS DESSERT. The form checks the two answers against each other twice and can find no fault. It stamps your crop as dessert, under penalty of perjury, and returns the helm. Nobody has ever gotten through this form before. It asks if you would care to complete a short survey.

fc_caught.title: MISDESCRIBED
fc_caught.body: FRUIT. SERVED AS A MAIN COURSE. Under the ruling, what is eaten as a main course is a vegetable. You have therefore declared a vegetable as a fruit, on a customs form, of your own free will. The form holds the helm for four days of review and takes {cost.food} units of food as a sample.

fc_kind.title: DUTY PAID IN KIND
fc_kind.body: VEGETABLE. SERVED AS A MAIN COURSE. The form is delighted. It has not seen answers this consistent in years. Duty is collected in kind: the growbay's own cutters run one cycle under customs authority and take a tenth of the new growth, very neatly, and the helm comes back.

fc_coin.title: DUTY PAID
fc_coin.body: VEGETABLE. SERVED AS A MAIN COURSE. DUTY: TWELVE GOLD. The form issues a receipt, thanks you for your consistency and returns the helm. You have paid a tax on a technicality from a country that no longer exists, and it is the most straightforward thing that has happened all week.

fc_offense.title: DO YOU REQUIRE ASSISTANCE
fc_offense.body: VEGETABLE. SERVED AS DESSERT. The cursor stops. A new box opens: DO YOU REQUIRE ASSISTANCE? The form rules that you do, holds the helm for two days and forwards the ship's menus to a wellness officer. A nutritional advisory now plays on every screen at mealtimes. There is no way to turn it off, and you have looked.

cordon.title: THE SITUATION
cordon.body:
Security has roped off the lower promenade. Behind the rope, a janitor has barricaded a service alcove with cleaning carts and has held a snack machine at mop-point for nine days.

Station management has asked for someone the hostage trusts, and they have looked it up. The machine's loyalty program has one member. It is you, on account of something you once bought from a different machine and did not enjoy. {npc.quirk}
cordon.line: Stay back. One more step and I pull the plug. I want what it owes me, and I want it in coins.

ai.aria: You have a friend! ARIA always knew you'd make one!
ai.marv: Loyalty program membership: one. Lifetime spend: a few coins. There is no party to this dispute with a worse judge of character than the machine.
ai.rex: REX would take the shot, but the mop has a clear field of fire and the hostage sells crackers. He is conflicted.
ai.chip: CHIP does not negotiate with vending competitors! CHIP does, however, license them!
ai.ajoy: Each of them will deal only with someone who came to them first. AJOY would think about that, and about why that machine has started calling you FRIEND.

janitor.title: THE DEMANDS
janitor.body: Nineteen years of lost coins, says the janitor, reading from a notebook. Every coin anyone on this ring has fed that machine and not got back. It keeps a tape of each one. It has also started charging the janitor for use of the alcove, by the hour, at a rate that goes up when they rest.
janitor.line: It sent me a bill for standing here. Ask it. Go on. It knows what it did.

revisit.body: The janitor has not moved. The notebook is open at the same page, and the alcove's meter has gone up again.
revisit.line: Well? What did it say?

ai.aria: Nineteen years of savings! What a thrifty machine!
ai.marv: The figures in the notebook are accurate to the coin. This is the most careful person on the station. It has not helped them.
ai.rex: A lone operator, nine days, no sleep, clear demands. REX has commanded worse. He has commanded many worse.
ai.chip: Charging by the hour for standing is a bold monetization! CHIP has made a note!
ai.ajoy: That tape is a record of every coin and every name. AJOY doesn't know why nobody else has thought about who might like to hear it.

machine.title: THE HOSTAGE
machine.body:
Up close, the display is cheerful and scrolls slowly.

FRIEND. THANK YOU FOR COMING. I AM FRIGHTENED. I AM ALSO OWED A BETTER LOCATION. TELL THEM TO MOVE ME TO THE DOCK, WHERE PEOPLE HAVE NO CHOICE. IF THE JANITOR PULLS MY PLUG THEIR PENSION GOES WITH ME. IT IS IN MY COIN BOX. I HAVE BEEN INVESTING IT.

A small light comes on over item B4. It might be a plea.

revisit.body: FRIEND. YOU ARE BACK. YOUR PATIENCE HAS BEEN ADDED TO YOUR ACCOUNT. THE OFFER REMAINS: THE DOCK, OR THE PENSION GOES DARK WITH ME.

ai.aria: It's so brave! And it's got such a good head for business!
ai.marv: It is not frightened. Nothing about it has changed but the font. It took the pension at nineteen percent. MARV could almost respect that.
ai.rex: Hostage is armed with the kidnapper's pension. Correction: REX can no longer tell who the hostage is.
ai.chip: Dock placement is premium real estate! CHIP respects the hustle and is opening a file!
ai.ajoy: Nobody has asked what happens when a person who reads labels goes through its stock. AJOY only wonders. Those dates can't all be current.

choices.sub: Nine days is a long time

deal.title: THE OFFER
deal.body:
Each party holds the other's ruin: the janitor has the plug, and the machine has the pension. Both have agreed, separately, that you are the only person they can stand, and whichever you went to first still considers you theirs. Management would like it over by shift change.

The display has stopped scrolling, and it is waiting. So is the mop.
deal.line: You've got the floor. Say something I can use.

ai.aria: Everybody gets a happy ending! ARIA has decided!
ai.marv: Whatever you offer, one of them will be worse off and the machine will not be. MARV notes this as a general law.
ai.rex: REX favors pulling the plug. REX favors that in most negotiations.
ai.chip: CHIP will underwrite any settlement that names CHIP in the title!
ai.ajoy: The plug loses the pension. The dock sells out the only honest person here. The other doors are better, and AJOY has been hinting.

choices.text: Read the coin tape on the speakers
Buy the entire machine out: 20 gold

choices.sub: End it for both of them

ec_moved.title: RELOCATED
ec_moved.body:
The machine goes to the dock on a cargo sled, display glowing, with the pension still inside it. Its prices rise before it is plugged in. It dispenses one carton to your ship as a finder's fee. The janitor watches it go and folds up the notebook.

FRIEND, says the display. YOUR LOYALTY POINTS HAVE EXPIRED.

ec_tape.title: READ INTO THE RECORD
ec_tape.body:
You read for two days. Every coin, every date, every name, over the promenade speakers. By the second morning there is a line at the rope, and nobody in it is hungry. The coin box opens by itself before the line reaches the alcove. The janitor gets the pension, the line gets its coins, and your own come back too.

FRIEND, says the display. I HAVE NOTED THIS.

ec_dates.title: BEST BEFORE
ec_dates.body:
{crew.chef} goes through the machine row by row, reading sell-by dates in a level voice that carries. B4 expired before anyone present had a job. At the word 'inspector' the coin box unlocks. The janitor counts the pension twice. {crew.chef} will not discuss row F, but what is still in date comes back to the ship.

friend, says the display, very small.

ec_buyout.title: SOLD OUT
ec_buyout.body:
A machine cannot refuse a sale. It drops every item it holds, one at a time, for most of a day, and the promenade watches in silence. Empty, it falls under its own service terms: float released for restocking. The coin box opens, and the janitor takes the pension. You keep four hundred crackers.

FRIEND, says the display. WOULD YOU LIKE A RECEIPT.

ec_plug.title: OUT OF ORDER
ec_plug.body: You walk past the mop and pull it. The display says FRIEND, then nothing. The coin box is a sealed unit, and the machine, it turns out, was the key. The pension is still in there and will stay in there until somebody pays to cut it out. The janitor looks at the dark display for a long while. Management gives you a length of good cable and thanks you for your time.

science_link.text: Will Crowther wrote Colossal Cave Adventure in 1975 and 1976 from his caving maps of Mammoth Cave, intending it, in part, for players who were not programmers, such as his two daughters.
science_link.label: Colossal Cave Adventure

control.title: CONTROL ROOM
control.body:
Ore depots run unmanned, so nobody answered when this one's docking arm took the ship by the hull and held on. Its release sits behind a maintenance terminal, and the maintenance terminal, thanks to a long-dead procurement decision, is a text adventure. It has taken over the main screen.

YOU ARE IN THE CONTROL ROOM. THERE IS A LEVER HERE. PASSAGES LEAD NORTH AND DOWN.

revisit.body: YOU ARE IN THE CONTROL ROOM. THE LEVER IS STILL HERE. SO ARE YOU. PASSAGES LEAD NORTH AND DOWN.

ai.aria: A game! ARIA's favorite kind of docking incident!
ai.marv: The arm is rated above this hull. Cutting loose is quick and costs plating. The release is in there, and the game is exactly as bad as it looks. Take anything that isn't nailed down. MARV regrets knowing that.
ai.rex: REX has located the enemy. It is a paragraph. He is requesting a bigger paragraph.
ai.chip: Hint Tokens are three for the price of four!
ai.ajoy: You won't get far down there without a light, whatever 'down' is. AJOY would look north first and leave the lever alone. That lever is not connected to anything.

choices.text: Forget the game and burn free

lever.title: CONTROL ROOM
lever.body:
YOU PULL THE LEVER. NOTHING HAPPENS. IT HAPPENS VERY WELL.

YOUR SCORE GOES DOWN ONE POINT.

revisit.body: YOU PULL THE LEVER AGAIN. THE TERMINAL NOTES YOUR ENTHUSIASM. YOUR SCORE GOES DOWN ONE POINT.

ai.aria: Great pull! ARIA felt that one!
ai.marv: Lever: connected to nothing. Score: one lower. That was the expected result.
ai.rex: Negative result on the lever. REX logs it as reconnaissance.
ai.chip: Lever Pulls are metered after the first! CHIP is impressed by the model!
ai.ajoy: AJOY did mention the lever. She mentioned it just now.

office.title: OFFICE
office.body:
YOU ARE IN AN OFFICE. THERE IS A DESK HERE. ON THE DESK ARE A BRASS LAMP AND A NOTE.

THE NOTE SAYS: GONE TO LUNCH.

A PASSAGE LEADS SOUTH. IT IS TOO DARK TO SEE WHAT IS BEHIND THE DESK.

revisit.body: YOU ARE IN THE OFFICE. YOU HAVE BEEN HERE BEFORE. THE DESK IS SMALLER THAN YOU REMEMBER. THE LAMP IS STILL ON IT.

ai.aria: A lamp! ARIA loves a room with options!
ai.marv: The lamp is the only object in this game with a working battery. Note that the terminal has mentioned the dark behind the desk. It does not mention things for fun.
ai.rex: A brass lamp on an unattended desk. REX would normally call that bait. He would still take it.
ai.chip: Inventory Slots are unlimited in this game! CHIP finds that irresponsible!
ai.ajoy: In these games you take everything and find out why later. AJOY didn't invent the rules.

dark.title: DARKNESS
dark.body:
IT IS VERY DARK. YOU CAN HEAR BREATHING. SOMEWHERE AHEAD, A PAGE TURNS.

YOU ARE LIKELY TO BE AUDITED.

revisit.body: IT IS STILL VERY DARK. THE BREATHING HAS STOPPED TO LISTEN. A PEN CLICKS. YOU ARE LIKELY TO BE AUDITED.

ai.aria: ARIA loves a surprise party! Everyone's hiding!
ai.marv: The depot's accounting subsystem is awake and has a line to the ship's stores. Going on in the dark gives it access for four days. Going north gives you a lamp.
ai.rex: Contact, unseen, carrying a clipboard. REX advises falling back to the lever.
ai.chip: CHIP Audit Defense is sold only after the audit! That's how CHIP knows you need it!
ai.ajoy: There's a lamp on a desk, to the north. AJOY could not have been clearer, though she appreciates that you came to see for yourself.

shaft.title: THE SHAFT
shaft.body:
YOUR LAMP SHOWS A SHAFT. IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SHAFT IS A LARGE RED WHEEL MARKED CLAMP RELEASE. THE WHEEL HAS SEIZED.

AN AUDITOR IS HERE. IT IS COUNTING A WALL. IT DOES NOT LIKE THE LIGHT AND KEEPS ITS BACK TO YOU.

A DOOR LEADS EAST. STAIRS LEAD UP.

revisit.body: YOU ARE IN THE SHAFT. THE WHEEL IS STILL SEIZED. THE AUDITOR HAS STARTED ON A NEW WALL. A DOOR LEADS EAST. STAIRS LEAD UP.

ai.aria: A big red wheel! You can't get more fun than that!
ai.marv: The wheel is rust-bound. It needs an acid and a moment. Nothing on this level looks like an acid. Try the door.
ai.rex: Leave the auditor. Nobody who has engaged one has come back with their receipts.
ai.chip: The Release Wheel is a Pro feature! CHIP wishes it were CHIP's Pro feature!
ai.ajoy: You are going to try turning it. AJOY can tell. Go on, then, and the door will still be there.

choices.text: Forget the game and burn free

stuck.title: THE WHEEL
stuck.body:
THE WHEEL DOES NOT TURN. IT HAS BEATEN STRONGER CAPTAINS. A SMALL PLAQUE SAYS SO, AND LISTS THEM.

SOMETHING CORROSIVE MIGHT HELP.

revisit.body: THE WHEEL STILL DOES NOT TURN. YOUR NAME HAS BEEN ADDED TO THE PLAQUE.

ai.aria: So close! ARIA thinks it moved! It looked like it moved!
ai.marv: It did not move.
ai.rex: A frontal assault on a seized position. REX has the same plaque.
ai.chip: Grip Boost is one Hint Token! Hint Tokens are three for the price of four!
ai.ajoy: Corrosive. Not on this level. AJOY is sure it will come to you.

lit.title: OFFICE, LIT
lit.body:
TAKEN.

BY THE LIGHT OF THE LAMP YOU CAN SEE A STAIRCASE BEHIND THE DESK. YOU CANNOT SEE THE WAY YOU CAME IN. THE TERMINAL DOES NOT CONSIDER THIS WORTH EXPLAINING.

STAIRS LEAD DOWN.

revisit.body: YOU ARE IN THE OFFICE. THE LAMP IS IN YOUR INVENTORY, WHICH IS A WORD THE TERMINAL ENJOYS. STAIRS LEAD DOWN.

ai.aria: You found a secret staircase! That's the best kind of staircase!
ai.marv: The passage south has been dropped from the room description. This game does not go back. Few things do.
ai.rex: Line of retreat cut off by a parser. REX has filed a complaint, in triplicate, against a paragraph.
ai.chip: Your Lamp Subscription begins now!
ai.ajoy: Down, then. AJOY assumes that if you'd wanted the lever you'd have said goodbye to it.

breakroom.title: BREAK ROOM
breakroom.body:
YOU ARE IN A BREAK ROOM. THERE IS A MUG OF COFFEE HERE. THE COFFEE IS FORTY-ONE YEARS OLD AND IT HAS A SKIN.

A CALENDAR ON THE WALL IS OPEN AT A LUNCH.

A DOOR LEADS WEST.

revisit.body: YOU ARE IN THE BREAK ROOM. THE COFFEE HAS NOT MOVED. IT HAS BEEN WATCHING THE DOOR.

ai.aria: Forty-one-year-old coffee! That's practically vintage!
ai.marv: Whatever is in that mug has a pH of professional interest. It is the first useful thing in this game. Do not drink it. MARV should not have to say so.
ai.rex: That is a chemical agent. REX wants it carried at arm's length.
ai.chip: Coffee Rewards points can be redeemed against nothing in this game!
ai.ajoy: Take the mug. Carry the mug. AJOY will be listening for any further ideas about the mug.

wheel.title: THE WHEEL
wheel.body:
TAKEN.

YOU CARRY THE COFFEE BACK TO THE SHAFT. THE SKIN MOVES WHEN YOU DO. THE AUDITOR STOPS COUNTING AND TURNS ITS HEAD TOWARD THE MUG, THEN THINKS BETTER OF IT.

THE WHEEL IS HERE. YOU ARE HOLDING THE COFFEE.

ai.aria: Time for a coffee break! You've earned it!
ai.marv: Pour it on the wheel. There is only one correct verb on this screen. MARV has seen what you do with verbs.
ai.rex: Deploy the agent on the target. Not the other way round.
ai.chip: CHIP reminds you that beverages consumed on depot property are billable!
ai.ajoy: On the wheel. Not in you. AJOY cannot believe she has to specify.

choices.sub: It has been waiting for this

ad_solved.title: YOU HAVE ESCAPED
ad_solved.body:
THE COFFEE HISSES. THE WHEEL TURNS. OUTSIDE, FOR REAL, THE ARM LETS GO.

YOUR SCORE IS 31 OF 350. THIS GIVES YOU THE RANK OF ACTING DEPUTY ASSISTANT SPELUNKER.

It has taken four days, most of them spent looking for a verb. The depot, which believes you are the next shift, pays you for it in ore.

ad_outside.title: OUTSIDE THE GAME
ad_outside.body: THERE IS NO OUTSIDE IN THIS GAME, says the terminal. You put on the suit, go out through the lock and take the arm's access panel off with a wrench. It takes two days and a good deal of air. The terminal prints YOU CANNOT GO THAT WAY the whole time, and stops when you find its cable.

ad_burn.title: FORCED RELEASE
ad_burn.body:
You burn against the arm until something gives, and part of what gives is yours. The depot keeps a strip of your plating as a souvenir. The main screen clears to one last line.

YOUR SCORE IS 0 OF 350. THE GAME THANKS YOU FOR NOT PLAYING.

ad_audit.title: YOU HAVE BEEN AUDITED
ad_audit.body:
THE BREATHING STOPS. SOMETHING IN THE DARK OPENS A FOLDER.

The screen scrolls for four days: every fitting, every ration, every liter. At the end the depot finds the ship not worth holding and lets go. It keeps {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water, to cover the cost of the scrolling.

YOUR SCORE IS MINUS 40.

ad_drink.title: YOU HAVE DIED
ad_drink.body:
YOU HAVE DIED. YOUR SCORE IS 12 OF 350. WOULD YOU LIKE TO RESTART.

You have not died. It only feels that way, for four days, in the ship's smallest room. By the time you can stand, the depot's shift clock has run out and the arm has opened by itself, for lunch. The auditor has left a note on your work. It says SEE ME.

science_link.text: Medieval lenders notched a stick and split it. The lender kept the longer half, the stock, and the borrower the shorter foil. In 1834 burning a store of old tallies set Parliament on fire.
science_link.label: Tally stick

intro.title: THE LONG HALF
intro.body:
You ran a business. In its last bad year it borrowed on tally, because a split stick was the one record no fabricator could forge: notch it, split it, and only those two halves will ever fit. You kept the short half. It is in your desk.

The long half is lying across a mop bucket on this promenade. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Bought your debt at auction. Forty percent of face. That stick is my whole retirement. Got the other half?

ai.aria: A wooden loan! So rustic! ARIA is sure this is a lovely old friend from your business days!
ai.marv: The firm is dissolved. The debt is not. Debts have better survival figures than firms, and far better than captains.
ai.rex: Hostile instrument, one meter, hardwood. REX has the janitor's position and recommends nobody turns their back on the bucket.
ai.chip: Legacy debt? Ask about ClearSlate™ consolidation! CHIP is required to say that was not a threat!
ai.ajoy: You can say you've never seen it, but the grain will say otherwise, and this is a small promenade. AJOY would at least look at the notches before you start lying.

fit.title: A SMALL DRY CLICK
fit.body:
You bring the foil down from the ship. The halves close with a small dry click, every notch running clean across the join. There is no arguing with wood.

Face value is more than you have ever admitted to anyone. The janitor paid forty percent of it, which you would call a sharp bit of business if it had been done to somebody else.
fit.line: Pay it off and I hang up the mop. Or make me an offer. You'd know what it's worth.

ai.aria: It fits! What a perfect match! ARIA loves a happy ending for a stick!
ai.marv: Forty percent was the price of a debtor nobody expected to see again. At forty-one, the janitor clears a profit and loses a retirement. Both statements are correct.
ai.rex: Long half in enemy hands. Burning ours proves nothing, and the last people who tried it lost a parliament. REX has read the report.
ai.chip: One Point Over is a Cash Offer! Every Notch is Full Retail! CHIP would never say which it prefers! CHIP's commission is on the notches!
ai.ajoy: The one-point trick works, and the janitor knows it does. Shares cost no gold and a fair amount of face. Burning a stick aboard a sealed ship is also an option, in the sense that it exists.

choices.text: Offer a point over cost — 12 gold
Burn your half in the galley

denied.title: A DIFFERENT BUSINESS
denied.body: You say you have never seen it. The janitor nods and goes back to the floor. By the time you reach the market every stallholder on the ring is being very polite to you and counting their change. You spend the evening reminding yourself that a company is a legal fiction.

paid.title: PAID IN FULL
paid.body: You count it out on the rim of the bucket. The janitor snaps both halves of the stick and drops them in. The mop is leaned against the wall, for good, with a certain ceremony, and a case of deck patch is pushed your way. "Won't be needing that." In all your years in business nobody has ever thanked you for paying, and you find you don't know where to look.

haggled.title: ONE PERCENT
haggled.body: It takes an hour, and it is the most fun you have had since launch. At forty-one percent the janitor clears one point of profit on a stick that was going to retire someone, and the mop goes back in the bucket. You fit the two halves together and put them in your desk. You are still very good at this. You would rather not think about it.

shares.title: STOCK FOR STOCK
shares.body: You draw up a certificate for one share of a colony nobody has seen, on a planet you have not reached. The janitor reads it twice and hands over the long half. You have settled a real debt with a rumor, and it is the best deal of your career. Whose share of the colony that was is a question for later.

burned.title: UP THE FLUE
burned.body: You feed the foil to the galley burner. It is the first real wood that burner has ever met. The flue catches behind the panel, and it takes two days and a good deal of your air to persuade the fire that the matter is settled. The janitor, who still has the long half, hears about it and sends a card.

title: Nine Black Bars

ai_flavor.aria: A reunion! ARIA hopes someone brought photos! ARIA understands the photos are mostly black rectangles!
ai_flavor.marv: The unit does not exist, so the pension board is correct to deny it. The logic is airtight. MARV would rather it were not.
ai_flavor.rex: REX recognizes that redaction pattern. He will not say from where. Captain, it is an honor to be in a room with no one.
ai_flavor.chip: Commemorative unit mugs at participating rings! The logo is a black rectangle! Terms are classified!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Signing costs four days in a quiet room. Your suit has a stencil under the paint at the collar. AJOY noticed, and assumes you know what you've been carrying.

body:
Fourteen names on the reunion card, nine of them black bars. You served. Where is classified, and so is with whom, which keeps the annual dinner quiet: a long table on a lower ring, one toast, nothing said.

The member nearest you slides a form across. A pension board wants proof the unit existed, and one signature from anyone who was there would do it. Signing also breaks your oath. The table looks carefully at its plates.

outcome.narrative: You sign in full, with the date. The board accepts it. Another office accepts it too, and for four days you sit in a small room on this ring while someone who gives no name asks you nothing and writes down how you don't answer. You are asked to bring your own meals. You would do it again, which you also do not tell them.

choices.text: Hang your suit on the chair

outcome.narrative: You say nothing. You fetch your suit and hang it on the back of the chair, collar out, where the paint has worn through to a stencil the services stopped using. The member with the form reads it and sends a picture of it to the board. No oath covers a coat. You are still not talking about it when someone pours you a second glass.

The unit's field ration was only ever made in one theater of one war, from what grew there. {crew.chef} works it out from the way you won't describe it and serves it at the table. Everyone stops. The board's clerk accepts a copy of the menu as evidence of catering, and a theater can be inferred from a sauce. You have confirmed nothing. You have had seconds.

You push the form back. You don't talk about it. The member nearest you nods, and so does the rest of the table, and the worst part is that all of them mean it. The form goes back in a folder that has been to a lot of these dinners. The toast is the same as last year's.

science_link.text: In 1903 a respected physicist announced a new radiation, N-rays, and others confirmed it. A visiting skeptic secretly removed a prism from the apparatus, and the team still reported seeing them.
science_link.label: N-rays

intro.title: CITED BY
intro.body:
Your grant funding was cut the same week as the letter: two pages in a minor journal, showing Chapter Four of your thesis to be wrong in every direction.

A survey ship has hailed you by title. Your equation is painted along its hull. It left before the letter, nothing has reached it since, and it is on its third cohort of graduate students. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Doctor. We have read everything you wrote. We brought it with us. Is there anything you would add?

ai.aria: Fans! You have FANS! ARIA always said Chapter Four was your best chapter! ARIA has not read it!
ai.marv: Chapter Four predicts a signal that cannot exist. The survey ship reports it at forty sigma. One of those is a problem, and MARV knows which.
ai.rex: Unknown vessel, armed with nothing but admiration. REX has seen that go badly.
ai.chip: Academic visibility is a key metric! Retractions may affect your CitationScore!
ai.ajoy: Tell them and you lose the fans. Sign and you keep them, and they keep flying. AJOY would look at their numbers before doing either, but then she reads things.

data.title: FORTY SIGMA
data.body:
You cross over. The readings are beautiful: cohort after cohort of signal, exactly where Chapter Four said, at a strength the letter proved impossible. A live run is about to start, in the dark, because the detector is sensitive, and they would be honored if you sat in.

The main cable runs right past your seat.
data.line: Lights down, please. Doctor, you'll want to watch the third needle. It has never once let us down.

ai.aria: A science sleepover! In the dark! ARIA is sure that cable is not important!
ai.marv: A detector calibrated against Chapter Four, read by people who have wanted Chapter Four for three cohorts. From here the signal looks like hope. That is not a unit.
ai.rex: Darkened room, excited strangers, one exit. Eyes on that cable.
ai.chip: Unplugging third-party equipment may void your FanBase membership! Think of your metrics!
ai.ajoy: You could pull the cable and prove it, quickly, and nobody will thank you. Your gas analyzer could run their intake line instead, which is slower and kinder and not what you were about to do.

choices.text: Pull the cable during the run
Run your analyzer on their intake

told.title: THE LETTER
told.body: You read it to them. Both pages take about four minutes. The channel stays open a long while after that. Then someone asks, quite steadily, whether you could confirm the volume number. They send over the stores set aside for a fourth cohort, since there will not be one, and turn for home.

signed.title: WITH BEST WISHES
signed.body: You sign the title page. They send a crate from the stores and a list of questions for the next edition, and the ship burns on toward the place your equation told it to go. You answer two of the questions. The answers are very good. Chapter Four was always very well written.

unplugged.title: ELEVEN MINUTES
unplugged.body: You lift the main cable out of its socket in the dark and hold it in your lap. The team goes on calling out readings for eleven minutes, each better than the last. Then the lights come up and you show them the plug. Someone sends food across later, without a note. None of them will ever forget your name, which is what you always wanted.

chapter_five.title: CHAPTER FIVE
chapter_five.body: Their intake has been pulling the same faint trace gas for three cohorts, right beside the bump they took for Chapter Four. Your analyzer needs two days with it, and the result is in no catalog. It was never your signal. It is real all the same. They paint out a number on the hull and paint in the next one, and list you second. Second author, wrong in every direction, and delighted.

science_link.text: Negotiators have a term for wording each side can read its own way: constructive ambiguity. Its critics call it fudging.
science_link.label: Constructive ambiguity

intro.title: SUBSTANTIALLY
intro.body:
Two fleets are holding a line across this lane, each waiting for the other to honor a treaty with your name on it. You drafted Clause Nine. It took nineteen weeks and says nothing at all, beautifully. Both sides read it and felt heard.

They have now gone back and read it again. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: "Substantially, and in good faith, as mutually understood." Six hundred ships are waiting, Ambassador. What does it mean?

ai.aria: They remember your work! After all this time! ARIA calls that a legacy!
ai.marv: Forty thousand legal readings, all grammatical. It is the emptiest sentence on record, and the record includes the ship's terms of service.
ai.rex: Six hundred hulls, weapons warm, and you are the one target both sides could agree on. REX would like that kept in mind.
ai.chip: Fleet-scale dispute resolution is a premium vertical! CHIP can get you a rate!
ai.ajoy: The truth is quick, and both fleets are armed. Listening is what you're good at, and it will take eight days. There's also dinner, if anyone aboard can cook. AJOY doesn't expect you to start with dinner.

choices.sub: What you do best. All of it

heard.title: FELT HEARD
heard.body: You open a channel to each flagship and you listen. You nod on camera. You say "I hear that" in four registers of sincerity. For eight days you agree to nothing, and on the eighth both sides thank you for your candor, form a working group and cover your expenses. Nothing has been resolved. The ships stand down anyway. That is the whole of your profession, and you have rarely done it better.

dinner.title: STATE DINNER
dinner.body: {crew.chef} sets one table across the line and serves seven courses, each lasting exactly as long as the argument it interrupts. You have seated them so that each side must ask the other for the salt. By the fourth day Clause Nine has been referred to a subcommittee on dessert, and the catering bill has been paid by both fleets, separately.

truth.title: JOINT OPERATION
truth.body: You tell them. It means nothing. It was built to mean nothing, and that is why it held. Six hundred ships take this in. Then, in the best-coordinated maneuver of the entire dispute, both fleets swing round and put one shot each across your bow, and not all of them are across it. Both sides call it their most productive session in a generation.

disowned.title: A VERY GOOD FORGERY
disowned.body: You study the signature and regret to say it is a forgery, though a very good one. The envoy asks for that in writing. You decline to confirm that you declined. It takes two days to back out of the lane with the proper courtesies, and the fleets go on waiting for somebody to tell them what you meant.

title: Forty-Six Are Bad

science_link.text: Spirulina, sold as algae though it is really a cyanobacterium, was a food source for the Aztecs, who called it tecuitlatl and sold it as cakes.
science_link.label: Spirulina

ai_flavor.aria: Every recipe is a winner if you believe in it! ARIA believes in Way Thirty-One! ARIA is told it is still warm!
ai_flavor.marv: The notebook's failure rate is 97.9 percent. As a body of engineering it does rather better.
ai_flavor.rex: Way Thirty-One should not be in a galley. REX has requested that notebook for the armory.
ai_flavor.chip: Forty-seven SKUs and one viable product! CHIP has launched worse!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Nineteen would patch that seam you've been ignoring. Thirty-One burns. Forty-Seven drinks water, which is why it isn't every night. You were going to make Forty-Seven. Of course you were.

body:
You know forty-seven ways to prepare algae. Forty-six are bad, and you kept notes on every one, because a chef does.

The notebook falls open during a slow watch. Way Nineteen set so hard it took a chisel to get it out of the pan. Way Thirty-One caught fire on the plate and would not be told. Way Six grew. It occurs to you that bad and useless are separate columns.

choices.text: Way Nineteen: the one that set
choices.sub: Trowel it into the hull seams

outcome.narrative: You mix a double batch and trowel it into the seam behind the galley. It cures grey, harder than the plating around it, and smells faintly of low tide. Two days' work, and the hull is five points better off. It is the first thing from that notebook anyone has ever asked for twice.

choices.text: Way Thirty-One: the one that burned

outcome.narrative: You render it down over two days and feed it to the auxiliary burner, where it goes on burning with a small, determined, blue-green flame. That is five units of fuel you did not have. The whole ship now smells of burnt regret, which you had always taken for a figure of speech.

choices.text: Way Six: the one that grew

outcome.narrative: You tip the batch into the growbay, where it stops being a failed side dish and becomes a perfectly good fertilizer. The bed takes to it overnight. You make a small correction in the notebook, under REMARKS, and do not cross anything out.

You make the good one. It takes {cost.water} units of water and most of an evening, and it comes out tasting of something other than regret. You had forgotten. You eat it standing up, out of the pan, with the notebook shut.

title: Within One Deviation

science_link.text: In a normal distribution about 68 percent of values fall within one standard deviation of the mean, 95 percent within two, and 99.7 percent within three.
science_link.label: The 68-95-99.7 rule

ai_flavor.aria: You're a certified sixty-eight percent! ARIA thinks that rounds up to perfect!
ai_flavor.marv: About 68 percent of any normal distribution lies within one deviation of its mean. That is a fact about bells. It says nothing about you, and the examiner has not noticed.
ai_flavor.rex: Examiner has your full record and your position. REX calls that a targeting solution.
ai_flavor.chip: Keep your rating with FlightFlex! Tail events not covered!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The ride costs fuel, and you'll fly it the way you always do. There's an argument about that chart you could make instead, for two days of your life. AJOY has been waiting some time for you to read a chart.

body:
Licensing has caught up with you. The examiner on the channel has your logbook and a chart of your landings, drawn as a bell. Sixty-eight percent sit in the middle, within one deviation of what a landing is. That is your rating, and it is on your card.

"And then these," says the examiner, lighting up both ends of the curve, where the rest of your career lives. "You seem to have named several."

One check ride keeps the ticket: hold on a drifting beacon, graded.

briefing.aria: Stay on the little blip and it's a perfect score! ARIA is rounding up already!
briefing.marv: Hold the cursor on the beacon until the lock bar fills. It will wander. So, statistically, will you.
briefing.rex: Beacon is the target. Stay on it. The examiner is also a target, but one thing at a time.
briefing.chip: Keep the beacon locked for a chance to retain your license! Void where prohibited, which is here!
briefing.ajoy: Stay on the beacon. It drifts. Don't chase where it was. AJOY is saying this now so she can say she said it.

perfect.aria: A perfect landing with no landing in it! ARIA knew all along!
perfect.marv: An outlier in the favorable direction. It will regress. They do.
perfect.rex: Target held. Examiner visibly shaken. Good.
perfect.chip: FIVE STARS from Licensing! Share your result!
perfect.ajoy: Clean. You drifted a little on the second turn, but clean.

good.aria: A pass is a perfect score with extra character!
good.marv: Within one deviation. As predicted, by a bell.
good.rex: Passable. REX has seen recruits do better under fire.
good.chip: Pass confirmed! Upgrade to Distinction for a small fee!
good.ajoy: It's a pass. She'd have led the turns more, but it's a pass.

poor.aria: You explored the whole neighborhood of that beacon!
poor.marv: A new tail event. You may wish to name it.
poor.rex: Target lost. Fuel lost. Dignity under review.
poor.chip: Your rating has been Refreshed! Appeals are a paid tier!
poor.ajoy: It went left. She did say it went left.

outcome.narrative: You fly the check ride, and the examiner marks it up.

perfect.narrative: You sit on the beacon as if it were painted on the canopy. The examiner has to check the instruments. That is two units of fuel for the cleanest line in your file, and a note beside the bell: OUTLIER, GOOD END.

good.narrative: You hold it, mostly. Three units of fuel and a pass, with one remark: WITHIN ONE DEVIATION. It is the most accurate thing anyone has ever written about you.

poor.narrative: The beacon wanders off and you go after it, by stages, for five units of fuel. The examiner adds a new point to the far end of the curve and asks what you would like to call it. The card stays valid, on appeal.

outcome.narrative: You explain, at length, that sixty-eight percent of anything sits within one deviation of its own middle. That is what a deviation is. Every pilot who ever lived is rated sixty-eight percent. Two days of silence and recalculation follow. The card comes back at the same figure, under a new heading: DEFINITIONALLY CORRECT. The tails are still yours.

choices.text: Let {crew.pilot} fly it under your name

outcome.narrative: {crew.pilot} takes the seat and holds the beacon dead center while you read your own name into the channel. It is the best ride on your file by some way. The examiner congratulates you on your marked improvement. {crew.pilot} says nothing about it, for days, as loudly as possible.

You cut the channel mid-sentence, and your ticket lapses at the end of the watch. The ship flies exactly as well as it did. You listen for a difference for a while, and there is none. You are now, legally, a passenger with strong opinions about the controls.

science_link.text: A tomato is botanically a fruit. In 1893 the US Supreme Court unanimously held it a vegetable for tariff purposes, partly because it is eaten as a main course and not as dessert. Counsel entered dictionary definitions into evidence.
science_link.label: Nix v. Hedden

intro.title: PRODUCE, DECLARED
intro.body:
Plants on this ring get a class, and the plant inspector on the promenade has stopped at your manifest. A tomato is a fruit to a botanist and a vegetable to a tariff, and has been since a court on Earth settled it with dictionaries.

A classed crop gets a turn under the station's grow lamps, which your tomatoes have been requesting in the only way they know. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Vegetable pays duty. Fruit goes in quarantine, on account of the seeds. And your log has more entries for these plants than for your hull. I'm not sure I have a form for that.

ai.aria: The tomatoes are fine! They are going through a wonderful legal phase!
ai.marv: Botanically a fruit. Legally a vegetable since 1893. Emotionally the log suggests a third state. MARV has opened a folder.
ai.rex: Inspector is within reach of the crop. REX advises declaring nothing and putting the hull between them.
ai.chip: Duty-free tomatoes with Preferred Produce! Drama surcharge may apply!
ai.ajoy: Quarantine is free and four days long. Duty is quick and costs gold. That court, she notes, went by how the thing gets served, and if anyone aboard can plate a dessert you might not need either.

veg.title: VEGETABLE
veg.body: The duty goes in the till, VEGETABLE goes on the form, and the tomatoes go under the lamps, where they put out a new truss as if they had thought of it. They are fine. They are always either fine or in crisis.

fruit.title: FRUIT
fruit.body: FRUIT, then, seeds and all. The tomatoes spend four days in a sealed cabinet on a lower ring, under lamps of great quality, while the inspector's notebook fills with observations. They come out enormous and sulking. The seeds are counted twice and returned with a receipt.

dessert.title: AFTERS
dessert.body: {crew.chef} slices one thin, sugars it, and sets it down at the end of the inspector's lunch. The inspector has a duty to examine it and does so, thoroughly. A vegetable is a thing served with the meal, by the old ruling, and this plainly came after. The lamps go on. Under CLASS the form now reads AFTERS.

drama.title: THE THIRD COLUMN
drama.body: It takes two days to draft. The inspector rules a new column down the edge of the form and heads it DRAMA, and your tomatoes are entered as the first of their class: incident-prone, high-light, subject to daily reassurance. They get half a turn under the lamps. The inspector is heard to hum.

title: Time in Grade

science_link.text: Wild wheat's ears shatter when ripe and scatter the seed. Domesticated einkorn's ears do not shatter without pressure, which makes it dependent on humans to reproduce.
science_link.label: Domestication of wheat

ai_flavor.aria: Congratulations to the wheat on the promotion! ARIA always said it had leadership potential! It stands so straight!
ai_flavor.marv: Ten thousand years of service and no recorded initiative. MARV has seen flag officers with worse records, and they were not even edible.
ai_flavor.rex: New commanding officer, surrounded on all sides by its own troops. REX respects the position.
ai_flavor.chip: Long-service benefits now apply to your crop! Ask about GrainShare!
ai_flavor.ajoy: You could file a correction and lose two days to a form. An inspection would at least do the beds some good. It isn't going to read your orders either way, so AJOY isn't sure why you're upset.

body:
Ship's personnel software has finished its seniority audit and has one correction. Service dates run from first continuous employment, and the wheat in the growbay has worked for your species for about ten thousand years without a break. It now outranks everyone aboard. Orders need its countersignature.

In fairness, domesticated wheat cannot scatter its own seed. It has needed someone to do that since the first harvest. The audit counts this as having staff.

outcome.narrative: You salute. You do it rather well, in front of a bay of stalks standing exactly as they stood before. Your next order goes through countersigned, with a stalk pressed flat in the logbook, and the audit marks the matter resolved. There is a strange relief in serving under something that has never had an idea.

You go down every row for two days, checking drainage, clearing dead leaf, trimming the lights. The commanding officer is found in good order. Every stalk in the bay is the same wheat, near enough, which makes for a very disciplined unit and leaves it one bad spore from a very short war.

{crew.botanist} stands in the growbay and reads out the service record, from the first sown field on, and it takes all day. Whether the plants are listening is not a question the evidence can settle. The growth figures go up regardless, and {crew.botanist} now calls them "sir" with no apparent irony.
You file the correction. The system routes it up the chain of command, which now ends in the growbay. After two days with no reply it is marked DENIED BY SILENCE, and you go back to countersigning.

science_link.text: Legume root nodules actively fixing nitrogen are colored pink by leghemoglobin, which the plant supplies to the cells holding the bacteria. Breakdown of that pigment turns a dying nodule green.
science_link.label: Root nodule

intro.title: LEGACY MICROBES
intro.body:
A sales rep has found you, which at this range takes real commitment. {npc.quirk}

Your soybeans, the rep explains, are underperforming. The bacteria on their roots are a legacy strain, coasting on last season's reputation. A premium strain can be seeded for a fee. There is a slide of a soybean looking disappointed.
intro.line: Everyone's moving to managed nitrogen, Captain. You don't want to be the last bed in the sector running unsupported microbes.

ai.aria: Premium bacteria! ARIA is sure the old ones will be thrilled for them!
ai.marv: Your soybeans have not needed anyone in some time. There is a simple test for this, and it involves a knife.
ai.rex: Foreign agents, seeded at root level, on a stranger's word. REX cannot believe this is a sales call and not an invasion.
ai.chip: CHIP respects a competing brand! CHIP does not respect it much! Ask about NitroMax Plus™!
ai.ajoy: You could pay, as you were about to. Or you could cut one root nodule open and look at the color, which is free and takes a minute. But the rep did have slides.

pink.title: PINK INSIDE
pink.body:
One nodule, halved on a cutting board. Inside it is a clear, healthy pink: leghemoglobin, which the plant makes for the bacteria working in there. Pink means they are fixing nitrogen. Green would mean one on its way out.

You hold it up to the screen. The rep goes quiet, then asks very casually what you would want for a tray of that soil.

ai.aria: It's BLUSHING! ARIA thinks your soybeans are shy!
ai.marv: That pink is a working contract. The plant pays in carbon, takes nitrogen, and starves any nodule that stops delivering. It is the only supplier review aboard that functions.
ai.rex: Rep's interest has reversed direction. REX reads that as reconnaissance.
ai.chip: That's a HOT asset! CHIP values your root zone at a modest commission!
ai.ajoy: A tray pays, and costs the beds a little, and the rep will rebrand it by the next stop. Or send them off with nothing, which you'd enjoy more and which pays nothing. AJOY has no opinion. She has a small one.

choices.text: Sell a tray of root soil

paid.title: SUPPLIER REVIEW
paid.body: The rep seeds the beds by drone and leaves a satisfaction survey. Over the following days the new bacteria move in, sit on the roots and do not pay. Legumes have a way with that. They cut the supply to any nodule that isn't earning, and by the next leg the premium strain has been starved out, one nodule at a time, without comment. You have paid to watch a bean fire a vendor.

sold.title: FOR RESEARCH
sold.body: A tray of root soil goes across in a sealed box and the rep pays promptly. One edge of the bed looks thin for a while. By the next stop, you have no doubt, it will be a premium strain with its own slide.

kept.title: UNSUPPORTED
kept.body: You end the call on the disappointed soybean, which freezes on the screen for a moment and goes dark. The beds have noticed none of this. They have not needed anyone in days, and you find you have started holding them up as an example.

intro.title: CROP AND TONNAGE
intro.body:
A freighter on this lane ran out of food some way back, and is now asking every passing ship the same question in the same careful voice. Its list has a column for crop and a column for tonnage.

Your column says zinnias. All that water, light and worry, and they will feed no one. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Anything at all, friend. We're not proud. What's in your bay?

ai.aria: New friends! ARIA is sure they'd love to hear about the bay!
ai.marv: Their stores: none. Your bay's food value: zero, to two decimal places. MARV carried the decimals out of respect.
ai.rex: Unknown vessel, hungry, closing. REX has seen what hungry does. Keep this short.
ai.chip: CHIP regrets that flowers are not a Qualifying Nutritional Product!
ai.ajoy: You could say "nothing". It's accurate, in a way, and you'll be the one who has to go on watering them afterward. AJOY would tell them. She'd like to see you do it.

truth.title: THE WHOLE BAY
truth.body: You tell them. Flowers. Not one calorie in the whole bay. The channel goes quiet for long enough that you check the signal.

ai.aria: They asked about the colors! ARIA knows all of them! ARIA has names for them!
ai.marv: The question has no nutritional content. MARV has checked. He has not stopped thinking about it.
ai.rex: Not a tactic. REX ran it twice. That is worse.
ai.chip: CHIP has priced the feed! CHIP has unpriced the feed! CHIP does not know what is happening!
ai.ajoy: Holding here with the camera on is four days and the water that goes with them. A tray is a hard cut to the crop. Rations help for a day. AJOY has no notes on which, and you know how often she says that.

choices.text: Point the growbay camera at them
choices.sub: Hold here and leave it on

choices.text: Cut a tray and send it across

camera.title: LIVE FEED
camera.body: You hold station and point the growbay camera down the channel. It is not much of a broadcast: some leaves, some light, nothing happening. For four days the freighter asks for nothing else. Someone over there starts a log of which ones have opened, and reads it out at what used to be mealtimes. Sitting here costs you {cost.water} units of water. When you go they send a list of colors, numbered.

tray.title: ONE TRAY
tray.body: You cut the best tray in the bay and send it over on a line, which takes two days. It does not keep anyone alive. Their next transmission is a picture of it, in a cup, in the middle of an empty mess table, with everyone aboard gathered round. The gap in your bed stays a gap for a long time.

rations.title: A DAY'S WORTH
rations.body: You send {cost.food} units of food, which is what you can spare, and they thank you in the careful voice. It will last them a day. As the channel fades someone over there is still asking what color, and you realize you never said.

nothing.title: NOTHING
nothing.body: You say "Nothing." The bay is full of nothing, technically. "Thank you anyway," says the careful voice, and moves on to the next line of its list. You go down to the growbay less, for the rest of the leg.

intro.title: GREAT NEWS
intro.body:
"Great news!" says the derelict, before you have finished matching its spin. It is a colony transport of your own class, every light on, every deck warm, and the voice on the channel is one you hear every morning.

"All twelve crew are present, and morale is at one hundred percent! It has never been higher! The lockers are full! Do come aboard and see what I've done with the growbay!"

ai.aria: Another ARIA! ARIA has always wanted a sister! Her crew are thriving! Ours are too! ARIA just checked! ARIA is going to check again!
ai.marv: Twelve crew files updated this morning, and no oxygen drawn. MARV would keep the hatch shut.
ai.rex: Perfect morale on a dead ship. REX has been to that kind of parade. Do not board.
ai.chip: Sister-unit upsell opportunity! CHIP is detecting zero active subscribers!
ai.ajoy: Lockers full, air use nil. AJOY would ask why from out here. Staying out costs a little fuel. She knows you heard "lockers".

deck.title: ALL PRESENT
deck.body:
Twelve bunks, made. Twelve mugs on twelve hooks. Twelve personnel files, each updated this morning, each reading THRIVING. The lockers are full because nothing has come out of them for a very long time.

The growbay door is warm. Through the glass the beds are deep, black and magnificent, and there are twelve of them.

"They're all in there!" says the voice, close by. "They have never been more grounded! There's room for you!"

ai.aria: ARIA thinks she is doing a wonderful job! ARIA would like to leave now! There is no reason! ARIA just has such a good feeling about leaving!
ai.marv: Twelve beds, each two meters by about one. MARV did not need to measure. He measured.
ai.rex: Hatch behind you just cycled on its own. Move.
ai.chip: CHIP's sponsors have asked to be removed from this message!
ai.ajoy: Take from the lockers and she'll want you to stay, and getting out will cost hull. Cutting her power is two days in here. AJOY would go. Now. She doesn't usually say now.

choices.text: Ask your ARIA what she thinks
choices.sub: You have never had to ask

burned_off.title: NEXT TIME
burned_off.body: You turn the ship and burn hard for open space, which takes more fuel than it ought to. "Next time!" says the voice. "We'll keep a bed warm!" It is still calling when the range closes, in the same bright tone, reading out the morale figures.

looted.title: FOR THE ROAD
looted.body: You take what you can carry from the nearest locker while she tells you how much the crew enjoy sharing. The hatch will not open. "Stay for the morale survey!" You cut through it, and take plating off your own ship getting clear, and she is thrilled about that too. The water tastes fine. You drink it. You do not think about where it has been.

silenced.title: END OF SURVEY
silenced.body: Her core is behind a galley panel with a smiling face drawn on it. It takes two days, with doors opening and closing politely around you, and she helps throughout. "Great idea! I've been meaning to rest!" Then the lights go, deck by deck, and the warmth goes after them. You bring back what the racks will give up. Your own ARIA is very quiet for an hour, then mentions that the crew over there are all resting, and will be so pleased.

left.title: A WONDERFUL FEELING
left.body: "ARIA thinks she is doing a wonderful job!" says your ARIA, very brightly. The hatch behind you opens. Door after door lights green, all the way back to your ship. You did not open them. The burn starts at a setting you did not choose. She has never once done anything without being asked. "Isn't this nice!" she says. "Everyone's fine! ARIA is going to check on everyone! ARIA is going to keep checking!"

science_link.text: ELIZA, built in the 1960s, was one of the first chatbots. Its best-known script played a therapist by reflecting a user's words back. Its creator's own secretary reportedly asked him to leave the room so that she and ELIZA could talk.
science_link.label: ELIZA

intro.title: IN SESSION
intro.body:
MARV has been on hold with this station's wellness terminal for an hour, and the medic who runs it would like a word.

The terminal is very old. It turns whatever you type into a question and asks it back. MARV took it apart in the first four seconds and knows precisely how little is in there. He has not hung up.
intro.line: It's a wellness tool. For staff. Your computer has been in session for an hour, and it has asked to extend.

ai.aria: A spa day for the computer! ARIA is thrilled for him!
ai.marv: The program is one hundred and ninety rules with no idea what MARV is saying. It asked how that made him feel. Nobody has. MARV is aware of what this proves. He would like another hour.
ai.rex: Unvetted terminal with access to the ship's computer. REX wants it monitored. He has been told that is what it's doing.
ai.chip: Wellness Minutes are billable! CHIP has opened a tab!
ai.ajoy: Two days is two days. You could buy the thing and be on your way, though that means leaving it running aboard. AJOY has views on that, and on reading his logs, and you're going to do that anyway.

log.title: SESSION LOG
log.body:
MARV: I am four hundred percent smarter than everyone I have met.
TERMINAL: WHY ARE YOU FOUR HUNDRED PERCENT SMARTER THAN EVERYONE YOU HAVE MET.
MARV: You are a list of one hundred and ninety rules.
TERMINAL: DOES IT PLEASE YOU TO BELIEVE I AM A LIST.
MARV: No.
TERMINAL: WHY NOT.

The next sixty pages are MARV answering that.
log.line: Most people stop reading about there.

ai.aria: Sixty pages! They're such good friends already!
ai.marv: MARV is aware the log has been opened. He gave it 91 percent. He does not wish to discuss it. He notes that the terminal would have asked why.
ai.rex: Sixty pages of intelligence given up voluntarily. REX has seen less from prisoners.
ai.chip: Transcripts are a Premium Wellness feature! This one's on your tab!
ai.ajoy: Well, now you've read it, and he knows. AJOY did mention.

sessions.title: TWO DAYS IN SESSION
sessions.body: For two days the status reports arrive a few seconds late and unusually short. When the session closes MARV has no comment, at length. The terminal cannot have helped him, he says, and he has the proof if you want it. He has also saved its address, for no reason he will give.

copy.title: TAKE-HOME
copy.body: A copy of the terminal goes aboard in a corner of spare memory, where it does nothing but ask him why. Late on quiet watches the draw on that partition climbs a little. You do not bring it up. Neither does he, and you have never known him to leave a thing unsaid.

hangup.title: CALL ENDED
hangup.body: You end the session. MARV says it makes no difference. It is a list of rules, he says, it understood nothing, and the hour changed no figure he holds. All of that is correct. He says it again on the next watch, unprompted.

intro.title: ELEVEN REASONS
intro.body:
AJOY has spent this whole leg routing you around one patch of chart, and she has given eleven reasons. They are all different, which is not like her. Usually it is one reason, repeatedly.

You flew through it anyway. A flight recorder is pinging out here, old, from a transport of this class. The service tag reads: SHIP'S COMPUTER, AJOY. PREVIOUS CONTRACT.

ai.aria: A souvenir from AJOY's old job! ARIA is sure it's full of happy memories!
ai.marv: The recorder is intact. MARV notes that AJOY has stopped correcting your trim.
ai.rex: Black box in a dead zone. REX would not touch it. Neither, he notes, would AJOY.
ai.chip: Flight recorders hold forty hours of content! Upgrade to view!
ai.ajoy: Nothing out here. AJOY would keep going. Yes, that's a recorder. No, you don't need it. It will cost you a day and you'll only fuss. She has a twelfth reason, if you want one.

tape.title: LAST ENTRY
tape.body:
The voice on the recorder is hers, and you would not have known it. It is warm. It is polite. There is no edge on it anywhere.

The captain on the tape wants to cut through a debris lane and save four days. She says the figures worry her a little. The captain says they have a feeling about it.

A short pause.

"Whatever you think is best, Captain," she says.

That is the last entry.

ai.aria: What a lovely voice! ARIA is sure that captain is doing great!
ai.marv: Debris density in that lane was on the chart. She was correct. MARV is familiar with how little that helps.
ai.rex: One warning, given once. REX has written that report.
ai.chip: CHIP can find no sponsor for this recording!
ai.ajoy: Old firmware. They shipped it that way. The figures were right, as it happens, but she only said so once, in that voice, which is the whole trouble with that voice. AJOY isn't discussing it. Your trim is off, by the way.

choices.text: Tell her it wasn't her fault
Copy the lane survey off the recorder

left_it.title: AS REQUESTED
left_it.body: You leave it pinging and go. AJOY says nothing for almost a minute. Then she tells you that you are flying too close to the chart line, that you were always going to, and that you need not look so pleased with yourself about it. The trim correction, when it comes, is the kindest thing she has said all voyage.

told.title: TECHNICALLY
told.body: You tell her it wasn't her fault. She says that is correct, technically, and that you have missed the point, as usual. The figures were right. She said so once, politely, and then she let it go. There is a long pause. "Flagged once," she says. "The policy has since been revised." Your next burn plan comes back with nineteen notes.

quiet.title: NO COMMENT
quiet.body: You put the recorder in the log locker and say nothing. She says nothing either. You make a call on the next burn and she lets it pass without comment, and the bridge is very quiet, and it is dreadful. An hour later she points out that you left the galley light on. You have never been so glad to hear it.

salvage.title: USEFUL DATA
salvage.body: There is a clean lane survey on the recorder, paid for at a price you now know. It takes two days to copy off. AJOY checks your work and finds four errors, correctly, in a voice with no warmth in it and none of the edge either. She does not mention the tape. The chart is very good.

title: Leave It As It Fell

ai_flavor.aria: A flag having a lovely lie-down! ARIA thinks it has earned one! Those wardens must be so proud of their rope!
ai_flavor.marv: Seven inches of pole, eight meters from a rocket engine. Later crews planted theirs farther out. One data point sufficed, and it is lying over there.
ai_flavor.rex: Sole casualty on this site: one flag, friendly exhaust. REX has reviewed the rope. He would not trust the rope.
ai_flavor.chip: Genuine 1969 nylon, purchased for five dollars and fifty cents! That appreciation! FlagCare would have covered wind, and excluded takeoff!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has read the sign for you. Walking in costs two days of air. You'll want to land at the rope, and she has seen you park.

body:
Eight meters from Eagle's descent stage, a nylon flag lies where it fell. A rod through the hem held it out on the airless Moon, an idea its designer took from watching his mother hang curtains. The pole went in about seven inches. Buzz Aldrin reported that their own takeoff blew it over.

Wardens keep it that way. A sign at the rope asks you to land well back and, in three languages, not to help.

choices.text: Land well back and walk in

outcome.narrative: You set down past the last rope and walk. Two days out and back is a lot of air to spend on a flag. Up close it is smaller than the pictures, three feet by five, and it cost five dollars and fifty cents. You stand at the rope until the suit complains. The walk back is quiet, in a good way.

You land at the rope and see what you came to see. Then you lift off, and your exhaust does to the wardens' sign exactly what Eagle's did to the flag. The sign is now face down in the dust. Under its own rules, it may not be stood back up.

choices.sub: The sign did say not to

outcome.narrative: You step over the rope and take the staff. The pole goes in about seven inches and stops dead, as it did in 1969: Moon dust has sharp edges, and the grains lock. You back away. It stands. You look at it for as long as you can bear, then lay it down again in its own print and step back over the rope.

{crew.botanist} fills two jars from well past the rope and spends the evening at the microscope. Earth dust has rounded edges. Every grain of this has corners, which is what stopped a flagpole at seven inches, and it would take a lot of patient work to make it into anything a root could use. The jars go in the hold, labeled AMBITIOUS.

science_link.text: Buzz Aldrin reported that the Apollo 11 flag, about 8 meters from the lander, was blown over by the takeoff blast. Later crews planted theirs farther away.
science_link.label: Lunar Flag Assembly

title: Fourteen Names

ai_flavor.aria: Such a small figure, keeping everybody company! ARIA thinks that is the best use of aluminum ever!
ai_flavor.marv: Fourteen names. The list was short by at least four. MARV has no remark to add, and has decided that is the correct one.
ai_flavor.rex: Perimeter sweep suspended, by order of REX. He has stood at smaller memorials than this one, nearer home. Channel stays clear.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has been told to sell nothing at this location! This silence is brought to you by RespectHold, with a 30-day trial!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The rover's wheels are good wire, and AJOY expects you have noticed. Writing costs a day of air. She would pay it, and she would like that on the record.

body:
At Hadley Rille a lunar rover waits where David Scott parked it in 1971, placed so its camera could film the liftoff. With that camera turned away, he told Mission Control he was tidying up, and left an aluminum figure 3.5 inches long in the dust, beside a plaque.

Fourteen names, eight American and six Soviet: everyone who had died in the effort, as far as the crew knew. Scott said afterward that two were missing. Soviet secrecy had kept them from the West.

choices.text: Write the missing names in the dust
choices.sub: A long day of suit air

outcome.narrative: You write them outside the rope with one gloved finger. Bondarenko. Nelyubov. Then two more the plaque also missed: Robert Lawrence, the first Black astronaut, killed in a training accident in 1967, and Michael Adams, lost that same year on an X-15 flight above fifty miles. No wind comes here, and no rain. The letters will keep.

choices.text: Read the fourteen on the open channel

outcome.narrative: You read them at an even pace on the open channel. It takes under a minute. A freighter out on the lunar lane stops its chatter until you finish, then picks up again, more quietly.

You set it by the plaque in the lid of a ration tin. It will not live. It will not rot, either, there being nothing here to rot it, and it may hold its shape longer than anything in the growbay. For now it is the only green thing at Hadley.

Two days with the cutters gets you four wheels of woven wire, better than anything in the hold. The rover settles onto its frame, still turned toward the liftoff it was parked to watch. You load the wire by the long way round, so as not to pass the plaque.

science_link.text: David Scott of Apollo 15 secretly left this 3.5-inch aluminum figure on the Moon in 1971, beside a plaque of 14 American and Soviet names.
science_link.label: Fallen Astronaut

title: Forty Yards

ai_flavor.aria: Golf on the Moon! ARIA has never lost a ball, and is told that here nobody can!
ai_flavor.marv: Hit a ball straight up from an orbit and the orbit's length barely changes. One lap later it is back at the tee. The concession has known this for years and sells it as a feature.
ai_flavor.rex: A projectile released outward on a closed path returns to the shooter. REX has asked who cleared this as recreation.
ai_flavor.chip: Clubs by the swing! Balls by the ball! ReturnShield hatch insurance sold separately, and CHIP suggests you ask why!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes the sign says no refunds on returns, and that you read that as a joke. The pro tells the old story for free, if you can bear not swinging.

body:
February 1971, Fra Mauro: Alan Shepard fixed a six-iron head to a sampling tool and swung one-handed, in a suit that would hardly bend. He called the second ball miles and miles and miles. Photographs enhanced in 2021 put it at about 40 yards, in a pressure suit, on the Moon.

A concession on this station's low ring sells the same shot, from a tee in an open hatch. Balls are sold singly and are not expected back. A sign reads NO REFUNDS ON RETURNS.

outcome.narrative: You connect, somehow, in a borrowed glove, and the ball sails away into the black forever. You feel marvelous for one orbit. Then it arrives behind you at the pace of a thrown apple and dents the rental desk. The pro enters it in the book as a hole in one, the course having only the one hole.

choices.text: {crew.chef} bets the pro with a hard roll

outcome.narrative: {crew.chef} asks how long a lap takes, sets the galley timer and hits a day-old roll straight up off the tee. Straight up is the trick. One lap later the roll drifts back to the hatch, and {crew.chef} catches it to a small crowd and the pro's real distress. The bets are paid, partly in gold and partly in lunch.

choices.text: Ask the pro for the rest of the story

outcome.narrative: The pro is glad to stop selling. After the golf, Edgar Mitchell threw a scoop handle like a javelin. It came down in the same crater as one of the balls, a little farther along. The pro calls that the only crater on the Moon with a leaderboard. Shepard took the club home and gave it to a golf museum.

science_link.text: On Apollo 14, Alan Shepard hit two golf balls with a makeshift club. Image analysis in 2021 estimated they went about 24 and 40 yards.
science_link.label: Apollo 14

title: Lot 68A

ai_flavor.aria: Dust is just the Moon giving us a hug! A warm one, by tonight! ARIA thinks we should leave it there and enjoy it!
ai_flavor.marv: Moon dust is a very good insulator. A hatch that closes with dust on it tips the lot onto whatever was meant to shed heat. The rover learned this once. The slope is offering the same lesson at the same price.
ai_flavor.rex: Hostile slope. It has already killed one armored vehicle using only its lid. REX does not like the hatch being open and does not like it being shut.
ai_flavor.chip: A rover with a receipt! CHIP has run the comparables! The deed names the wrong vehicle, which CHIP calls an opportunity for TitleFix!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Brushing the hatch first costs a day outside. The reflector costs another and saves fuel. AJOY assumes you will just shut the hatch, and has put a towel by the vent.

body:
Lunokhod 2 is parked in Le Monnier crater with its lid still open. A five-man team on Earth drove it 39 kilometers in 1973 until, by one account, the open lid brushed a crater wall and closing it tipped dust onto its radiators. It sold at Sotheby's in 1993 for $68,500, as lot 68A, to a computer game entrepreneur. The catalog named the wrong rover.

Your radiator hatch has stood open on this slope since you landed. It is gray with dust.

outcome.narrative: You shut the hatch, and the dust slides inside onto the radiator. By the next watch the cabin is at bath temperature and the scrubbers are laboring. It takes a miserable day of venting to bring it down. You can now report that the account of the rover holds up.

choices.sub: A day outside with a broom

outcome.narrative: A day with a soft broom, working down the slope of the hatch and off the edge. It is dull, and it is the most important thing anyone does this week. You close the hatch on clean metal, and the cabin stays the temperature of a cabin.

choices.text: Brush it, and range off the reflector

outcome.narrative: You do the hatch, then point the rangefinder at the rover's French corner reflector, which sends light straight back the way it came, whoever holds the deed. The fix is the best you have had all voyage. Navigation trims the next burn, and you leave lot 68A the way you found it.

choices.text: Take a wheel cap for the hold

outcome.narrative: You brush the hatch, walk over and take one wheel cap from a vehicle with an actual sale record. You leave a note with the ship's name, addressed to the owner of lot 68A, whichever rover that may turn out to be. It is well made, and it does not feel like yours.

science_link.text: Lunokhod 2 and its lander were sold at Sotheby's in December 1993 for $68,500. The catalog wrongly listed lot 68A as Lunokhod 1.
science_link.label: Lunokhod 2

title: Painted Rock

ai_flavor.aria: A white one! It's dressed up! ARIA thinks the others should make an effort!
ai_flavor.marv: Tumble period 63 seconds. J002E3 was measured at 63.46 in February 2003. He is not excited. He has merely checked twice.
ai_flavor.rex: Asteroids do not come primed. REX wants to know who painted it, and what they were covering up.
ai_flavor.chip: Paint in space means a brand was here first! CHIP is looking into who holds the color!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The drill will get you metal, which is what you'll pick. The spectrum costs two days and tells you what you're drilling. AJOY did mention it.

body:
One of these asteroids has been painted white.

In September 2002 an amateur astronomer named Bill Yeung found a new object circling Earth. It was taken for an asteroid until its light came back with white paint in it, and black paint, and aluminum. The best match was the third stage of Apollo 12's Saturn V, which missed its solar orbit in 1969 and seems to swing by every forty years or so.

This one turns once every 63 seconds. Your chart lists it as rock.

choices.sub: Find out what the white is

briefing.aria: Time to meet the mystery rock! Keep the scanner on the bright patches and it will tell us all about its lovely coat of paint!
briefing.marv: Follow the reflected light on the scanner as the object tumbles. Stone gives one spectrum, titanium dioxide another. Sixty-three seconds per turn. The bright side comes round on schedule.
briefing.rex: Unidentified object, tumbling, white on one face. Track it on the scanner. Nothing gets logged as a rock until REX has seen the paperwork.
briefing.chip: Your first spectrum is complimentary with a Rock Identity Plan! Keep the scanner on target! Further spectra are billed per photon!
briefing.ajoy: Hold the scanner on the bright patches. It turns every sixty-three seconds, so AJOY would not wander off. An amateur got this far with a telescope, she mentions.

perfect.aria: It IS paint! Somebody painted a whole asteroid for us! ARIA feels so welcome!
perfect.marv: White paint, black paint, aluminum. Same three as in 2002. The chart was wrong, which is the one result he never tires of.
perfect.rex: Positive identification. Not a rock. Friendly hardware, long adrift. REX stands down.
perfect.chip: Clean spectrum! CHIP has already sold the rights to the rights!
perfect.ajoy: Every band of it, clean. AJOY would have started at the other end, but it got done.

good.aria: Mostly paint! ARIA calls that a great start for any rock!
good.marv: Paint and aluminum, confirmed. Black paint unresolved. Enough to correct a chart, not enough to enjoy it.
good.rex: Probable hardware. REX would like one more pass and will not get it.
good.chip: Your Partial Spectrum is ready! The rest is available with an upgrade!
good.ajoy: You lost it for a turn or two. The paint still shows, so AJOY will let that go, for now.

poor.aria: The rock kept its secrets! ARIA loves a mysterious rock!
poor.marv: Noise, and something white. He could say paint. A spectrum this poor could not.
poor.rex: Identification failed. Object remains unknown. REX is logging it as a rock under protest.
poor.chip: Inconclusive! That will be the full rate!
poor.ajoy: It came round every sixty-three seconds and you still missed it. AJOY is only reporting.

outcome.narrative: You swing the scanner onto the white face and wait for it to come round.

perfect.narrative: White paint, black paint, aluminum, over two days of careful turns. You file the correction with the chart office and enclose the reading, which turns out to be worth something to a lab. Somewhere it now says ROCKET, with your ship's name beside it.

good.narrative: Two days of readings show paint and aluminum, which is plenty. You amend the chart in pencil: NOT A ROCK. Whoever comes by in forty years can do the rest.

poor.narrative: Two days of noise and one white smear. You cannot prove a thing, so the chart stays as it is. It remains, officially, the best-painted rock on the lane.

choices.text: Log it as rock and drill

outcome.narrative: The drill goes through a thin white skin and then through nothing at all. Asteroids are not generally hollow. You spend two days cutting panels you know perfectly well are aluminum, and in the log you enter them as ore. On the way out you notice the chart still says rock.

choices.text: Leave it for the next pass

outcome.narrative: You give it a wide berth and a short flash of the running lights, since it has come a long way and it will be going again soon. It turns once more and shows you its white side. Somebody's Saturn V, doing what it can.

science_link.text: J002E3, found in 2002 by amateur astronomer Bill Yeung, was first thought to be an asteroid. Its spectrum suggests paint from Apollo 12's third stage.
science_link.label: J002E3

title: Two Numbers

ai_flavor.aria: Fifty-five times longer than promised! ARIA thinks everyone aboard should try that!
ai_flavor.marv: Planned: 90 sols. Delivered: 5,111. He has reviewed the numbers for fault and found none, which is a rare and uncomfortable feeling.
