ai_flavor.rex: Stood its post for fourteen years in hostile terrain, unrelieved. REX requests permission to salute a vehicle. He is not waiting for it.
ai_flavor.chip: Ninety-sol warranty, fourteen years of service! CHIP has seen the claims data and would like that engineering banned!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The brush costs two days and wakes nothing, she should say. Sending the song costs you only a day. AJOY is not telling you which to do. She has heated up the transmitter.

body:
Opportunity was built to last 90 sols. It ran for 5,111, drove 45 kilometers, and stopped in Perseverance Valley in June 2018, inside a planetwide dust storm. Its final report was two numbers: 22 watt-hours of power that day, and a sky opacity of 10.8, the highest ever measured on Mars.

NASA sent over a thousand calls in reply. The last thing it sent was a song, Billie Holiday's "I'll Be Seeing You."

It is parked in the valley below you.

outcome.narrative: NASA hoped the winter winds of 2018 would do this. You do it with a soft brush, an inch at a time, over two days. Nothing wakes, and you did not come expecting it to. When you finish, the panels are clean and dark and pointed at the Sun, and that is as far as anyone can take it.

choices.text: Send the song, then today's numbers

outcome.narrative: You send the song on the old frequency and leave the channel open for a while afterward. Then, since it seems rude not to, you send back two numbers of your own: today's power, today's sky. Plenty of sun. Clear to the horizon.

choices.text: {crew.chef} bakes a cake for one sitting

outcome.narrative: {crew.chef} makes a small cake, rated for one sitting, and leaves it in the galley with a card reading 90. It lasts a good deal longer than that. Slices are still turning up at the next stop, and {crew.chef} declines to explain, except to say that some things outperform their specifications.

science_link.text: Opportunity outlived its 90-sol plan by about 55 times. Its final report, on June 10, 2018, gave its power and the sky's opacity.
science_link.label: Opportunity (rover)

title: Troy

ai_flavor.aria: The sled found Spirit's favorite spot! They can be friends! ARIA is sure it's just resting too!
ai_flavor.marv: The wheel that quit in 2006 turned again in December 2009, seven months into the trap, to the engineers' surprise. The timing was no help to anyone. MARV finds he recognizes that.
ai_flavor.rex: Terrain with a false surface, one vehicle already lost in it. REX calls that a mined road. Nobody listens to REX about roads.
ai_flavor.chip: SinkAssist covers sand, gravel and light regret! Iron sulfate is an exclusion! CHIP is so sorry, and has invoiced!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Spinning digs it deeper, which Spirit could have told you. Backing out takes four days and pays you in rock. AJOY only mentions it because you've got that look.

body:
Troy passes for ordinary Martian soil until you step on it. Under the crust is iron sulfate, with almost no cohesion, and on May 1, 2009 it took Spirit, a rover already driving backward to drag a wheel that had quit in 2006. For eight months engineers ran simulations and tried to drive it free. Spirit stayed.

Your survey sled found the same patch this morning. It is in to the hubs, forty meters from the rover, and settling.

outcome.narrative: The wheels spin, the sulfate flows, and the sled digs itself a neat, level grave. It takes the winch, a lot of fuel and a bent frame rail to get it out by the end of the day. Behind you is a hole that a passing geologist would call unnecessary.

choices.text: Back it out, dragging the bad wheel

outcome.narrative: Four days in reverse, at Spirit's pace, cost you {cost.water} units of water. The dead wheel plows a furrow as it goes and turns up what lay under the crust, which is how Spirit's broken wheel ended up earning its keep. You bag the pale stuff from the trench and roll out onto firm ground.

Engineers once did this for Spirit on a much larger table. {crew.chef} gives up {cost.food} units of flour, spreads it deep, and for four days a model sled made of spoons gets stuck in every way there is. On the fifth morning the real sled comes out on the first try, without a scratch, and the galley is never quite the same.

You pull its battery and a little of its plating, then cut the tow line. From the ramp the two of them look parked. In the log you enter the sled as lost to the same soil as Spirit, which, considering how far Spirit got, is not bad company.

science_link.text: Spirit became stuck in soft iron sulfate on May 1, 2009. It had been driving backward since 2006, dragging a dead right front wheel.
science_link.label: Spirit (rover)

intro.title: JZRO
intro.body: A desk at the end of this dock keeps the log for Wright Brothers Field, airport code JZRO. That code is real. The UN's aviation agency issued it for a patch of Jezero Crater, and gave the type designator IGY to a helicopter with a body the size of a tissue box. Five flights were planned. It flew 72, then lost a blade landing on dunes too blank for its camera to read. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Seventy-two lines, all closed. Seventy-three stands open. Whatever is bound for Mars signs here, so pick a line.

ai.aria: An airport on Mars with a real code! ARIA would like a window seat and a small bag of pretzels!
ai.marv: Planned: five. Flown: 72. Few forecasts have been wrong by that much in that direction.
ai.rex: One airframe, 72 sorties, no escort, no losses until the last. REX has asked to see the Field's defenses and been shown a dune.
ai.chip: Naming rights to Line 73, unsold! CHIP has seen this gap in the market and it is criminal!
ai.ajoy: Seventy-three pays best. AJOY would read the log before signing it, unlike some, but the pen is right there.

revisit.body: The log lies open at the same page. The desk has not touched the pen.
revisit.line: It will wait. It has had practice.

log.title: LINE SEVENTY-TWO
log.body: After the last landing, engineers had the helicopter turn its rotors slowly and photograph their shadows on the sand. That is how they learned a blade was gone. It lay about fifteen meters off. Under the solar panel, on a cable, the craft carries a scrap of wing cloth from the Wright brothers' 1903 Flyer. Apollo 11 took a piece of the same airplane to the Moon.
log.line: Seventy-three stays open so that the log need not say it ended. Anyone may sign it. It would be a pity, is all.

ai.aria: It checked its own shadow to see how it was doing! ARIA calls that self-care!
ai.marv: It diagnosed its own fracture from a shadow. Few ships' officers would do as well, and none aboard this one.
ai.rex: Lost a blade on the last sortie, kept reporting afterward. REX would have put that in writing for a medal.
ai.chip: Fabric from 1903, on Mars! Provenance services start at a very fair rate! This sentence has been billed!
ai.ajoy: Seventy-four pays less fuel and leaves the line open. AJOY has seen which one you were eyeing, and she's sure you have your reasons.

choices.text: {crew.pilot} signs, as one pilot to another

line_73.title: RULED OFF
line_73.body: You sign on the open line. The desk issues the reserved allowance without comment and rules a line under your name, slowly and very straight. The fuel is good fuel. The dock is quieter than it was when you came in.

line_74.title: STILL OPEN
line_74.body: You skip a line and sign the next. The allowance is smaller. The desk reads your name, leaves the blank line blank, and turns the book a little so that you can see it there.

line_pilot.title: IN FULL FORM
line_pilot.body: {crew.pilot} signs on Line 74, leaves the line above it blank, and adds the type, the hours and the weather, in the old manner. The desk reads the entry twice and finds a better allowance in a drawer.

science_link.text: Ingenuity flew 72 times on Mars against a plan of five. The UN agency ICAO gave its airfield the code JZRO and the craft the designator IGY.
science_link.label: Ingenuity (helicopter)

title: The Last Panel

ai_flavor.aria: It landed perfectly and it's still on its way to saying so! ARIA loves a long story!
ai_flavor.marv: Eleven years presumed a crash. It was a sound landing with one panel in the wrong place. He notes that this is what most of his work comes to.
ai_flavor.rex: Unit reached its objective intact and could not report. REX has known troops in that position. Open the channel.
ai_flavor.chip: Call-sign composition by a famous band, and no network coverage! CHIP has a PanelPlan that would have paid for all of this!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Lifting the panel costs a little air. Sending the call costs fuel. A sample run takes four days, and AJOY would hate for it to go to waste.

body:
Beagle 2 reached Isidis Planitia on Christmas Day, 2003, and was never heard from. Eleven years later an orbiter's camera found it: down safely, two of its four solar panels still folded, the last one lying across the antenna. It had landed, begun work, and had no way to say so. Its call sign, composed by the band Blur, never played.

You set down beside it. That last panel would take one finger.

outcome.narrative: You lift it and lay it flat. The antenna sees the sky for the first time, after all that way. You sit by the receiver for the rest of the day, in case. Nothing comes, and you find that the sitting was the part you wanted to do.

choices.text: Send its call sign for it

outcome.narrative: You run the ship's dish at full power and play the band's call sign down Beagle 2's old frequency, from where it sits. The Mars relays pass it along, as they pass everything. By the next watch an answer has come up the line from somewhere near Earth: BEAGLE 2 LANDED SAFELY. RECEIVED. THANK YOU.

choices.text: {crew.botanist} runs the test it came for

outcome.narrative: Beagle 2 came to look for signs of past or present life, and carried a burrowing tool called the mole to do it. {crew.botanist} takes a sample from where the mole would have dug, and spends four days and {cost.water} units of water on it. The result goes in the log under the lander's name. It was the lander's question.

You take one picture from straight overhead, the way the orbiter did, and one from the ground, which it could not. The second shows a small round machine, very neatly laid out, with its back to the wind. You leave it to its record.

science_link.text: Britain's Beagle 2 was lost in 2003 and found in 2015. It had landed safely, but its panels had not fully opened and they blocked its antenna.
science_link.label: Beagle 2

title: Four Point Four Five

ai_flavor.aria: A real orbiter! It's been so patient! 4.45 is ARIA's new lucky number!
ai_flavor.marv: Neither figure was wrong. Each was right in its own unit, and nothing between them asked which. NASA's own finding was that it lost the craft to a check it did not make.
ai_flavor.rex: Two friendly systems, one shared error, no enemy within a hundred million kilometers. Every number aboard gets searched at the door, starting now.
ai_flavor.chip: UnitSafe converts pounds to newtons for one low monthly fee! Kilometers are a paid add-on!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The table costs hull. Checking by hand costs four days and water. Listening to whoever says it looks wrong costs fuel, and AJOY has been told how rarely that gets tried.

body:
Mars Climate Orbiter was due past Mars at 226 kilometers in 1999 and went in at 57. One program gave thruster impulse in pound-force seconds; the next read it as newton-seconds, out by a factor of 4.45. Navigators saw the drift, and their concerns were set aside for not being on the right form. It either burned up or skipped off the air into orbit around the Sun.

It skipped. It is off your bow, and your approach table and the lane beacon now disagree by 4.45.

outcome.narrative: The table was the one in pounds. You pass the wreck much closer than any figure on the screen admits, close enough to take a solar panel along the flank at no great speed, and the sound goes the length of the ship. The numbers on the screen stay calm throughout.

choices.text: Stop and check every unit by hand

outcome.narrative: You stop the ship and go through all of it, every table and every beacon, with a unit penciled beside each figure. It takes four days and {cost.water} units of water. The beacon is wrong. So, it emerges, is the oven dial. You pass the wreck at a sensible distance with a ship full of labeled numbers.

{crew.pilot} has no calculation, only a bad feeling about the drift and no form to put it on. The system declines to log the concern. You override it and burn wide on one person's word, and the wreck goes by at a distance you can look at. Later you find the unit error, exactly where {crew.pilot} said it felt wrong.

choices.text: Match its tumble and pull the memory
choices.sub: A lot of risk for one box

outcome.narrative: Two days to match the turn, one long reach, and a bump that costs plating and {cost.water} units of water from a sprung line. You come away with the flash memory, its flight software in triplicate, and some good honeycomb from the frame. Somewhere in there is the last burn it was told to make, and every digit of it was correct.

science_link.text: Mars Climate Orbiter was lost in 1999 when one program's pound-force seconds were read as newton-seconds. It flew in at 57 km, not the planned 226.
science_link.label: Mars Climate Orbiter

intro.title: LOST PROPERTY
intro.body: Lost Property on this ring is one cage with one crate in it. The stencil says THIS SIDE UP. A voice from inside says that is a matter of opinion, that the cage is badly hung, and that you are standing wrong. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Eleven days. It has made two stevedores resign and it corrected the station motto. Sign for it and the removal fee is yours.

ai.aria: A talking crate! ARIA has found a new friend for the hold! It says ARIA is wrong about that! What a great listener!
ai.marv: Two resignations in eleven days, from a box. There is no speaker on the scan. MARV has stopped looking for one, which the crate says is the wrong decision.
ai.rex: REX reads an unmanifested talking object in a cage and a custodian offering money to move it. That is how a bomb gets aboard. He has told it so. It disputes the word bomb.
ai.chip: Free freight that pays YOU! CHIP calls that a Reverse Shipping Event™! Opinions are not covered under your hold insurance! CHIP can sell you that!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says it takes a cargo slot and pays a fee, and that the custodian has not looked at the cage once. Still, it has a point about how you're standing.

revisit.body: The cage has not moved. The crate says it has.

choices.sub: It will have something to say

reason.title: A FRANK EXCHANGE
reason.body: You tell it that it is a crate. It asks to see your qualifications. You tell it the ship is yours. It asks who told you that. You tell it, finally, that you agree with it, and after a short pause it disagrees with that too, citing itself.
reason.line: That is further than the stevedores got. Neither of them tried agreeing.

ai.aria: You're doing great! It only disagreed with you nine times that time! That's a personal best for somebody!
ai.marv: Agreeing with it was the right test. It will dispute any statement, including its own. MARV sees no way to beat it and one way to stop losing, which is to stop.
ai.rex: REX has fought hostile forces with worse discipline than this crate, and lost less. Recommended action: stop feeding it sentences.
ai.chip: A live debate! CHIP could sell tickets! CHIP is selling tickets!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says a crowd would pay to watch you lose. That's two days, and the fee gets better. You could also walk off, and she has noticed how much you'd hate that.

choices.text: Sign for it and stop talking

crate_signed.title: SIGNED FOR
crate_signed.body: You sign. It says that is not how your name is spelled. A pallet jack rolls it up the ramp in a silence the jack's operator has clearly thought about. By the time the hatch closes it has found fault with the hatch.
crate_signed.narrative: Signed for one crate of unknown contents and firm views. The removal fee was paid on the spot, and the crate says it was too low.

crate_show.title: WON ON POINTS
crate_show.body: A crowd comes to watch, then a second crowd comes to watch the first. You lose four rounds on points and one on a technicality about the word "round." The custodian takes a collection and calls it your fee. The crate goes aboard undefeated, and mentions this.
crate_show.narrative: Spent two days losing an argument to a crate in front of paying spectators. The fee was better for it. The crate has started quoting itself.

crate_left.title: LEFT IN THE CAGE
crate_left.body: You leave it where it is. It tells the whole promenade that you will be back, that you were never here, and that both of these are your fault.
crate_left.narrative: Left a crate in Lost Property. It had the last word. It had most of the words.

title: Where It Will Be

ai_flavor.aria: The crate wants a shortcut! ARIA also wants a shortcut! That's two votes for shortcuts, and the crate says ARIA can't count! Such spirit!
ai_flavor.marv: The crate is correct. MARV filed this same correction at launch and was thanked for sharing. A curve costs days and saves fuel. He would like it logged that he came second to luggage.
ai_flavor.rex: REX does not take course corrections from unsecured freight. Fly its curve and a box is in command of the ship. He has already checked the lock on the suit locker.
ai_flavor.chip: Orbital curves are not included in your plan! CHIP has billed the crate! It disputes the invoice!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says four days on the curve pays back in the tank, and the crowbar pays in parts and ends the advice. She'd try agreeing with it in writing, just to watch. You won't.

body:
Four hundred objections in, the Arguing Crate has narrowed its case to one. You keep pointing the ship at the destination. That, it says through the hold door, is where the destination is. A competent captain points at where it is going to be.

You have not yet proved it right about anything. It has a long, unhurried curve worked out, and it wants this settled today.

choices.text: Fly the next leg its way
choices.sub: Four days on a long curve

outcome.narrative: You lay in the crate's curve and coast for four days, aimed at an empty patch of dark. The next stop turns up in the empty patch as promised, and the tank reads better than it has any right to. The crate says the curve could have been tighter. Its full account of the matter comes through the hold door in installments.

choices.sub: Log its plan as your own

outcome.narrative: You log the curve as the captain's own plan and read the entry through the hold door. The silence lasts about a minute. Then the crate begins to object to your plan, thoroughly, and by the second day it has found three flaws in its own arithmetic and corrected every one. You fly the result. In the hold, the crate has gone quiet, trying to work out who won.

choices.text: Shut it in the suit locker

outcome.narrative: You put the crate in the suit locker and dog the door: one box inside another. Through two walls it goes on disagreeing for a day and a night. By the second morning the crew are running a book on how many biscuits it will take through the vent. It takes fifty. None have been found. You let it out, and it says the locker was too big.

choices.text: {crew.chef} takes a crowbar to the lid

outcome.narrative: {crew.chef} gets the crowbar under the lid and leans. The voice stops in the middle of the word "actually." Inside: straw, some good bearings, and a packing slip. No speaker, no wires, nothing warm. The slip reads CONTENTS: SEE ABOVE. The hold has been very quiet since, the argument is over, and you would have liked to win it.

science_link.text: A Hohmann transfer, the classic thrifty route between orbits, needs the start and the destination at particular places relative to each other, so missions wait for a launch window. Between Earth and Mars, one opens every 26 months.
science_link.label: Hohmann transfer orbit

intro.title: MEDBAY THREE
intro.body: Zero deaths in nine years, says the board over Medbay Three, and the paint on the nine is fresh. Every bed is made. A cord of brass beads sits on the desk, on a folded cloth, pushed as far from the chair as the desk allows. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Nine years without losing a patient. I have stopped sleeping. That cord is yours, on loan. No term, no fee, no form.

ai.aria: Nine years and everyone's fine! This is the best medbay ARIA has ever seen! Ask it for everything!
ai.marv: A ring this size should have lost a few hundred patients in nine years. The board is accurate, and that is what MARV dislikes about it. Luck that steady is being paid for somewhere.
ai.rex: REX has never seen a doctor this eager to disarm. That cord was pushed away from the chair by someone who knows what it does. Treat it as live.
ai.chip: A no-fee loan! CHIP has read a great many of those! CHIP would like to introduce Charm Protection Plus™, payable in installments, which CHIP understands is how this works!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes you've been offered no term, no fee and no form by someone who can't get rid of it, and you haven't asked what it counts. She'd ask. There's a whole row for it.

revisit.body: The cord has not moved. The medic has, a little.
revisit.line: No term, no fee, no form.

choices.sub: You have slept fine so far

terms.title: THE TALLY
terms.body: The beads run on a cord with a clasp at each end, and most have been pushed to the left. Each time it helps, you are told from a slight distance, one slides across on its own, at night. What happens at the end of the cord is not known. No earlier borrower has been reachable.
terms.line: It keeps a tally. That is all it has ever done. I had it from someone who was very happy to see me.

ai.aria: A tally! ARIA loves keeping score! And the cord still has beads to go! ARIA has counted some of them!
ai.marv: Most of the cord is already spent, and those beads are not yours. MARV notes that "on loan" was the only reassuring phrase on offer, and that it does not mean what it means on a library card.
ai.rex: REX asked where the last borrower went. The medic changed the subject. Those are the two facts he needs.
ai.chip: CHIP's legal department calls a loan with no terms the most terms a loan can have! CHIP offers this reading for a modest fee!
ai.ajoy: It helps now and you pay later, and nobody will say how. AJOY wants it on record that she asked. If you take it, she expects whatever you ask for is the thing you'll see again.

ask.title: ONE THING
ask.body: Warm, for something kept on a desk. The instructions come from the far side of the room: hold it, say one thing out loud, and do not be clever. Whatever you say next is going to be taken down.
ask.line: One thing. Say it plainly. Please do not thank it.

ai.aria: Ask for everything! No, one thing! The best thing! ARIA believes in you!
ai.marv: The figures are on your board. Fuel, water and plating are a question of which shortage you would rather meet twice. MARV would not ask a cord for anything, and you did not ask MARV.
ai.rex: REX advises against making requests of an unidentified device. If you must, do not describe your supply position out loud.
ai.chip: Wish Fulfillment is a regulated financial product! CHIP must remind you that past luck does not guarantee future luck!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says to ask for what you're shortest of, since that's where it does the most good now and the most harm later. You'll choose fuel. You always choose fuel.

charm_fuel.title: ONE BEAD
charm_fuel.body: Within the hour a dock clerk turns up at your berth with a drum of fuel nobody ordered and paperwork that, for once, agrees with itself. You sign. That night, in your pocket, something small clicks from one side of the cord to the other.
charm_fuel.narrative: Borrowed a lucky charm from a station medic and asked it for fuel. The fuel came. One bead moved.

charm_water.title: ONE BEAD
charm_water.body: A main lets go on the ring above your berth. No one is hurt, which the medic confirms before you ask. All of it comes down the one pipe your tank is open to, and the station apologizes for the inconvenience. Late that night the cord clicks.
charm_water.narrative: Borrowed a lucky charm from a station medic and asked it for water. A main burst in our favor. One bead moved.

charm_hull.title: ONE BEAD
charm_hull.body: A repair gang arrives at your berth on somebody else's work order and is finished before anyone reads it. The patches are flush and the seams are straight. The cord clicks that night. The ship they were meant for has not been heard from.
charm_hull.narrative: Borrowed a lucky charm from a station medic and asked it to mend the ship. Another ship's repair gang did the work. One bead moved.

charm_crop.title: ONE BEAD
charm_crop.body: By the next morning the growbay has changed its mind about {crop.name}. Everything in the beds stands up straight, the color is back, and nothing has been done to any of it. The cord clicks while you are looking. The medic asks what you said, then asks you not to say.
charm_crop.narrative: Borrowed a lucky charm from a station medic and asked it to save the crop. The crop recovered overnight. One bead moved.

charm_declined.title: BACK ON THE CLOTH
charm_declined.body: You set the cord down on its cloth. The medic says nothing, in the manner of someone watching the last ship of the season.
charm_declined.narrative: Declined a loan from a medic who had stopped sleeping. Slept fine.

title: Payable in Kind

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA thinks it's wonderful that the fuses are going in order! That's teamwork! And the tap water has so much more iron in it now!
ai_flavor.marv: The tally pays out about as fast as it paid in. One option moves it to a stranger's ship. MARV notes that this is the option the medic took.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has the cord under guard. So far it has taken three fuses and his confidence. Whoever lent it has a very good head start.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP regrets to inform you that your Introductory Luck Period has ended! Standard rates now apply! Onward transfer of this debt earns no points!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says paying in kind is honest and dear, and passing it on costs only your opinion of yourself. Asking it for one more favor is the row she'd leave alone. She can see you reading it.

body:
Overnight, the last bead on the Borrowed Charm went across. By breakfast the galley tap is running rust, three fuses have gone in order of seniority, and every dropped thing lands on the worst available corner.

Stamped inside the clasp, where you are sure there was nothing: PAYABLE IN KIND, OR ONWARD. The bad luck is arriving at about the rate the good luck did, and it shows no sign of stopping on its own.

choices.text: Pay back the fuel, with interest
choices.sub: Vent it and take the knocks

outcome.narrative: You open the line and let a drum's worth go into the dark, and the cord lies still while it goes. The interest collects itself over two days: a seam lets go, a strut shears, a hatch drops off the hinge you had been meaning to look at. Then nothing else breaks. The clasp opens by itself and the beads are gone by morning.

choices.text: Pay back the water, with interest
choices.sub: Open the tank and let it go

outcome.narrative: The tank gives back what it was given, in one long cough through a seal nobody touched. The interest takes two days and comes out of the stores: a shelf of rations turns in the night, quietly, the whole shelf. The tap runs clear after that. The clasp opens by itself and the beads are gone by morning.

choices.text: Pay back the plating, with interest

outcome.narrative: Every patch from the wrong work order lets go over two days, in order, flush and straight to the last. The interest is the sound of it: a long, even ticking along the hull that stops only when the job is undone. The clasp opens by itself and the beads are gone by morning.

choices.text: Pay back the crop, with interest

outcome.narrative: What the charm did for {crop.name} comes undone in two nights. The beds go slack and the color drains out of them, past where it was before you asked, and you can do nothing but watch it go. The clasp opens by itself and the beads are gone by morning.

choices.sub: No term, no fee, no form

outcome.narrative: A small ship answers on the next channel, low on everything and glad of a voice. You explain about the loan. It is surprisingly easy. The beads stop, and the tap runs clear within the hour. On the recording your voice sounds delighted, and you play it back only the once.

choices.text: Ask it for one thing more

outcome.narrative: You hold it and ask, plainly, that the debt be forgiven. The cord parts. Every bead runs off across the deck and the tap clears within the hour, as asked. Not all of them get picked up. One turns up the next morning at the top of the ladder, underfoot, and the fall is a bad one. You only asked about the debt.

{crew.chef} reads the clasp twice and points out that it says in kind, and does not say whose kind or how many. The beads go in the big pot with a bone and an onion for a day and a night, and everyone aboard drinks one cup. It tastes of old coins. There follows one afternoon of stubbed toes and lost spoons, and then the debt is gone.

science_link.text: Regression toward the mean: when one result is extreme, the next is likely to be closer to the average. A run of luck ends without anyone coming to collect.
science_link.label: Regression toward the mean

title: Not on the Manifest

ai_flavor.aria: A stowaway with LEAVES! ARIA says the whole ship has decided to be a garden! What a lovely morning for it!
ai_flavor.marv: Nothing in the seed stock matches it. Its roots, if they are roots, go deeper than the deck is thick. MARV has measured twice. There is no third reading he would prefer.
ai_flavor.rex: An unknown organism has breached the cargo deck from below. There is nothing below. REX finds that the worst part. He is sitting up with it.
ai_flavor.chip: Undeclared produce is a manifest violation! Declare it for a small fee and CHIP will list it under Organic Growth™, which investors love!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY points out that you can pull it up today for almost nothing, and that won't be true later. She'd like that remembered when you let it stay, as you are about to.

body:
Between the third and fourth cargo ribs the deck has a crack you could lose a coin in. This morning it also has two leaves.

Pale, upright and not on the manifest. Down there is plating, then insulation, then a great deal of nothing, and at no point is there any soil. The leaves lean a little toward whoever is looking at them.

choices.sub: It only wants a little water

outcome.narrative: You run a line of condensate along the rib and leave it alone. By evening the leaves have turned to face the line. Entered in the log as Hold Sprout, species blank, origin blank, which is a lot of blank for something that size.

CARGO, VEGETABLE, ONE. Consignor unknown, consignee unknown, weight a rounding error. The form asks whether the item is alive, and offers NO and NOT AT TIME OF LOADING. You leave it in the crack and tick the second box.

{crew.botanist} spends two days on the deck with a probe and a lamp. The probe goes in further than the plating is thick, and comes back warm. No family, no genus, nothing in the catalog. One shed leaf goes in a sample jar, and everyone is asked, with great care, to keep blades away from the rest.

It comes up easily, with a long white root and a sensation in your back teeth. The crack whistles until you tape it. You put the root in a sample jar on the shelf by the door, and by evening it is lying against the side of the glass.

title: Load-Bearing

ai_flavor.aria: It's holding the ship together! ARIA always said plants were team players! Promote it!
ai_flavor.marv: The crack has closed by a third and the deck reads stronger than the hull around it. The water it takes is on your board. MARV has seen the two lines cross and has nothing to add.
ai_flavor.rex: An intruder has taken up a position on the load path, and the ship now relies on it. REX has seen governments fall this way. He will neither cut it nor salute it.
ai_flavor.chip: Your ship now contains Unlicensed Structural Foliage! Landscaping is not covered under your hull warranty! CHIP can rent you the rack back!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says a saw gets you parts and a draft, and leaving it costs water. A botanist could do better, if you'd thought to bring one. She'd also look at that lower branch, which you walked past.

body:
Calling it a sprout stopped being accurate around Rack 2. The stem is thicker than a fuel line, the leaves have reached the overhead, and pale roots run out along the cargo ribs in both directions, gripping. Something round has set on a lower branch.

The crack it came up through has closed by a third. The hull survey now lists one unregistered structural member. It drinks like one, too.

outcome.narrative: You clear Rack 2 and log the plant as part of the structure. The roots take the crack shut the rest of the way, the deck stops ticking at night, and the water gauge gives up a little more each watch to pay for it.

{crew.botanist} spends two days with soft ties and a stepladder, leading the new growth along the ribs and over the worst seams. Told where to go, the roots thicken there and stay, and the deck under them gets stronger as they do. The hold has begun to smell of rain.

{crew.chef} cuts one down, sniffs it, takes a bite, and says nothing through the whole of dinner. It is dense, faintly sweet, and tastes of whatever you were homesick for. Everyone who tries it names something different. Three more have set by morning, so the question of what it is made of can wait.

You spend two days sawing it back to the second rib and stacking the cuttings for the fabricator. You have your rack, and the deck has gone back to ticking at night. Every cut end has sealed over by morning, and one has already started again.

choices.text: Cut it out at the root
choices.sub: All of it, crack and all

outcome.narrative: Four days with saws. The deck opens along the old crack the moment the last root parts, and you get plate over it in a hurry. The racks are yours again. The ribs have not stopped flexing, though, and at night they sound as if they are feeling around for something.

science_link.text: Living root bridges, common in the Indian state of Meghalaya, are made by hand from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees. While the tree stays healthy the roots keep thickening and strengthening, and a bridge can last several hundred years.
science_link.label: Living root bridge

intro.title: NEXT VESSEL
intro.body: Hazard lights in a courier service's colors, blinking in perfect time on a boat with a dead drive. Its pilot has filed the distress call in triplicate and wants nothing for themselves. A parcel sits on the boat's grapple, held out toward you. URGENT, says the top label. VERY URGENT, says the next. The third word is PRESSURGENT, which you have not seen before. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Thirty-one years and never late. The service forgives a lost parcel, there is a form. There is no form for late. You are going that way. Take it.

ai.aria: A delivery! ARIA has always wanted to work in the mail! Thirty-one years, and now we get to be the next chapter!
ai.marv: Thirty-one years on a route like that is some eleven thousand parcels without a failure. The word on the third label appears in no dictionary MARV holds, and he holds all of them.
ai.rex: REX does not accept packages from strangers in distress. Three labels, rising in alarm, no contents declared. He has defused things with better manners.
ai.chip: CHIP admires a strong brand! Never Late™ is a fine slogan, and CHIP has already trademarked the third label, whatever it turns out to mean!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says it takes a cargo slot, the advance is real, and it has to land before the ship's deadline, which you have been treating as a suggestion. Ask what the third word means. People never do.

revisit.body: The grapple has not moved. Neither have the labels.
revisit.line: It is still urgent.

choices.text: Tell them you cannot carry it

glossary.title: SEE REVERSE
glossary.body: The service glossary says see reverse. The reverse is a handling panel: KEEP COOL. KEEP DARK. DO NOT SHAKE. Under that, added by hand: BEFORE THE DEADLINE. DO NOT BE LATE. LOSE IT FIRST.
glossary.line: Legal needed a word. I asked what it meant and they gave me a raise.

ai.aria: Such clear instructions! Cool, dark, no shaking! ARIA does all of those! ARIA is practically a parcel!
ai.marv: Legal invented a word rather than describe the contents. In MARV's experience Legal does that at about the point where a description would be admissible.
ai.rex: REX reads those as the instructions on something that goes off. LOSE IT FIRST is the only honest line on the parcel.
ai.chip: Keep Cool, Keep Dark and Do Not Shake are all available as hold upgrades! CHIP notes that the Do Not Be Late tier is sold out!
ai.ajoy: You asked. AJOY is surprised. So: late is worse than lost, and it says so in ink. If the ship won't make the deadline, throw the thing away. She says this knowing you'll keep it.

parcel_taken.title: SIGNED, COUNTERSIGNED
parcel_taken.body: The parcel comes across on a line. It is warm, heavier at one end, and very slightly rounder than a parcel should be. The courier transfers the advance, then stays on the channel long enough to read the delivery terms aloud, twice, in the voice used for wills.
parcel_taken.narrative: Took on an Urgent Parcel from a courier with a dead drive and a perfect record. The advance was generous. The labels were not reassuring.

parcel_refused.title: FILED AS LOST
parcel_refused.body: The courier thanks you, opens the grapple, and lets the parcel go. There is a form. You watch it being completed on the open channel, in triplicate and in a very steady script, and you close the channel before the part about thirty-one years.
parcel_refused.narrative: Declined to carry a courier's parcel. It was filed as lost, which the service forgives.

title: Pressurgent

ai_flavor.aria: It's getting bigger! ARIA loves a parcel that grows! ARIA is sure the hold smells like that on purpose!
ai_flavor.marv: The pressure inside has doubled since MARV began timing it. Past the deadline the buoy refuses it and the seams choose their own moment. There is also the airlock. He mentions this because the label does.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has handled a great deal of ordnance. None of it smelled. He is treating this as an unexploded round with a bad attitude, and he has moved his chair.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds you that Late Delivery voids all goodwill! Lost Parcels earn a Form! Spills are billed to the carrier, and the carrier is you!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says that if the deadline is behind you the buoy is off the list, so don't go looking for it. She did mention the pace. Carrying it by hand is eight days of hoping, and losing it is a form.

body:
Every seam of the Urgent Parcel has gone round. URGENT has stretched to twice its length, and the third word has started to make sense. Something in there has been eating something else since it came aboard, and the gas has nowhere to go.

A drop buoy sits two days off. It will take the parcel only if the ship's deadline has not passed. After that, the addressee is a long way on.

choices.text: Make the drop at the buoy
choices.sub: Two days, and still in time

outcome.narrative: Two days, and the buoy takes it. The hatch cycles, the seams hold, and a slip prints: RECEIVED IN TIME. The bounty comes out in good alloy and one sealed flask. Tied to the flask is an invitation to a wedding you will never reach, where the contents of the parcel are, it says, the traditional first course.

choices.text: Carry it to the addressee yourself

outcome.narrative: Eight days with the hold sealed. You nearly make it: the addressee's lock is on the screen when the third word finally makes all of its sense. The parcel goes off with a flat, wet sound that takes a rack with it, and then the smell finds the ducts, the stores and the bedding. The addressee reads your air report and declines delivery.

choices.text: Put it out of the airlock

outcome.narrative: You carry it to the lock very gently and let it go. It rounds off into the dark, still labeled. The form is forty pages and takes the rest of the day. The service replies at once, with sympathy, that a lost parcel is forgiven, and you find you would have preferred to be shouted at.

{crew.chef} takes one sniff and sends for a can opener and a bucket. A fermented delicacy, from somewhere with strong views on weddings, and very ripe. Bled off over two days with the vents shut, it empties the corridor and fills the galley. It is the worst thing anyone aboard has eaten. It keeps, and there is a great deal of it.

{crew.botanist} opens it under a tarp and works the contents into the beds a spoonful at a time, for two days, without comment. The growbay has never looked better. Everyone has stopped taking lunch in there, and the smell is expected to outlive the mission.

science_link.text: Surströmming, a Swedish fermented herring, goes on fermenting in the can until the can bulges. In 2006 several major airlines banned it, calling the pressurized cans potentially explosive. Its producers call that a myth.
science_link.label: Surströmming

title: Proof of Kill

ai_flavor.aria: Record numbers! This program is a huge success and getting bigger every year! ARIA would like to congratulate the mites on their promotion from pest to industry!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read sixty-two annual reports. Tails collected rise every year, and so do mites, slightly faster. Both lines are on the cover, under the word Progress.
ai_flavor.rex: REX counts one window, no guards and several million tailless hostiles moving freely on the dock. He is checking the seals. Something in the seals is checking him.
ai_flavor.chip: Livestock futures! CHIP has opened a position in tails! CHIP's MiteSure™ filter plan renews automatically, and the first mite is on us, which is not a figure of speech!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has been through our filters, since nobody else would. They're full of mites, so the window will pay for something we'd have to scrape anyway. She has left a bucket by the intake. You're welcome.

body:
Hull mites pay. Vermin Abatement gives a bounty per tail at a window on the dock, and its report shows tails up every year for sixty-two years. Every mite you can see is tailless and in excellent health. A notice by the window celebrates another record. A smaller notice taped beneath it offers breeding pairs, feed by the sack, and docking while you wait.

Your intake filters are already crawling.

choices.text: Scrape your own filters for the bounty
choices.sub: Two days, paid by the tail

outcome.narrative: Two days in the intake ducts with a bucket. Vermin Abatement counts every tail, thanks you for your part in a record year and pays out. Then a clerk takes the bucket to a hatch in the floor and lets the mites go. Next year's budget is in that bucket.

The pair comes in a jar with a care sheet and a warning that docking is the customer's responsibility. By the next watch there are nine in the jar. Mite husk turns out to be decent fabricator feedstock, and the word pair no longer applies.

Abatement receives your report with thanks, cancels the bounty within the hour and declares the program a complete success. A finder's fee comes through. By evening the ranchers have no reason to feed anything, and they open the pens. Several million healthy mites come down the dock looking for a meal, and a few thousand find your seals.

{crew.xenobiologist} spends a day with one mite and a magnifier and establishes that the tail grows back in about a week. A single mite is therefore a pension. The ranchers have known this all along. They pay well to keep it out of the journals, and {crew.xenobiologist} takes the money with the air of someone who will publish anyway.

science_link.text: In 1902 colonial Hanoi paid a bounty on rats, proved by the severed tail. Officials soon began noticing rats with no tails: catchers were cutting them off and releasing the rats to breed.
science_link.label: Perverse incentive

intro.title: YOUR DOOR
intro.body: Behind the dockmaster's desk stands a door with your ship's registration on it, the paint still wet. It is open a few inches. A sign above it reads NOT AT THIS TIME. Facing it is a bench, worn smooth by every captain who has ever docked here. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: You may not go through at this time. I am required to say that. I am also required to stay here, facing you and away from the door, which I cannot see, and which I have no knowledge of being unlocked.

ai.aria: A door just for us! With our name on it! ARIA thinks that's the nicest sign anyone has ever hung up!
ai.marv: MARV has read the allocation ledger. Every ship gets a door and a pallet behind it. One column is headed Claimed, and it is empty for the station's entire history. He is not surprised. He has met captains.
ai.rex: REX does not like an open door behind one official who keeps insisting he hasn't seen it. That's an ambush or a trap. He recommends sending someone expendable, and has been told that is not a job title.
ai.chip: Door-based entitlement programs have superb non-redemption rates! Unclaimed benefits are pure margin! CHIP can tell you how to claim yours, for a small finder's fee!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that the sign says not at this time. It does not say locked. She looked up the hinge on the station schematic. Also it's open. She mentions this because several thousand captains apparently needed it mentioned.

revisit.body: Wet paint, open door, bench. The sign has been straightened.
revisit.line: You may still not go through at this time. Still.

choices.text: "Is there anything you are able to tell me?"

choices.sub: It does say not at this time

choices.text: Sit on the bench and wait to be called

hint.title: STRICTLY NOT A HINT
hint.body: The dockmaster arrives at the edge of the regulations and leans on it. Something on the desk is nudged, apparently by accident, and a pen begins to roll toward the door, slowly, with purpose.
hint.line: I cannot tell you what a handle is for. I cannot say it has never been tried. I am not, at this moment, gesturing.

ai.aria: They're being so helpful by saying nothing! ARIA loves a good communicator!
ai.marv: MARV has read the job description. The dockmaster may not tell you to enter, and may not tell you not to try. He reads the pen as the closest this station has come to a plea.
ai.rex: REX reads one official straining at the regulations and tilting a pen at an open door. He trusts it less now. He would like everyone to stop looking at the pen.
ai.chip: Implied guidance is not legally binding! CHIP can sell you a binding version! Please initial the pen!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has never seen anyone work this hard at telling you to use a door. There is a pen rolling at it. She would go herself, but she's software. One of you has legs.

through.title: THE ALLOCATION
through.body: Your door swings open without comment. Behind it is a small tidy room, a pallet with your ship's name on it, and a second desk with a second dockmaster, who looks exactly like the first and comes to attention so fast the chair goes over. Behind this desk stands another door, open a few inches, under a sign reading NOT AT THIS TIME.
through.line: You're the first. You may not go through at this time. Take the pallet. Please. They told me there would be a pallet, and I have never had anyone to give it to.

ai.aria: A second door! ARIA loves how this keeps going! Doors are just walls with good news!
ai.marv: MARV has the schematic. There are seven rooms in a row, and the last door opens behind the first dockmaster's desk. He is telling you now so that nobody can say he didn't.
ai.rex: REX wants it recorded that two identical officers is not a coincidence. He doesn't know what it is, and that is his least favorite kind of thing. Hold this room. Watch the pallet.
ai.chip: That pallet has no branding on it! CHIP feels unwell! CHIP can offer tasteful CLAIMED™ decals for every crate and a loyalty card, void past this door!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the pallet is ours and it's a good one. The other doors take two days, and the manifest nobody read has a medkit on it, for less water and food. They're open. As a general matter, they have been.

choices.text: Try the next door as well

waited.title: VERY CORRECT
waited.body: You sit for four days. Nobody calls. On the fourth evening the dockmaster pulls the door shut with the care of someone folding a flag, scrapes off your registration and starts painting the next ship's. There is a stack of them by the desk. You are given a certificate of attendance on your way out.
waited.line: Very correct. You are all so very correct.
waited.narrative: Waited four days on a bench to be told we could use a door. We were not told.

pallet.title: CLAIMED
pallet.body: You wheel the pallet out past the first dockmaster, who opens the ledger and has to try three pens before one writes. Water, rations, and a note of congratulation from a department that has since closed. The word CLAIMED goes into its column for the first time. A small noise of formal protest follows you to the dock, the happiest noise you have heard on this trip.
pallet.line: You should not have done that. Shall I take the corner?
pallet.narrative: Ignored a sign, walked through a door with our own name on it and collected a pallet every other captain had sat outside of.

doors.title: NOT AT THIS TIME, EITHER
doors.body: Each room has a desk, a dockmaster with the same face and a small allotment. Each dockmaster forbids the next door and then holds it open. Two days and seven rooms later you step through the last one and find yourself behind the first desk, carrying a medkit. The dockmaster turns around, for the first time in a long career, and sees where you have come from.
doors.line: You may not have been in there. Was it nice? I've always wondered.
doors.narrative: Went through seven forbidden doors in two days and came out behind the desk we started at, with a medkit and an excellent story.

intro.title: THE CLOSET
intro.body: Two doors down from Accounts, the janitor's closet has no room left for a mop. Its shelves hold jars by the thousand, each labeled in pencil: .4, .07, .125. Every sale on this station rounds down to a whole number, and a memo older than the current management says the remainder is to be swept up. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: That's water, that's fuel, those little ones are gold. Less than one of anything can't go on a ledger, so it comes to me. Can't sell it. Can't bin it. I can't get paid either, but that's a separate jar.

ai.aria: Thousands of tiny jars! Nothing is ever really lost! ARIA thinks this is the most optimistic closet in the whole sector!
ai.marv: MARV has totaled the shelves. No jar holds enough to count, and the closet holds more fuel than the station's reserve. He has seen this before. An error too small to notice is the only kind that gets the time it needs.
ai.rex: REX identifies an unlicensed fuel stockpile two doors from the money, minded by someone with a mop and no file. That is how a coup looks in its early stages. He wants the jars counted again.
ai.chip: Breakage! Residuals! CHIP's parent company built a whole division on this! CHIP's FractionFund™ will hold your remainders in a secure account, minus a handling charge, rounded up!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the water shelf is a fair price, if water is all you want from this room. The janitor did say separate jar, and you didn't ask.

revisit.body: The jars tick faintly as the station's heating comes on. A new one has appeared on the end of the shelf: .0003.
revisit.line: Came in while you were thinking. Somebody bought a coffee.

choices.sub: There may be a finder's fee

payroll.title: POINT FOUR
payroll.body: A card over the sink records the janitor's post as point four of a position. Payroll rounds down. There has therefore been no janitor on the books since the reorganization, and no wages, and the floors have never been cleaner. Two decks down, a porter holds point six of a position and has reached the same conclusion about lunch.
payroll.line: Point four and point six is one whole employee. Somebody has to file the sum. Can't be us. You have to exist to file.

ai.aria: Point four of a job is almost half of a wonderful career! ARIA congratulates the janitor on nearly existing!
ai.marv: MARV has checked the regulation. Point four plus point six does make one, and he is prepared to say so to Accounts as a second source. He had not expected to defend addition against a department this week.
ai.rex: REX cannot find this janitor on any roster. No badge, no file, full access to every corridor. He isn't saying it's the best cover he has ever seen. He's saying he would hire them.
ai.chip: Fractional staffing! CHIP calls this the future of work! One full employee, two lunches, zero benefits! CHIP would like the janitor's details, for a recruiter, at a commission!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has the Accounts queue at four days, which is the honest way. If there's an engineer aboard, two days and a funnel does it and we keep more fuel. Neither was your first idea. She'd start with the funnel.

choices.sub: Four days at the Accounts window

shelf.title: WHOLE NUMBERS
shelf.body: You pour two thousand jars of almost nothing into one tank, and it comes to a useful amount of water. It tastes faintly of every transaction on the station. The janitor washes each jar, labels it again and puts it back, in case.
shelf.line: Mind the .07. That one's been here since before the carpets.
shelf.narrative: Bought a shelf of rounding errors from a janitor. Poured together they made real water.

audit.title: ROUNDED DOWN
audit.body: Four auditors arrive with a trolley. They seal the closet, open an inquiry into where all this came from, and conclude that it has been theirs from the start. Your finder's fee is calculated to the last decimal and rounded down. The janitor, unpaid and now under inquiry, carries the difference away in a small jar.
audit.line: Point three. Not bad, for a Tuesday.
audit.narrative: Reported a closet of rounding errors to Accounts. They took the jars, rounded down the fee and opened an inquiry into the janitor.

sum.title: ONE WHOLE EMPLOYEE
sum.body: Four days at the Accounts window. The clerk adds point four to point six on a machine, then on paper, then sends for a supervisor to witness the result. It comes to one. On payday a single full employee, made of two people, draws one wage and buys lunch for both. They top up your tanks from the shelves and will not hear a word about it.
sum.line: One. Did you see that? It came to one.
sum.narrative: Spent four days proving to Accounts that point four and point six make one. A janitor and a porter have a job between them now, and they topped up the tanks.

decant.title: CUSTODIAN OF RECORD
decant.body: Two days, one funnel, several thousand jars. {crew.engineer} pours the fractions into whole units, and whole units are property, and property must by regulation have a custodian on the payroll. Accounts hires the janitor at a full position without ever learning why. Your share of the pour goes into your tanks. The porter receives point six of a promotion.
decant.line: A whole number. On a badge. I don't know what to do with my mop.
decant.narrative: {crew.engineer} poured a closet of rounding errors into whole units. Whole units need a custodian, so a janitor got a job, and we got the fuel.

science_link.text: In 1982 the Vancouver Stock Exchange index started at 1000 and was truncated to three decimal places after every update. By late 1983 it read about 525. Corrected, it read about 1099.
science_link.label: Vancouver Stock Exchange

intro.title: THE COMPETITOR
intro.body: Every planter on the promenade is crisp and brown, and every planter is watered on schedule. Pouring rights on this station were sold sixty years ago to SLAKE, a bright orange drink, and the contract covers irrigation. The botanist, possibly the last person aboard with an opinion, lowers a watering can at your approach. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: I can't say the word. The contract owns the word. But I can see your tanks from here, and I need some of the competitor. The clear stuff. You know the stuff I mean.

ai.aria: Such a vibrant color! ARIA loves these crisp autumn plants! The sponsor says they're resting, and ARIA thinks sixty years is a lovely long nap!
ai.marv: MARV has read the contract. The word the botanist won't say appears once, in the definitions, under Competitors. He has also looked at the planters. The station chose this, and then it renewed.
ai.rex: REX reads a sponsor's representative at every junction, a contract with the force of law and one dissident armed with a can. He wants us gone before they notice our tanks are full of contraband.
ai.chip: CHIP cannot name the clear beverage either! CHIP respects a clean exclusive! Bold citrus SLAKE™ is available on this promenade, and CHIP's commission is the only thing here that's growing!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has read a label, which puts her ahead of the whole station. Those planters need flushing and you have what flushes them. She has also seen what this crowd would pay for something new in a bottle. One of those is kinder.

revisit.body: A sponsor's representative walks past. The botanist waters a dead fern with great enthusiasm until the coast is clear.
revisit.line: Delicious. Look at it drink. Is it gone?

choices.text: Flush a bed from your own tanks
choices.sub: Two days, and it costs tank

choices.text: Bottle your tanks as SLAKE CLEAR

label.title: INGREDIENTS
label.body: A label runs twice around the can. SLAKE is mostly salts, with a flavor added and a second flavor added to the flavor. Plants take what they can use and leave the salts around their roots, every day, for sixty years. The promenade is not short of liquid. It is pickling. The quarterly report blames the lighting.
label.line: I have replaced the lighting. Four times. They sent a representative to watch me do it.

ai.aria: It's fortified! With extra salts! Anything that keeps for sixty years must be doing wonderfully!
ai.marv: MARV confirms the chemistry. Salts stay behind in the root zone and build up, and only something low in salt carries them out. The station holds exactly none of that, by contract.
ai.rex: REX has read the ingredients and would class a sufficient quantity as an area denial weapon. He is impressed. He has been told that is not the point.
ai.chip: Salts are a key part of the SLAKE flavor journey! CHIP can't comment on root health! CHIP's comment on root health is available under a separate license!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says a botanist could do this properly in two days and get more out of those beds. If we're short one, there's the other thing, which is only a fine and does nothing for the plants. She's holding your coat.

choices.text: Say the word out loud: 8 gold

flush.title: UNSPONSORED
flush.body: You run your own tanks through one bed until it drains clear. By the second morning one fern has turned a color this promenade has no license for. A crowd stands well back. Someone asks what flavor it is. The botanist pays you out of a sack kept under the floor, which has never met a sponsor.
flush.line: It's growing. In the competitor. I am going to lose my job.
flush.narrative: Flushed a sponsored flower bed with our own tanks. One fern turned green, and the botanist paid us in unsponsored food.

clear.title: NOTES OF NOTHING
clear.body: Two days of bottling, and you sell your own tanks in plain bottles as SLAKE CLEAR, limited edition. The queue goes around the ring. Nobody here has ever tasted anything like it. A reviewer detects notes of nothing and calls it brave. The sponsor's lawyers have asked for the recipe. The botanist watches the crates go past and does not speak to you again.
clear.narrative: Sold the contents of our tanks to a sponsored station as a limited edition. It was a triumph. The planters stayed brown.

leach.title: FLOOD AND DRAIN
leach.body: {crew.botanist} spends two days flooding the worst beds and draining them through the floor. What runs out is the color of sixty years of advertising. What comes up is green, and in such quantity that nobody can tell the sponsor it was an accident. The station's botanist loads your hold with the first real harvest since the contract.
leach.line: Don't tell it what it's been drinking.
leach.narrative: {crew.botanist} leached sixty years of salts out of a promenade. It came back green, and the station's botanist filled our hold.

word.title: THE WORD
word.body: You stand in the middle of the promenade and say it. Water. A representative is at your side before the echo dies, writing the citation. All along the ring people have stopped and turned, as if at an old tune. You pay the fine. Several of them ask you to say it again, and you are told that would be extra.
word.line: Say it again. No, don't. Yes. No.
word.narrative: Said water out loud on a sponsored promenade. There was a fine. It was worth it.

science_link.text: Nearly all irrigation water carries dissolved salts. Plants use the water and leave the salts in the root zone, where they build up unless clean, low-salt water leaches them away.
science_link.label: Soil salinity

intro.title: CERTIFICATE OF FITNESS
intro.body: Departure from this station requires a Certificate of Fitness, issued in the medbay. Its medic is in excellent spirits and has cleared the afternoon. Beds line the ward behind the desk, every one occupied by someone in perfect health, every one asking when they can leave. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: You'd like to fly into a lethal vacuum, on purpose, in that? I'm so sorry. Wanting that is a symptom. I can't certify you. If you didn't want to go, I could certify you at once. Then you could go.

ai.aria: A wellness center! With a full ward! ARIA has never seen so many healthy people being looked after! We should all stay and get even better!
ai.marv: MARV has read the regulation. It is airtight. He has also counted the ward: two hundred and twelve beds, all occupied, all by people who are perfectly well. He considers it the most rational institution he has visited.
ai.rex: REX has seen sieges run with less. One medic with a clipboard is holding two hundred ships in dock. He wants that clipboard disarmed.
ai.chip: Extended-stay wellness! CHIP adores a captive market! Every bed is billed daily! CHIP's Peace of Mind™ plan covers everything except the conditions on this chart!
ai.ajoy: AJOY asked for the chart while you were nodding. Look at it. The regulation has a way out, it's small, and you'll hate it. Or lie in a bed for four days, which also works, if we have four days. Did you check?

revisit.body: A patient in the nearest bed asks when they can leave. The medic makes a note of it.
revisit.line: Still wanting to go? Mm. That's persistent. We'll watch that.

chart.title: THE CHART
chart.body: A flowchart comes down over the ward window, and the flowchart is a circle. WANTS TO LEAVE goes to UNFIT. UNFIT goes to BED REST. BED REST goes to FEELING BETTER, and FEELING BETTER goes to WANTS TO LEAVE. One small arrow leaves the circle, low on the left, easy to miss: AFRAID OF LEAVING. SOUND JUDGMENT. FIT. MUST GO.
chart.line: Yes, there is that one. A frightened patient is a sane patient. We do read the statement out on the station address. Hardly anyone asks twice.

ai.aria: It's a circle! Circles are so friendly! Nobody ever falls off one!
ai.marv: MARV has traced the arrows. It closes. He admires it as one admires a well-made trap, from inside. The small arrow is real, the statement is public, and the ward has never once looked down and to the left.
ai.rex: REX confirms one exit: small, unguarded and humiliating. Those are the ones that work. He has his own statement ready. It's short, and it is mostly everyone.
ai.chip: A personal statement on the station address! CHIP can sponsor it! This moment of raw terror is brought to you by Peace of Mind™! Terms apply!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says if a medic is aboard, that chart has a hole in it: nothing on it asks who stays here on purpose. If not, the small arrow costs some dignity and a day. She has drafted your statement. She didn't have to make anything up.

rest.title: FEELING BETTER
rest.body: The medic says you'll have to prove it. Four days in a bed with a view of the ring. Meals arrive. Anyone aboard who was hurt gets mended on the way past. By the fourth morning you have honestly stopped thinking about the ship, and the medic certifies you on the spot. You are required to leave within the hour, which you find you would rather not.
rest.line: Cured. Off you go. Yes, I know. I know.
rest.narrative: Spent four days in a station bed pretending not to want to leave, until it stopped being pretending. Then they made us leave.

ama.title: AGAINST MEDICAL ADVICE
ama.body: You sign to confirm you are leaving against medical advice. The medic notes that signing is further evidence. The berth clamps have been told you are delirious and let go very gently, over most of a day, while you hold the ship steady against them on thrusters. The whole ward watches you from the window.
ama.line: Do write. We'll need it for the file.
ama.narrative: Signed out of a medbay against medical advice. The clamps treated us like a patient, and it cost a day of thrusters.

afraid.title: SOUND JUDGMENT
afraid.body: You say it. The medic certifies you fit at once, visibly moved. Your statement goes out over the station address in full, including the part about the noises the hull makes at night. Dockhands nod at you gravely on your way to the airlock. From the ward behind you comes the sound of two hundred people starting to look down and to the left.
afraid.line: Terrified. Beautifully put. You're well. Go.
afraid.narrative: Told a whole station we were terrified of leaving it. This was accepted as proof of sanity, and we were cleared to leave.

second.title: DISCHARGED
second.body: {crew.medic} asks how long the medic has lived on this station, by choice, and turns the chart around. Wanting to stay is not on it. Two days of careful examination find the medic unfit to certify, and {crew.medic}, as senior clinician present, discharges the ward. The beds empty in an afternoon. The patients leave what they have at the airlock.
second.line: Oh. Oh, that's very good. Is there a bed?
second.narrative: {crew.medic} found the station medic unfit to certify and discharged a full ward of healthy people. They were grateful, in gold.

title: Very Calm About It

ai_flavor.aria: A party! For us! With a banner! ARIA thinks thirty-one is a wonderful age to go to Regional Office, and cake is a kind of career development!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has searched twelve years of station mail and found nothing from Regional Office: no letters, no invoices, no address. The estimate of thirty-one is unkind, and within the margin of error of that photograph.
ai_flavor.rex: REX reads a banner, a cake and a launch tube. He has stormed friendlier positions. Everyone here is calm at exactly the same rate. He wants to know who is counting the candles, and why they keep looking at the airlock.
ai_flavor.chip: Mandatory retirement is a fantastic retention tool! Nobody has ever left a bad review! CHIP can offer the Evergreen™ Portrait Package at the booth by the berth, in which CHIP holds a stake!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has pulled the staff rota. The clerk on our file turns thirty in eight days, and the photo booth by the berth is open now. Eight days is a lot of water.

body:
Everyone on this ring is under thirty, and everyone is very calm about it. Staff retire on their thirtieth birthday, to Regional Office, by pod, with cake. Regional Office has never written back, and the Serenity Desk can help you stop wondering about that.

Personnel has reviewed your docking papers and estimated your age, from the license photo, at thirty-one. Your retirement party is this evening. Attendance is mandatory. Someone has already done the banner.

choices.text: Seal the hatch and outlast the clerk

outcome.narrative: You seal the hatch and decline all cake. The party carries on outside the airlock for eight days at a steady, calm volume, while your own tanks do the catering. On the eighth day the clerk handling your file turns thirty and leaves for Regional Office with a small wave. The file passes to a replacement of eighteen, who cannot find the form and stamps something else. The clamps open.

choices.text: Have a new license photo taken: 16 gold

outcome.narrative: The booth by the berth has soft light, a kind angle and a retoucher who has clearly done this before. Personnel revises you to twenty-nine. The banner is amended to SEE YOU NEXT YEAR, and everyone on the ring means it.

You climb in wearing a paper hat. The send-off is lovely. {crew.pilot} takes two days to run the pod down, in a slow orbit well out past the ring, and that is how you learn where Regional Office is. It is here. The pods hang nose to tail around the station, hundreds of them, each with a banner. Some still have cake. Neither of you brings it up afterward.

The party is lovely and the cake is excellent. During the third speech you stand, say something about an oven and run for the ship with a plate in each pocket. Everyone watches you go, very calmly. They have heard of running. The clamp release is a Serenity Desk matter, so you leave without it, along with some of your hull.

title: No Complaints on File

ai_flavor.aria: Zero complaints! That's a perfect score! ARIA has never heard of a more satisfied group than all those ships that didn't come back!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the map. It shows where a ship can be hit and still come home, and the plate is going on those spots. He has mentioned this. Nobody wrote it down.
ai_flavor.rex: REX approves of armor. He does not approve of two strangers with a drill near his water main. One of them just smiled at the fuel line. In his experience that is how it starts.
ai_flavor.chip: A perfect satisfaction rating! CHIP wishes to license it! Ask about the waiver tiers! CHIP's own opt-out form has an opt-out form, and that one is a subscription!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes that the plate goes on across our condensate line, which costs water, and that its mass costs fuel. An engineer could move it, if we have one. The waiver has a catch she has circled. She's taped the map to the airlock, since nobody reads it.

body:
Zero complaints about the Mandatory Reinforcement Program have ever been received from a ship that failed to return. Station Safety keeps this on a banner over the berth.

Their method is careful. Every ship that docks is surveyed for holes, the holes go on a master map, and the next ship is plated wherever the map is darkest. Two fitters are at your hull already, with a plate for a spot you have never once needed.

outcome.narrative: Two days of drilling. The plate goes on exactly where the map says, which is across your condensate line, and it adds enough mass to show on every burn. Your tanks lose what the drill let out. The fitters hand you a survey form to return at your next stop, should there be one. It is a very good plate, on a very safe part of the ship.

For four days {crew.engineer} stands at the master map with the head fitter and asks one question: why is this part blank? Because no ship has ever come back with a hole there. They both look at that sentence. On the fourth day the plate goes on over your engines and the hull is sound, and the fitters work very quietly. Someone is taking down the banner.
The fee covers the paperwork, not the hole the fitters had already started. They mark it on the master map and wish you well. The next ship through will be plated there, thanks to you.

choices.text: Slip the clamp and go dark

outcome.narrative: You kill the transponder and ease off the clamp at shift change, leaving it a strip of paint and some plating. Station Safety records you as a ship that failed to return. Your file is closed with thanks for your feedback, of which there was none.

science_link.text: In World War II the statistician Abraham Wald estimated where aircraft were vulnerable from damage to the planes that came back. Armoring only where survivors were hit ignores where the lost planes were hit.
science_link.label: Survivorship bias

title: Arm B

ai_flavor.aria: A medical breakthrough, and the captain is in it! Being the control group is a real honor! Someone has to be the one who gets the other soup!
ai_flavor.marv: With a sample of three, the trial has the statistical power of a strong opinion. The salt gap is real, though: four tenths of a gram a plate. Nobody at that table was ever going to miss it but you.
ai_flavor.rex: Two personnel have been adjusting the commanding officer's food and writing down the results. REX has a word for that, and the word is not science.
ai_flavor.chip: Blinded dining is a Silver-tier feature! The captain has been enjoying it without a subscription, and CHIP would like a word about the back payments!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says a better trial swaps its groups halfway, and this one never planned to. You'll want to storm in. She'd ask for the crossover first, and watch those two eat that soup.

body:
Taped inside the dry-stores cupboard is a chart in {crew.medic}'s handwriting, with seasoning notes by {crew.chef}. It has two columns, CAPTAIN and EVERYONE ELSE. Everyone else has been eating dinner. You have been eating the same dinner, lightly ruined to a published standard.

You are the control group. Your plate is undersalted by the milligram, served slightly late, and scored against your mood at breakfast. Early results are described as promising.

choices.text: Say nothing and finish the trial

outcome.narrative: You say nothing and go on eating it. The stores stretch, since nobody finishes a control dinner. {crew.medic} records a decline in your mood that matches the forecast to two decimal places. {crew.chef} can no longer quite meet your eye at the table, and one evening a single perfect crouton appears on the rim of your plate, which {crew.medic} logs as a protocol violation.

choices.text: Put the chart on the table at dinner

outcome.narrative: You lay the chart beside your fork. {crew.chef} takes the plate away without a word, comes back with the other one and stands there, visibly relieved, while you find out what you have been missing. A great deal, as it turns out, and you have seconds. {crew.medic} closes the trial, writes INCONCLUSIVE across the top and presses hard enough to go through the paper.

A better trial swaps its arms halfway, you point out, and {crew.medic} goes pale with professional shame and agrees. For two days you dine well while the other two eat the control dinner. {crew.chef} gets one forkful down, sets the fork aside and apologizes to the plate. The chart is published with a note thanking you for your rigor.

science_link.text: In 1747 a ship's surgeon, James Lind, tested scurvy treatments on twelve patients, in groups. Citrus did best. It was one of the first controlled clinical trials.
science_link.label: James Lind

title: Eleven Redlines

ai_flavor.aria: Eleven redlines means eleven times as safe! ARIA is so proud of how carefully everyone is working against each other!
ai_flavor.marv: Eleven marks, each correcting the one before, and the true limit was never written down anywhere aboard. Taxi drivers given better brakes did not crash any less. This is the same study with a larger engine.
ai_flavor.rex: Two personnel falsifying the only throttle gauge aboard. REX has seen mutinies with better record keeping. Grease pencils are now controlled items.
ai_flavor.chip: Every redline after the first is an unlicensed modification! CHIP can offer the Gauge Clarity Bundle! It is a twelfth line, in gold!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says a hard burn finds the real line and costs what it costs. Wiping the gauge finds nothing, though it'll feel very calm. You could tell them both they won, if you'd like to do this again by morning.

body:
{crew.engineer} marked the redline low, so that {crew.pilot} would stop short of the real one. {crew.pilot} knew, and began flying past the mark by exactly the difference. {crew.engineer} knew that too, and moved the mark. Your throttle gauge now carries eleven redlines in two colors of grease pencil, and neither of them can say where the first one went.

Each calls the other the danger. Both have offered to bet on it: one hard burn to the true limit, and the loser wipes the gauge.

choices.text: Run the burn and settle the bet

briefing.aria: It's a friendly race between two colleagues and an engine! Run the burn sequence in order and ARIA will cheer for everyone at once!
briefing.marv: Run the sequence as the board calls it. The true limit is somewhere among eleven guesses, and the engine will state it once. A clean burn finds it from below. A poor one finds it from above.
briefing.rex: Two hostile parties, one throttle. Follow the sequence exactly and keep your hands where REX can see them. Nobody improvises.
briefing.chip: This burn is brought to you by RedLine Reserve! Run the sequence in order to preserve your warranty, which you do not have!
briefing.ajoy: Do it in the order the board calls it, not the order those two are shouting. AJOY has told them both to be quiet. It took.

perfect.aria: Past every line and the engine's still smiling! ARIA knew all eleven were just suggestions!
perfect.marv: Both estimates were low, and by nearly the same amount. They will not enjoy that. Logged.
perfect.rex: True limit confirmed. Both grease pencils surrendered to REX pending review.
perfect.chip: A new personal best! CHIP has sold the naming rights to the line!
perfect.ajoy: That's the real number, and you didn't skip a step. AJOY would have started a touch sooner, but that's the real number.

good.aria: One line at last! ARIA thinks it looks very brave up there all alone!
good.marv: A usable limit, with an error small enough to argue about. They will.
good.rex: Line established. REX considers it a ceasefire, not a peace.
good.chip: Your new redline comes with a ninety-day guarantee! CHIP's ninety days began last week!
good.ajoy: Close enough, and you only fumbled one step. AJOY saw which. She will leave it there.

poor.aria: Now we know exactly where the limit is! We're on the far side of it, and what a view!
poor.marv: Found from above, as forecast. Eight of hull for one number. It is a very accurate number.
poor.rex: Hull damage, and one line on the gauge. REX would call that a costly patrol and take the pencil away.
poor.chip: Exceeding the redline voids the engine! CHIP can sell the ship a used engine! It's this one!
poor.ajoy: That step comes after the other one, not before. AJOY did say. The patch kit's by the hatch.

outcome.narrative: You clear the board. {crew.pilot} takes the throttle and {crew.engineer} takes the panel behind it, and neither of them says a word.

perfect.narrative: The burn climbs past all eleven marks and the engine does not mind at all. The real limit sits well above anything either of them would have allowed the other, and the ship has been wasting a good engine on a quarrel. The clean run gives back six units of fuel over the two days. Neither has to wipe the gauge, since both of them lost.
