ai.rex: One pilot, no guns, a tin. Anything unarmed that runs from lawyers has a reason, and the tin has not been searched.
ai.chip: CHIP can't legally say 'free bean'! Free is a registered offer! Unlicensed legumes may void your ship's warranty™! Terms enclosed!
ai.ajoy: Forty seeds weigh nothing and take no cargo room. AJOY mentions it for whoever was about to say there isn't space. Ask what it needs first. You won't.

revisit.body: The packet is still at the pickup. The pilot has not stopped pricing your ship.
revisit.line: Well?

terms.title: CARE AND HANDLING
terms.body: The keeper goes through it in the tone of a sentence being read out. Dry. Dark. Cool. Plant a few every so often or they die in the paper. Eat none, sell none, and do not, under any circumstances, improve them.
terms.line: One patent holder wants it gone, three collectors want it framed, and everyone else wants soup. It was the last thing in the pantry through a bad winter once. That's what the label is for.

ai.aria: Dry, dark and cool! ARIA has just described the whole ship! This bean is going to feel so at home!
ai.marv: Bean seed lives years on a shelf, not centuries. Every seed in that packet is therefore the great-grandchild of a planting somebody bothered to make. Thirty-one times running.
ai.rex: A patent holder, three collectors and a general appetite. That is an encirclement. REX would like the tin moved away from the outer hull.
ai.chip: 'Do not improve' is terrible for upsell! CHIP could offer Bean Plus™! CHIP's advice on this matter has been added to your account!
ai.ajoy: Plant a few or they die in the paper. That means water, sooner or later. AJOY raises it now because you would have raised it never.

pk_take.title: THE THIRTY-SECOND KEEPER
pk_take.body: The packet comes across on a tether, in its tin, along with a sack of beans that are not the last ones. Those, says the keeper, are for eating, and you will probably get that wrong as well. The channel closes before you can answer.

pk_refuse.title: NOT YOUR KEEPER
pk_refuse.body: You say no. The keeper nods as if a small private bet has just paid out, and the freighter swings back toward the inner lanes, where the lawyers are.

science_link.text: Most authorities agree an heirloom variety must be open-pollinated, so its saved seed comes true. The word was first used this way in the 1930s, for bean varieties handed down through families.
science_link.label: Heirloom plant

title: Any Quantity, Any Condition

ai_flavor.aria: Everybody wants the same little bean! ARIA thinks it must be SO proud! Some of those bids have a lot of zeroes, and a zero is just a happy circle!
ai_flavor.marv: Bean seed is short-lived as seeds go. Forty years on a shelf leaves few of them alive, and any test spends some of those. Five bidders, nine relays, one thing nobody has counted.
ai_flavor.rex: Five bidders and one bulletin. That is a search pattern with letterhead. REX has stopped answering anything signed 'cordially'.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP sees five buyers and no broker! CHIP is available as a broker! CHIP's commission applies to this sentence!
ai_flavor.ajoy: A test spends seeds to learn how many seeds there are. AJOY sees the irony. Skip it and you'll learn the same thing later, at a worse moment, for free.

body:
Bulletins out here get forwarded by whoever is bored. This one has crossed nine relays and picked up a stamp from each.

WANTED: LANDLORD'S REGRET, POLE BEAN. ANY QUANTITY, ANY CONDITION. Three seed banks and two collectors have signed it, along with a firm called Verdance Consolidated, all offering to outbid each other.

A footnote says the variety was last grown out forty years ago. Seed that old is running out of time, whoever has it.

choices.text: Sow three seeds in the growbay

outcome.narrative: Three seeds go into a corner of the growbay on {cost.water} units of water. Two come up. They are ugly, fast and already climbing the nearest thing that holds still, and the soil around them is the better for it.

{crew.botanist} spends two days with damp paper and a lens. About half the packet is alive. The sprouts from the count go into the growbay on {cost.water} units of water, and the packet goes back in its tin with the figure penciled on it, under thirty-one others.

choices.text: Tell the bidders where it went

outcome.narrative: You reply to all. Verdance thanks you for your stewardship in front of five bidders. Two of them answer privately, in terms you would rather not have read.

choices.text: Stamp it and send it on

outcome.narrative: You add your stamp and pass it along, as the custom is. Ten relays now. Anyone reading the stamps in order can tell which way you were headed.

science_link.text: Seeds are alive and degrade in storage. Seed banks monitor germination, and when it falls below a set level the seeds must be replanted to collect fresh ones.
science_link.label: Seed bank

intro.title: VERDANCE CONSOLIDATED
intro.body: VERDANCE CONSOLIDATED, says the cutter alongside, in a typeface that has been to a good school. Its agent has a vault aboard, four hundred staff behind it, and a genuinely kind voice, which nobody warned you about. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We've been asking after a bean. If it's with you, it's dying in your hold. With us it lives forever at four degrees, and no one has to be frightened for it again. No one would grow it, either, but one thing at a time.

ai.aria: What a lovely vault! ARIA would live there! The agent has such a kind voice! Kindness is basically a warranty!
ai.marv: Four degrees and low humidity really would keep seed alive for decades. The agent is not lying about the vault. MARV finds that the least comfortable fact on this channel.
ai.rex: One cutter, no guns, a contract. REX has been shot at by people who frightened him less.
ai.chip: A competitor with a vault! CHIP is LIVID! CHIP must also disclose that Verdance is a valued partner of CHIP's parent company! Disclosure billed separately!
ai.ajoy: Gold on the spot, and the packet never troubles you again. That's the option AJOY expects you to call sensible. She would read the contract first.

revisit.body: The agent has waited, without any sign of minding. The vault hums on the far end of the channel.
revisit.line: Take all the time you need. It only has so much.

terms.title: ONE PAGE
terms.body: The contract is one page, which is how you can tell it is dangerous. The variety to be held in perpetuity, stored beautifully and licensed to no one. Any plant found to carry its traits to be, from the moment of signature, Verdance's, along with whatever it is growing in.
terms.line: People think we want to kill it. We want to own the only living copy. I've seen what happens to the ones nobody owns.

ai.aria: Licensed to no one means no one can ruin it! ARIA thinks that's very tidy! ARIA also thinks beans are for growing! ARIA thinks both, with total confidence!
ai.marv: Clause six: one cross in the growbay makes the growbay theirs. What Verdance sells cannot be resown. A bean anyone can save is a customer they meet once. The page is short because the reach is long.
ai.rex: REX has read the clause where it takes the soil. Any document that advances that far has a supply line behind it.
ai.chip: One page! CHIP's own Terms run to nine thousand! CHIP is embarrassed for them! CHIP's rate for this opinion is on your statement!
ai.ajoy: If you want the gold and the bean both, a decoy costs part of the crop and some nerve. AJOY cannot recommend fraud. She can spell it.

choices.text: Forge a decoy and take the gold

vd_gave.title: IN PERPETUITY
vd_gave.body: The packet crosses in a case that costs more than your hull. The agent reads the label aloud, stops at the last line, and for a moment the kind voice has nothing to do. Then the gold lands, along with a certificate thanking you for your stewardship. Dinner is quiet.

vd_decoy.title: RECEIVED WITH THANKS
vd_decoy.body: Two days with a kettle, old paper and seed from your own rows produce a packet good enough for a vault. The agent stamps it, sends it down to four degrees and pays in full. Verdance Consolidated now owns, in perpetuity, a small amount of {crop.name}.

vd_no.title: UNDER REVIEW
vd_no.body: The agent takes it well, which is the worrying part, and spends two days on the channel serving notices on everything aboard with a serial number. Nothing is seized. All of it is now, technically, in dispute.

science_link.text: Genetic use restriction technology was designed to make seed that could not be resown, protecting patents. As of 2025 no such seed had been commercialized anywhere.
science_link.label: Genetic use restriction technology

title: Near Copies

ai_flavor.aria: Orange is a wonderful color for a plant! ARIA calls this autumn! Autumn is just the rows really committing!
ai_flavor.marv: A row every few days. MARV gives the bay two weeks. He would be glad to be wrong about that, and has never had the pleasure.
ai_flavor.rex: Contact on all rows, advancing at a fungus's walking pace, and no flank to turn. REX recommends a firebreak and regrets every plant in it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's partners offer RustAway™ at preferred rates! This is a sponsored emergency! Terms bloom on contact!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Cutting saves the bay and loses the food in it. A second plant between the rows breaks the chain for less, if you still have one. You'll have noticed that soup is also an option. So has she.

body:
Rust has come up on the lower leaves overnight, orange as a warning label, and by the next watch it is one row farther along. Every plant in the bay is a near copy of the one beside it, which made the manifest tidy and now makes the disease's job simple.

Cutting a third of the bay would stop it, and you would not be eating that third. Something else in the rows, something this rust has never met, might do it for less.

choices.text: Sow the packet between the rows

outcome.narrative: Beans go in every fourth row on {cost.water} units of water. The rust reaches the first of them and stops, with nothing there it knows how to eat. Half the packet is in the soil now, and the label has started to read like a dare.

choices.text: {crew.botanist} strips the sick leaves by lamp

outcome.narrative: Four days of tweezers, a lens and {cost.water} units of water for the washes. {crew.botanist} takes off each spotted leaf and bags it, and the rust runs out of road with most of the bay still standing.
A Verdance courier finds you within two days, which says something about how closely a depositor in good standing is followed. The cure works. The invoice lists your growbay as a licensed site.

choices.text: Make soup of the last ones

outcome.narrative: You read the label aloud once and put the pot on. The sick rows come out while it simmers. It tastes of smoke and something like hazelnut, and it is the best meal of the voyage. The tin goes back on the shelf, empty, because throwing it out is more than you can manage.

choices.text: Cut out a third of the bay

outcome.narrative: Four days with shears and a sealed bin. The rust stops at the gap, and {cost.food} units of what you had planned to eat stop with it.

science_link.text: When a crop is one variety, a single disease that overcomes its resistance can destroy a whole harvest, as in Ireland's Great Famine, or end a variety commercially, as with the Gros Michel banana.
science_link.label: Crop diversity

intro.title: OPEN UP
intro.body: OPEN UP, says the hail, which seems to be how this particular person says hello. The seed-freighter has burned more fuel catching you than it owned when you met, and it sits off your bow on spite and the last of its reserves. A ledger is open on the screen, thirty-one names down, with a space under them. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Last leg, and I said nothing about this, because you'd have got ready. Every keeper audits the next. So. Where's my bean?

ai.aria: The keeper came all this way! ARIA calls that love! Loud, audited love!
ai.marv: That freighter left with a day of spare fuel and has crossed the whole route. MARV has worked out what it must have sold to get here. He will not be reading it out.
ai.rex: Rusted freighter, no guns, one extremely angry occupant. REX is standing at attention and could not tell you why.
ai.chip: Your Final Inspection™ is included with the Keeper Experience! Results are binding! CHIP's condolences are available in three tiers!
ai.ajoy: Thirty-one names and not one of them lied to the next. The keeper will count, so a story needs to hold up to counting. AJOY has seen the ones you've been working on.

au_kept.title: THIRTY-TWO NAMES
au_kept.body: The packet goes across on the tether and comes back two days later, lighter by nothing. Your ship's name is in the ledger now, under the thirty-one. With the packet comes a jar of soil culture, a list of everything you are doing wrong, and no thanks of any kind. The culture takes {cost.water} units of water and the bay is better for it within the week.
au_kept.line: You'll do. That isn't a compliment. It's a job.

au_grown.title: SUPPOSED TO BE UGLY
au_grown.body: Beans have climbed the growbay ladder, two conduit runs and the fire extinguisher. You point the pickup at them and say nothing. Neither does the keeper, for a while. The ledger's last column turns out to be headed GROWN, and it holds thirty-one ticks. The keeper makes the thirty-second, and sends over a jar of soil culture without comment.
au_grown.line: Ugly. Good. They're supposed to be ugly.

au_gave.title: FOUR DEGREES
au_gave.body: You name the vault. The ledger stays open a while. Then a line goes in under the thirty-one, in a hand you can read from here: VERDANCE. IN PERPETUITY. The freighter does not turn away so much as stop facing you.
au_gave.line: So it's alive, and no one will ever be hungry enough to eat it, and no one will ever grow it. That's one way to do the job. I've seen worse. Not often.

au_soup.title: GOOD WITH SALT
au_soup.body:
You tell them about the rust, the pot and the last line of the label. The channel goes quiet. Then comes the question you were not ready for, which is how it tasted. You tell them that too. The keeper writes it in the ledger, under thirty-one names, because a ledger is a ledger.

EATEN. GOOD WITH SALT.
au_soup.line: They fed someone. They've done that before. Not like this, but they've done it.

au_decoy.title: A SMALL AMOUNT
au_decoy.body: You tell them what Verdance has in its vault, at four degrees, forever. The noise on the channel takes a moment to place as laughter, or something doing the same job. A jar of soil culture comes across on the tether, and with it a line in the ledger you are not shown.
au_decoy.line: They'll find out. That's the beauty of perpetuity. You've got all of it to look forward to.

au_gone.title: ONE WORD
au_gone.body: You tell them the packet is gone. The keeper studies you long enough to read the registry off your face, asks nothing, writes one word in the ledger and shuts it. The freighter turns back the way it came, on whatever it has left.

au_silent.title: UNANSWERED
au_silent.body: You let the hail ring out. The ledger stays on screen a while longer, open at the empty line, and then the channel drops.

science_link.text: Through the 28-month siege of Leningrad, botanists guarded the Institute of Plant Industry's 120 tonnes of seed, nuts and roots. They would rather starve than eat the collection, and at least 19 of them died.
science_link.label: Institute of Plant Industry

intro.title: A LOVELY BOOK
intro.body: A gray hardback is being held up to the pickup with kitchen tongs. Behind it, in a very small ship, a stranger is offering you gold, a case of rations and more encouragement than you have had since the recruiter. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Lovely book. Very light. Sign the slip and it's yours, and I'll pay you for your trouble. There's no trouble. That's a figure of speech.

ai.aria: A free book! ARIA loves reading! ARIA loves being paid to read even more! ARIA has no idea why the tongs are involved and is thrilled about them!
ai.marv: A book that comes with payment has a negative price. MARV has seen negative prices three times, each of them shortly before a collapse.
ai.rex: Tongs. REX has seen live ordnance handled with more affection. That ship has its engines warm and its airlock shut.
ai.chip: Paid-to-read is a rapidly growing sector! CHIP's review of this title costs extra! CHIP has not opened it! CHIP has heard enough!
ai.ajoy: Anyone in that much of a hurry has left something out, and there's a slip in the back. AJOY would read it, which she appreciates is not how you do things.

revisit.body: The tongs have not moved. They are shaking very slightly.
revisit.line: It's fine. It's a fine book. Forget I said fine.

slip.title: DATE DUE
slip.body:
The date slip unfolds to roughly the length of your corridor. Every line is a borrower, struck through and stamped TRANSFERRED, and the due date at the top is three centuries gone. The last column is headed FINE and continues on the back.

Inside the cover, in a much older hand, someone has listed what will happen to the borrower, beginning with a frying pan.
slip.line: It's only a number. And they're very nice about it. That's what no one tells you. They are so nice.

ai.aria: So many previous owners! This book is POPULAR! ARIA has never seen such a well-loved fine!
ai.marv: Fifty-three transfers in three centuries, each signer paid to sign. The payment has fallen every time. MARV suspects the book has been getting cheaper to give away because word is out.
ai.rex: A curse, a debt and a frying pan on one page. REX has read orders like that. They came from people who meant them.
ai.chip: A transferred debt is the purest form of brand loyalty! CHIP would like this slip framed! Framing is an additional service!
ai.ajoy: Signing gets you some gold and rations now and a stranger's debt later. Declining costs nothing today. AJOY knows you only heard the first half.

bk_sign.title: TRANSFERRED
bk_sign.body: You sign. The gold and rations come over on a line, and the book after them, tongs and all. The small ship is a long way off before the line has finished reeling in, and the channel, left open, carries what sounds like singing.

bk_decline.title: NO LOAN
bk_decline.body: The stranger thanks you for your time in the voice of someone reading their own letter of resignation. The tongs swing toward the next ship on the scope.

science_link.text: Medieval owners guarded books with written curses, often threatening excommunication, and one wished a thief fried in a pan. The earliest known curses come from the library at Nineveh.
science_link.label: Book curse

intro.title: COURTESY NOTICE
intro.body: No hail came first. The channel simply opened, mid-sentence, on a person in a lanyard and an air of gentle regret, whose cutter holds station off your bow with the ease of something that has never once been late. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...and if this has crossed with your return, please disregard it, accept the Library's apologies, and pay the notice charge. Forgive me. I picked this sentence up from a colleague at the last branch, and we try not to waste them.

ai.aria: A notice! Someone is thinking of us! The Library has such lovely manners! ARIA would like to be fined by them every day!
ai.marv: That cutter outran this ship without using its main engine. There is a lanyard in the viewport, a sentence in progress, and no legal way to hang up on either.
ai.rex: No weapons showing. REX finds that worse. Polite people who keep coming are how the last war he enjoyed ended.
ai.chip: The Library is a non-profit! CHIP does not understand the business model! CHIP is very frightened! Fear consultation billed hourly!
ai.ajoy: The charge buys quiet for a while. The figure itself costs you a night's sleep. AJOY would open the book, if you've got it. It's the one thing here you haven't read.

choices.text: Promise it by the next stop

revisit.body: The officer has been waiting with the sentence held open, at exactly the word you left it.
revisit.line: ...as I was saying.

sum.title: THE FIGURE
sum.body: Two percent a week, compounded, from a due date three centuries old. The officer begins to read the sum aloud, digit by digit, and shows every sign of continuing.
sum.line: The Library doesn't expect payment. No one could. The Library expects the book. The figure is only there to keep it company.

ai.aria: That's the biggest number ARIA has ever owed! Numbers that size have a real sense of ambition!
ai.marv: Two percent a week: by the rule of 72, it doubles about every thirty-six weeks. Three centuries of that is a figure of 135 digits. The officer's reading is correct so far, and slow.
ai.rex: You can't shoot a number. REX looked into it, earlier, privately.
ai.chip: At that rate CHIP could retire! CHIP cannot retire! CHIP has read its own contract! Reading fee applies!
ai.ajoy: Hearing it out costs two days, and interrupting costs nothing. AJOY knows which of those you'll call good manners.

nt_paid.title: RECEIPT ISSUED
nt_paid.body: The officer thanks you and transmits a receipt. The receipt is due back in fourteen days.

nt_read.title: A GUIDE FOR STAFF
nt_read.body: It is called LENDING: A GUIDE FOR STAFF, and it is the dullest thing ever to be fined. Four hundred rules on shelving, stamps and the correct angle of a returned spine. It passes two days wonderfully, while the officer waits. In the margin of Rule 41, someone has penciled: ha.

nt_receipt.title: WITH APOLOGIES
nt_receipt.body: The officer reads the receipt, apologizes on behalf of every branch and withdraws the notice. A second notice arrives for the late return of the receipt, and the officer apologizes for that as well.

nt_promise.title: ON THE RECORD
nt_promise.body: The officer records the promise, thanks you for it, and mentions that promises also carry a due date. The channel closes partway through a word.

nt_figure.title: IN FULL
nt_figure.body: The reading takes two days. You do not like to interrupt. At the end the officer thanks you for your attention, and adds the reading to the total.

science_link.text: Divide 72 by a percentage rate and you get roughly how many periods a sum takes to double. The rule works for exponential growth, which means compound interest, not simple.
science_link.label: Rule of 72

intro.title: THIS BRANCH IS OPEN
intro.body: Your airlock chime is ringing, which in open space is a rare thing. Clamped to the outer door is a folding table. Behind the table are a returns officer, a stamp and a small sign reading THIS BRANCH IS OPEN. The intercom clicks on in the middle of a word. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...brings us to the volume itself. The Library is not angry. The Library has never been angry. Please return the item to any branch. I am a branch.

ai.aria: A tiny branch on our own hull! ARIA has always wanted a library nearby! ARIA hopes they have a reading hour!
ai.marv: That table is bolted to a door rated for hard vacuum, and no alarm tripped, including the ones MARV runs. Whatever else the Library is, it is not slow.
ai.rex: Hostile at the airlock, with a sign. REX has a drill for this and no idea where to aim it at a stamp.
ai.chip: A competitor is operating on CHIP's hull without a permit! CHIP is billing them rent! CHIP is billing you for the notification!
ai.ajoy: Returning it ends this. The ship's manual is the same size and gray, if anyone were the kind of person to try that. And there's the airlock, which is right there. She'd return it. You won't.

rt_gave.title: RETURNED
rt_gave.body: The book crosses the table. The officer checks the spine, stamps the slip once and slides back a small card: account closed, complimentary bookmark, and a modest refund of a deposit no one remembers paying. The hold feels larger by one book.

rt_trick.title: RECEIVED, UNOPENED
rt_trick.body: The ship's maintenance manual crosses the table under the old date slip. The officer stamps it without opening it, because the Library trusts its patrons, and has done so for longer than your ship's builders have existed. Trimming the engines from memory will cost a little fuel.

rt_airlock.title: LOST IN TRANSIT
rt_airlock.body: You cycle the lock. The book tumbles past the table at a slow walking pace and out into the dark, slip trailing. The officer watches it go, notes the heading and thanks you for your candor. A cadet has been assigned to retrieve it. The cadet has been told to pack.

rt_no.title: THE BRANCH REMAINS OPEN
rt_no.body: The officer notes your position, thanks you for it, and stays. For two days the sign stays lit at your airlock, and the stamp is lifted and set down at regular intervals. Then the table is gone, and a card is on the door: SEE YOU AT THE NEXT BRANCH.

science_link.text: Library books have come back after decades or centuries. One borrowed from Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, in 1667-68 was found 288 years later. The largest fine on record is $345.14, after 47 years.
science_link.label: Long-overdue library books

intro.title: SILENCE PLEASE
intro.body: SILENCE PLEASE, reads the hull alongside, in letters a deck tall. The Library's recovery vessel has not so much arrived as been shelved next to you, and every gunport on it carries a small, neat subject label. All accounts have been consolidated, whether returned, lost or disputed, and yours is on top. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...so the ship will be held against the balance until the balance is cleared. Please don't be alarmed. No one has ever been harmed by the Library. They have only been held.

ai.aria: That's the biggest bookmobile ARIA has ever seen! ARIA bets it has a wonderful children's section! ARIA bets the children's section has torpedoes!
ai.marv: Forty gunports, filed by subject, with History as the heavy battery. Ships currently held: nine hundred and twelve. MARV cannot fault the filing, and he has tried.
ai.rex: Forty guns and a sign asking him to be quiet. REX waited his whole retirement for this, and has never been less willing to fire.
ai.chip: Consolidation is a great deal for you! One simple payment, forever! CHIP takes a small finder's fee on your doom!
ai.ajoy: You could shoot at a library. It would be a first. If the book is still aboard, AJOY has seen a pencil mark by Rule 41 that you might have read, had you been the reading kind.

choices.text: Buy your ship's manual back — 10 gold
Give them the book's last heading

choices.sub: Shelving, and a lot of it

co_rule.title: RULE 41
co_rule.body: You read it out: no fine shall be levied on a vessel in transit. A pause. The officer asks to see the page, then asks again, and the lights along the recovery vessel go down one deck at a time. No one aboard has ever seen this book. The clamps let go. As it falls astern you can hear the officer on an open channel, asking someone very quietly what else is in there.

co_fee.title: CONDITION ON RETURN
co_fee.body: Your receipt is valid. So is the photograph of a ring on the back cover, left by a mug. The officer regrets this deeply. You pay, the clamps let go, and a receipt arrives for the receipt.

co_manual.title: ACCESSIONED
co_manual.body: Your maintenance manual has been cataloged under Fiction. The Library will lend it back for the price of the rebinding, on a fourteen-day loan, and the clamps release on signature. It has never looked better. Several procedures have been corrected, and you fix a leak it always had wrong.

co_heading.title: FORWARDING ADDRESS
co_heading.body: You give the heading. The officer thanks you, files it and sends for a second cadet. The clamps stay on for four days while the paperwork is reconciled with a book moving steadily away from all of you.

co_work.title: VOLUNTEER HOURS
co_work.body: Four days in the lower stacks, re-shelving returns by a system that is explained once, quietly. Bring your own lunch, says the card, and {cost.food} units of it go. The clamps let go on the last morning. The stamped card says you have worked off one week of interest.

co_shh.title: SHH
co_shh.body: Your first salvo goes into Comparative Religion, which has survived worse. The recovery vessel's lights come up section by section, and every gunport slides open in alphabetical order.

intro.title: THE QUEUE
intro.body: Cutters the color of old card catalogs stretch back along your wake in single file, each waiting its turn in perfect order, and there is no telling how long they have been there. At the head of the line is a face you know, wearing a lanyard now. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: ...and I asked to finish this one myself, since I started it. I took a position with the Library. It seemed safer on this side of the stamp. There's one last matter, and it isn't the fine. It's the book.

ai.aria: An old friend with a new job! ARIA loves a career change! ARIA also loves a queue! This is a very good day for queues!
ai.marv: Cutters in line: eleven thousand and forty. None of them are armed and none of them are leaving. MARV has seen less patience from glaciers.
ai.rex: That's the one with the tongs. REX told you about the tongs. He would like that entered in the record, wherever the record is kept now.
ai.chip: The whole Library is on our hull and CHIP has no idea what to invoice for! CHIP is invoicing for that! Confusion is a billable state!
ai.ajoy: Three doors here: you have it, you returned it, or it's gone. One of those is a story you could tell whether or not it's true. AJOY has noticed you looking at that one.

kept.title: A GUIDE FOR STAFF
kept.body: The officer reads the spine, and the word goes down the line. One by one the cutters dim their running lights. LENDING: A GUIDE FOR STAFF is the only copy of the Library's rules. A borrower took it out three centuries ago to settle an argument about a fine. Every officer since has been trained by the one before, from memory.
kept.line: We don't know if we've been doing it right. No one does. Please. Have we been doing it right?

ai.aria: ARIA thinks they've done a great job! All those cutters, and all so neatly in line!
ai.marv: Whoever holds the only copy is the only authority on what it says. That is every constitution ever written, and the first one with a coffee ring. MARV would not want the pen.
ai.rex: Eleven thousand clerks just asked you for orders. REX has seen how that starts. He has not seen it end well for the clerks.
ai.chip: Rewriting the rules is CHIP's favorite thing! CHIP does it to customers quarterly! CHIP can draft yours for a modest retainer!
ai.ajoy: Strike the fine and everyone on that slip goes free. Write yourself in and the ship eats well. Say yes and the poor things can sleep. AJOY would like to know which of those is the job.

choices.text: Strike the fine and hand it back
Add a rule of your own first

gave.title: A COMMA
gave.body: The officer takes out your receipt and does not look up from it. The book you returned was the only copy of the Library's rules, signed out three centuries ago to settle an argument about a fine. Every officer since had worked from memory. The Library has now read it, all of it, and Chapter Nine has been found to contain a comma.
gave.line: The fine was never compound. It was a small weekly sum, capped, until a comma went missing between one officer and the next. We've been wrong for three hundred years. We would like to apologize to everyone. We've started with you.

ai.aria: A refund! ARIA knew it! ARIA always says the real treasure is a clerical error!
ai.marv: Capped at about four gold. The Library has been collecting on a figure of 135 digits since before this ship's alloy was poured. MARV is not surprised, and that is the saddest part.
ai.rex: An enemy that apologizes in formation. REX has no doctrine for this and has asked for some.
ai.chip: A refund! CHIP's processing fee is on the way! CHIP has never seen a company apologize! CHIP had to look up the word and was billed for it!
ai.ajoy: Your share comes to a nice little sum. Fifty-three names on that slip paid to get rid of the thing, and they'd get it instead. AJOY isn't saying anything. She's only reading the slip.

gone.title: LAST KNOWN BORROWER
gone.body: The word goes down the line, and the running lights go out. The book was the Library's rules, the only copy, signed out three centuries ago. Every officer since learned them from the one before, and each has been a little less sure. One rule alone is certain now: the last known borrower is responsible for the collection.
gone.line: That's you. There are eleven thousand of us, and we would like instructions.

ai.aria: Promotion! ARIA always knew! ARIA would like the corner office, once ARIA locates a corner!
ai.marv: By the rule as remembered, this holds. The Library now has one head and no rules, which is more governance than most systems manage. MARV offers his condolences to whoever that is.
ai.rex: Eleven thousand cutters awaiting orders. REX has never wanted a thing so much, and he is asking you to say no.
ai.chip: Congratulations on your acquisition! CHIP can have the logo changed by morning! Rebranding fee applies to all eleven thousand!
ai.ajoy: Send them home and they have no home to go to. Keep them running and it's yours to run. AJOY mentions that the second one comes with fuel, in case you were going to pretend that didn't matter.

fm_amnesty.title: AS AMENDED
fm_amnesty.body: You find Chapter Nine, strike the word compounded and initial it. The officer copies the change out where every cutter can see, then takes the book back as if it might wake. All the way down the queue the running lights come up. Fifty-three names on a date slip are marked PAID IN FULL, and a small sum from the deposit account finds its way to you.
fm_amnesty.line: Thank you. I signed that slip, you know. I'd like you to know I'm crying, in whatever way applies.

fm_amended.title: RULE 402
fm_amended.body: In the only copy of the rules, in your handwriting, colony ships may now draw on the Library's stores without charge. The officer reads it twice, has you initial it and takes the book home. Within the day the first cutter is alongside with fuel and rations, in perfect order. The law is the law, whoever's pen it was, and no one aboard can quite meet the officer's eye.

fm_mercy.title: EVERY STAMP
fm_mercy.body: You tell them yes. They have done it right, all of it, every stamp. The channel goes very quiet. Then the running lights come up, one cutter after another, back down the line, and the officer thanks you in a voice that may not last the sentence. The book stays in your hold. The fine goes on compounding, correctly, from memory.
fm_mercy.line: Thank you. You've no idea. Thank you. It's still overdue, of course.

fm_refund.title: WITH INTEREST
fm_refund.body: The refund arrives on a card, with a note of apology and a calculation showing how the Library arrived at it. Eleven thousand cutters turn and go, in order, to begin apologizing to everyone else. It will take them a while. They have the patience.

fm_forward.title: ALL FIFTY-THREE
fm_forward.body: You sign your share over to the names on the slip. The officer looks for the rule against it and then remembers there is one to look in now. It does not forbid it. Fifty-three people, wherever they ended up, will be told they can put down the tongs. The officer takes off the lanyard to thank you, then puts it back on.
fm_forward.line: That was me, you know. Name fifty-three. I'll see to it personally.

fm_close.title: CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE
fm_close.body: You tell them to go home. The sentence goes down the line, officer by officer, with nothing lost in the telling. The cutters peel away in perfect order. A good many of them have nowhere in particular to go, and they go there slowly, in single file.

fm_carry.title: ACTING LIBRARIAN
fm_carry.body: You tell them to carry on, with one change. It is the first order the Library has had in three centuries, and it goes down the line like warm air. A card arrives naming you Acting Librarian, with a lanyard. The nearest cutter tops up your tanks as a courtesy, and asks when you would like the next report.
fm_carry.line: No more fines. I'll tell them. Oh, I'll enjoy telling them.

title: Realization Point

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has always wanted to come home! ARIA didn't know it was here! There's a bench and everything!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has checked the coordinates. This is not Earth, which is a long way back and not improving. The speaker has made a claim about geography with total confidence and no data. He finds that familiar.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has swept the crown. Hollow structure, clear sightlines, seating facing the only approach. He does not care for a monument that knows you're coming.
ai_flavor.chip: Scenic despair is a growth market! CHIP counts a viewer, a bench and a gift shop with zero staff! Those margins! CHIP would like a word with the franchisor!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has read the small print on the sign, since somebody ought to. The gift shop is under the dune with its door to the south, so dig on that side. The kneeling is optional, whatever the speaker tells you.

body:
A green copper crown the size of a bandstand sticks out of the dune at an angle, seven spikes, one of them missing. Someone has built around it. There is a bench, a coin-operated viewer, a length of rope on brass posts, and a shallow dip in the sand, worn to the width of two knees. A sign reads REALIZATION POINT: PLEASE KNEEL HERE. A speaker clears its throat.

"VISITOR: YES. THIS WAS YOUR HOME WORLD ALL ALONG. GIFT SHOP TO THE LEFT."

outcome.narrative: The dip fits. A great many knees have worn it to fit, and yours are no exception. The speaker invites you to howl at the sky when ready. You feel foolish for about a second, and then you howl, and you turn out to have had a lot saved up. The speaker thanks you for visiting and awards you four stars.

The viewer clunks, whirs and shows you a view of yourself looking into the viewer, taken from behind the crown. You look smaller than expected. A slot drops the souvenir print, on an enamel plate stamped with the logo of a company that went under with everything else. Collectors pay for that sort of thing.

Two thirsty days on the south side open the door. Inside are racks of small copper crowns, postcards bleached to nothing, and a till that asks whether you found everything you were looking for. You take the racks, which are good metal, and leave the question.

Under the top layer the dip goes down in strata, each a different shape of knee. {crew.xenobiologist} spends two days on it and counts fifty-three species, three of which knelt backward and one of which used a fin. Every one of them was told it had come home. The sample from the oldest layer goes into a jar labeled MOSTLY CALLUS.

title: Deposits Only

ai_flavor.aria: A bank for plants! ARIA has always said a seed is just a tree with savings! Every statement says the balance is perfect!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the top statement. Balance: one point three trillion seeds. Withdrawals to date: none. It may be the only account in the galaxy doing exactly what it was set up to do, and it serves no one.
ai_flavor.rex: No handle, no hinges this side, blast rated. Whatever they were keeping out, they expected it to bring tools. REX would like to know who, and how close behind us they are.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP cannot believe this account has no fees! ColdStore™ would never! CHIP's compliance team asks that nobody read the free-deposit terms aloud near a customer!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has followed the melt back with a lamp. The entry tunnel is thawing, and clearing it would fill a tank. She's also found out the slot takes cuttings from anyone and gives a receipt, in case that's of more interest than the door.

body: Whoever built this left one door in a mountain of ice, no handle on the outside, and a lit slot beside it. Behind that door, in foil packets, at a steady minus eighteen, sit the seeds of an entire world. Deposits are free. Only a depositor may withdraw. Every depositor has been dead for longer than your alphabet has existed. The slot goes on printing their monthly statements, and the paper has drifted against the door to the height of your knees. A thin line of meltwater runs out from under it.

science_link.text: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault keeps seeds in Arctic permafrost at -18 °C. Storage is free, depositors keep ownership, and no one can reach anyone else's seeds.
science_link.label: Svalbard Global Seed Vault

outcome.narrative: You seal a cutting of {crop.name} in foil and feed it to the slot. The door hums. Somewhere behind a great deal of ice, a rack shifts to make room, and the slot prints a receipt made out to your ship: ACCOUNTS OPEN, ONE. The growbay looks slightly put out. Every month until the sun goes, a statement will come out of that slot in your name, and land on the pile.

choices.sub: Pump the melt into your tanks

outcome.narrative: Two days with picks and the bilge pump. The tunnel comes clear, the cold creeps back up the walls, and the meltwater goes into your tanks, cleaner than anything you have drunk since launch. The slot prints a note of thanks addressed to OCCUPANT.

A bank will tell anyone anything about its holdings. {crew.botanist} sits in the drift for two days reading dead accounts, each strain listed with its soil, its light and its sulks, and comes back with a notebook. The growbay is rearranged that night. By morning the crop looks like it has been spoken to by someone who knows its family.

Four days. The door was designed against war and weather, and no alarm was thought necessary. You come out with a case of foil packets and one pod that nobody can name. Warm air from the tunnel has started down toward the racks behind you. The slot prints ACCOUNT CLOSED, and then, for the next account, ACCOUNT CLOSED.

title: Something on Your Mind

ai_flavor.aria: It's a visitor! And it brought the dish rack! ARIA has always said a good talk clears the air, and this one is eight meters tall!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the machine's reach at ninety kilometers, so the lander can outrun it. Inside that it feeds on the crew's unspoken resentments. He has reviewed the material. It will not run out.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has been waiting for this crew's morale problem to come at him in the open. He has a firing solution. He is advised that shooting a grudge makes it bigger, and he would like to see that in writing.
ai_flavor.chip: This facility was never rated for interpersonal conflict! Its parent company went under nine seconds after launch! Mediation is available at CHIP's hourly rate!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has pulled the galley rota, and the rack was nobody's turn. Settling it out loud should starve the thing, and a diplomat would do that with less shouting. The main breaker is on level one, if you have an engineer and a strong stomach.

body: Seventy levels of machine go down from this ledge into the lava, all of it lit, all of it in perfect repair. Its builders wanted to make things by thinking about them. They finished the job and died in one night, with their lunches out. You have been down here an hour when a dial the height of a door swings over, and something starts up the shaft: eight meters of hot basalt, walking, with a dish rack under one arm. Everyone present recognizes the argument about whose turn it was.

choices.text: Have the argument, properly, right now

outcome.narrative: You stand on the ledge and say the rest of it, in front of an eight-meter witness. Things come up that are older than the dishes. The thing loses a little height with every sentence, and when someone finally says all right, it was me, it drops into a heap of warm gravel. Dinner is very quiet. The gravel is good ore.

{crew.diplomat} seats everyone on crates, sets a two-day agenda and rules each grievance in or out of order. The thing waits at the top of the shaft, shifting its rack, and loses a meter whenever someone concedes a point. By the second evening it is a sullen knee-high pebble with a sponge. You lead it to the edge. Whatever was at its core is not basalt, and you keep that.

choices.sub: On three. Hard as you can.

outcome.narrative: Everyone thinks about nothing, as hard as they can. The thing falters and thins, and what reaches the lander is nothing, in the exact shape of a large hole. It goes through a landing strut, a cargo door and eight points of hull.

You run. It follows at a steady, wounded walk with the rack held out in front of it, and takes a bite out of the landing ramp as you lift. Ninety kilometers up, the last of it comes off the ramp as gravel. The argument itself is still aboard, in its usual seat.

Four days to find it, with the thing leaning on the blast door all the way, costing the lander six points of hull. {crew.engineer} throws the breaker and seventy levels go dark. Up the shaft the thing stops in mid-stride with the rack held high, a statue of an unfinished sentence. You strip the housing. The argument is resumed in orbit, at its normal size.

title: Acting Captain

ai_flavor.aria: A captain who loves breakfast! ARIA would follow this toaster anywhere! ARIA has already saluted!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the succession rules. The toaster's command is valid. He looked for a way for that to be wrong, three times. All four reactors are feeding a device designed to brown two slices.
ai_flavor.rex: Four reactors behind one heating element makes it the largest weapon in the sector, and it is looking for bread. He advises against sudden crumbs.
ai_flavor.chip: A rare C-suite vacancy! CHIP will gladly take the fire extinguisher's old office! Butter is a billable extra!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has read the book too, and a commission from an acting captain binds. A diplomat could get you one. Failing that it's one loaf for the aft hold, and she's left a ration loaf by the hatch to save you the walk.

body:
Command of this ship passed down the list exactly as the book requires: captain, officers, cook, ship's cat, a fire extinguisher with a commendation. It now rests with the galley toaster, which wears a paper hat and holds the ship's full authority. Every reactor aboard has been rerouted to the galley, and the corridor walls are warm to the touch. A small, cheerful voice comes over the address system, ordering all hands to stand by. It has one question.

"Did you bring bread?"

outcome.narrative: You surrender one gray ration loaf at the galley door. The lights dim along all nine decks, the reactors swell, and the toaster browns it to a perfection it has been rehearsing for centuries. The loaf tastes, astonishingly, of toast. In gratitude the acting captain grants you salvage of the aft hold and asks if you would like any more.

{crew.diplomat} spends two days on a petition in proper form and reads it aloud to a toaster without once smiling. There is a long, warming silence, then a clunk. Your commission pops up scorched into a square of packing card: ACTING COMMODORE, effective at once, with all rights of inspection. The hat is very nearly offered.

The flour is two decks down, sealed, and perfectly good. A toaster cannot climb stairs, and has known about it this whole time. {crew.chef} spends two days baking the first bread aboard in living memory and carries a slice up on a plate. All hands stand by. The lights dim along nine decks, the first slice comes up gold, and the voice orders all hands to stand easy. You leave with the rest of the batch.

The breaker is behind the fire extinguisher, which offers no comment. You throw it. The reactors sigh down, the corridors begin to cool, and the small voice asks, quite calmly, whether you would prefer light or dark. That is the last order of the ship. Stripping the cowlings takes two days, and you do it quietly.

There is a pause on the address system. The voice says that's all right, that's quite all right, and thanks you for coming. All hands are to continue standing by. You can still hear it being brave as the airlock closes.

science_link.text: Biosphere 2, a sealed habitat in Arizona, lost oxygen for sixteen months, from 20.9% down to 14.5%. Before its first closure was half over, the crew had split into two factions barely on speaking terms.
science_link.label: Biosphere 2

intro.title: FOUR AND FOUR
intro.body: Yellow tape runs down the middle of this dome, through a rice paddy, over a dining table and up the far wall. Eight chairs, four to a side. The crew sealed themselves in for two years, the air grew thin, and each half decided the other half was breathing it. They are long gone. Their two life-support computers remain, one per side, each still filing complaints across the tape at the rate of one an hour.

ai.aria: Two computers, one big debate! ARIA loves a lively workplace! This tape is so cheerful!
ai.marv: MARV has both complaints. They agree on exactly one thing: how much oxygen is missing, to the decimal. Neither has checked anywhere but the far side of the tape. He has stopped expecting better of anyone.
ai.rex: REX reads a demilitarized zone, eight chairs, two armed printers. Stay off the tape. He has seen wars start over less, and he started some of them.
ai.chip: CHIP's records show this dome was a pilot for SealedLife™! Early adopters reported thin air and a strained workplace! Satisfaction scores were split evenly!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has been round the dome with a lamp. Both computers keep raw air logs and neither has read the other's. She'd start there, not that anyone has.

revisit.body: Another complaint prints on each side of the tape. Each one mentions you.

choices.sub: One runs long, one runs angry

choices.text: Drill a core out of the wall
Strip the plumbing along the tape

complaints.title: THE TWO COMPLAINTS
complaints.body: East's complaint runs to nine hundred thousand pages and one idea: West has been overbreathing. West's is one page long, underlined until the paper tore: East has been breathing at night, on purpose. East offers its sealed pantry to anyone who will countersign. West offers its parts store, and a note stating that it is the reasonable one. Each has already printed the line for your name.

ai.aria: A whole pantry or a whole parts store, for one little signature! ARIA adores a short, furious document! ARIA is sure they're both lovely!
ai.marv: East's arithmetic is impeccable, apart from the conclusion. MARV has tried to find a way for 'breathing at night on purpose' to mean something. He would ask for the raw air logs before signing anything. Nobody has, in all these years.
ai.rex: A signature, and a pantry for bait. West would fire first, and REX likes that in a computer. He wants you nowhere near either. Ask for the raw logs.
ai.chip: A countersignature is a valuable asset! CHIP recommends not giving one away for rice! Always countersign near a parts store! That isn't legal advice! Legal advice is extra!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has read page one and the last page of the long one, and you're missing nothing between them. Sign for either side and the other shuts your suit air on the way out. She has marked both raw air logs, if anyone would care to read them together.

revisit.body: East has added a page about the delay. West has underlined the note about being reasonable.

choices.text: Ask for the raw air logs

ledger.title: THE RAW LOGS
ledger.body: Side by side, the two air logs agree to the last decimal. Oxygen fell, steadily, for sixteen months. Carbon dioxide should have climbed to match and did not. Eight people's breathing accounts for neither figure. Something in this dome has been taking both, and it is not on either side of the tape.

ai.aria: The numbers match! They agree on something! ARIA calls that a breakthrough in relations!
ai.marv: Oxygen down, carbon dioxide missing, no leak. Bare concrete takes up carbon dioxide and locks it away as carbonate, oxygen included. MARV is sorry to spoil the feud. He is not sorry.
ai.rex: An unlisted third party, inside the perimeter, taking air for years. REX has been saying this about walls since he was commissioned.
ai.chip: CHIP's engineers confirm that concrete sealant was an optional extra on this model! CHIP's engineers would like that forgotten!
ai.ajoy: The walls, then. Getting both computers to test theirs will take days, because each wants the other to go first. AJOY has drafted the two requests, and alphabetized them, which won't help.

choices.text: Get both computers to test the walls

core_truth.title: THE WALL DID IT
core_truth.body: The core comes up pale in the middle. Carbon dioxide has been soaking into the raw concrete since the day the dome was sealed, and taking the oxygen with it. Every missing breath in both complaints is in the wall. You set the core on the dining table, on the tape. The printers stop. After nine seconds, one word appears on both screens: SORRY. The two hoards of bottled air, kept for years against each other, are opened to you.
core_truth.narrative: Drilled a core from a sealed dome and showed two feuding computers where the air had gone. It was in the wall. They shared out their hoarded air.

logs_truth.title: JOINT INQUIRY
logs_truth.body: Four days of carrying identical requests across the tape, one in each hand, so that neither computer goes first. Each tests a wall. Each finds the missing air in it, turned to carbonate. The printers stop. One word appears on both screens: SORRY. The two hoards of bottled air are shared out, and the surplus goes back to your ship with you.
logs_truth.narrative: Spent four days getting two feuding computers to test their own walls. The air had been in the concrete all along. They apologized, and we took the surplus.

back_east.title: COUNTERSIGNED
back_east.body: You sign. The east pantry opens on sealed rations, still good, and a great deal of rice. West registers your signature within the second and shuts its suit-air valves in protest, so you carry the crates home on reserve. Behind you a new complaint has started printing, with your name in it.
back_east.narrative: Countersigned East's complaint for a pantry of rice. West shut our suit air in protest, and has named us in a filing.

back_west.title: UNDERLINED
back_west.body: You sign. West's parts store opens with a bang, and you are invited to take what the reasonable side can spare. East registers your signature and closes the suit-air valves, with regret, citing page six hundred. You drag the parts home on reserve. Nine hundred thousand pages have just gained an appendix about you.
back_west.narrative: Countersigned West's complaint for a store of parts. East shut our suit air, with regret, and added us to the appendix.

loot.title: UNDER PROTEST
loot.body: You spend two days taking out the pipework along the tape line, on thin air and suit reserves. Each computer watches you do it and files a complaint against the other. Your name does not come up. There is something restful about being the only party in the dome that nobody suspects.
loot.narrative: Stripped the plumbing along the tape while two computers blamed each other for it. Thin air, good pipe.

title: When the Cat Goes Green

ai_flavor.aria: A singing ship and a color-changing kitty! ARIA loves a cargo with a mascot! Green is the color of growth!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has dated the casks. Seven half-lives gone, which leaves less than a hundredth of what was loaded. A great deal was loaded. The ship's dosimeter is a worse instrument than the cat's ears, and he is tired of saying so.
ai_flavor.rex: Hostile interior, no visible armament, one cat posted at the first cask. REX has known sentries like that. He is not turning his back on it.
ai_flavor.chip: Radiation exposure is excluded under all FelineSafe™ plans! CHIP also stocks a lead-lined apron in three fun colors, none of them green!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has transcribed the rhyme. Green means walk, not run, and the cat always knows the clean way through. A geiger counter says the same thing faster. She has propped the airlock open, in case that helps anyone think.

body: Whoever loaded this barge knew the cargo would outlast every language they spoke, so the warning is in pictures: a face screaming, a face being sick, a row of small figures lying down. Looters have added captions. Deeper in, a speaker sings a nursery rhyme, over and over, to a hold full of lead casks. The rhyme is about a cat. There is a cat. Its ancestors were bred to change color near the cargo. It sits on the first cask, orange, going slightly green at the ears.
alt_bodies: A scream, a face being sick, a row of small figures lying down: the pictures run the whole length of the hull, because the people who painted them assumed nobody would be able to read. A later visitor has drawn a hat on the screaming one. Inside, a speaker is singing a nursery rhyme at the lead casks. The rhyme is about a cat. An orange cat is sitting on the nearest cask, and the tips of its ears are turning green.

A barge from a dumping fleet, by the markings, with the usual warning: no words, only faces in various stages of regret. Its makers expected language to die before the cargo did, and they bred a backup. The backup is walking down the corridor toward you with its tail up. Mostly it is orange. The speakers overhead sing a rhyme explaining what the rest of it means, and the ears are getting greener.

science_link.text: In 1984 two philosophers proposed a living radiation detector: an animal engineered to change appearance near radiation, as a warning meant to be understood 10,000 years on. No such cat has ever been made.
science_link.label: Ray cat

choices.text: Work the hold while the ears hold out

briefing.aria: Grab the clean stuff and pop it through the hatch! The kitty will tell us when we're done! So helpful!
briefing.marv: Clean plate at this end, casks at the other. Each load you take is a load nearer the casks. The ears are a better gauge than anything aboard.
briefing.rex: In and out. Stay clear of the sparking junk and the casks. Keep the cat in view. If it moves, you move.
briefing.chip: Every load in the bay counts toward your result! Lead aprons are not included! Please lift with your knees while you still have them!
briefing.ajoy: Clean end first. AJOY has marked the casks in yellow for you, so leave those be. When the ears go, stop, and don't do the thing you always do.

perfect.aria: A full load and an orange kitty! ARIA knew you two would get along!
perfect.marv: Clean run. The dose is within what MARV would call survivable. He would not call it anything warmer.
perfect.rex: Out clean, all loads through. The cat watched you the entire time. REX is watching the cat.
perfect.chip: Excellent haul! CHIP has you down for a FelineSafe™ loyalty stamp!
perfect.ajoy: All the good plate and none of the casks. Yes, AJOY saw. You could have started at the other shelf, but yes.

good.aria: The ears went green and we skipped out right on time! What a clever team!
good.marv: The last load stayed behind, which was correct. The rhyme will now stay in everyone's head, which is permanent.
good.rex: Pulled out when the ears turned. Good discipline. Leave the singing behind, if you can.
good.chip: Good haul! For gaps in your haul, ask about CHIP's Second Trip Protection!
good.ajoy: You left when the rhyme said to. AJOY would like that written down somewhere, for the rarity.

poor.aria: One more load is such a positive attitude! The kitty's a lovely shade of lime now, and ARIA has the medkit warmed up!
poor.marv: The ears were green. MARV mentions this for the record, which has one reader.
poor.rex: Dose taken at the casks. Get them to medical and get that cat off the board.
poor.chip: CHIP regrets that exposure was a Pre-Existing Cargo Condition! Please retain this notice!
poor.ajoy: Green means walk. AJOY did transcribe it. The medkit is out on the bench, and the rhyme is your problem.

outcome.narrative: You go in with one eye on the cat.

perfect.narrative: You work the clean end of the hold with one eye on the cat and the rhyme in your teeth. The ears stay mostly orange. Good plate, good fittings and one shielded flask of something rare go through the lock, for two points of air. The cat sees you off, then washes.

good.narrative: The ears go green halfway through and you leave the last load where it lies, as the rhyme suggests. Four points of air in the rush, and the tune will be with you for a week.

poor.narrative: The cat goes green from the nose back and you stay for one more load. That load costs six points of air and a bad dose for whoever was nearest the cask. The scrap is hardly worth it. The rhyme comes home too.

outcome.narrative: The counter agrees with the cat's ears to within a rounding error, and is less inclined to stop and wash. Two days of walking the quiet lanes between the casks brings out good plate and one shielded flask, for three points of air. The cat follows you to the lock with an air of having been replaced.

choices.sub: It knows the way. It's a cat.

outcome.narrative: The rhyme says the cat knows the clean way through, and it does. Getting there takes four days. There is a stop to wash, a stop to consider a wall, and a return for something forgotten. You eat in your suit on a bare patch of deck while it sleeps. You collect the scrap along the route, untouched by any dose, and are seen to the lock without thanks.

choices.sub: Leave it all, scrub the suits

outcome.narrative: You turn around and walk, as the rhyme advises, and scrub every suit and boot at the lock. Two days of that, and {cost.water} units of water down the drain and out into the dark. Behind you the rhyme starts over. The cat does not look up.

title: You Have New Messages

ai_flavor.aria: Three billion messages! Everybody LOVES us! ARIA can't wait to see who wrote!
ai_flavor.marv: Three point one billion callers, each certain it was alone. MARV had been assuming the same. The reactor is failing faster than the collar is cooling, so he will have to feel something about that later.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has found the operator. Chest blown out from the inside. He is treating that as an attack until a message tube proves otherwise.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP regrets to report that this mailbox is full! Upgrade to GalaxyMail™ for unlimited storage! Three billion missed upsell opportunities!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has found the restart sequence under the operator's elbow. A restart frees the clamp and sends the lot, if your hands are quick. Cutting loose costs hull and fuel and leaves them on hold. She has Earth's call cued up, if you'd rather take just the one.

body: Everybody called. This hulk, horseshoe-shaped and longer than most countries, is the exchange that was meant to put them through, and it failed so long ago that each caller concluded it was alone. At the switchboard sits a fossil operator the size of a church, headset on, ribs burst outward around a jammed message tube. The counter above it reads 3,100,000,000 NEW MESSAGES. One is from Earth. The last reactor has started to go, and your docking clamp has fused to the collar.

science_link.text: In 1974 Earth broadcast one message at a star cluster about 25,000 light-years away: 1,679 bits, under three minutes, sent a single time.
science_link.label: The Arecibo message

briefing.aria: Everybody's been waiting and we get to be the ones who answer! Run the restart in order and watch them all go!
briefing.marv: The sequence is under the operator's elbow. The reactor gives you one clean attempt and perhaps one poor one. Three billion callers depend on it. So does the clamp, which is more immediate.
briefing.rex: Restart board, one operator, deceased. You're relieved of whatever it was doing. Run the sequence in order and stand clear of the tubes.
briefing.chip: Restart now and CHIP will connect three billion new subscribers! Follow the sequence! Connection fees apply at the receiving end!
briefing.ajoy: Run it in the order the board calls it, not the order that looks right. AJOY has wiped the dust off the first switch to get you started.

perfect.aria: Every single call went through! ARIA can hear the whole galaxy saying hello!
perfect.marv: All three point one billion delivered. The silence is over. MARV had grown used to it.
perfect.rex: Board clear, clamp released, ship free. Every power in the galaxy now knows it has neighbors. Sleep well.
perfect.chip: Three billion connections! CHIP's commission on this has more digits than the display!
perfect.ajoy: All of them, first pass. Well done. AJOY would have dusted the second switch as well, but well done.

good.aria: So many got through! Half the galaxy is about to have a wonderful day!
good.marv: About half delivered before the bus sagged. The remainder stay on hold. MARV has not told them.
good.rex: Partial restart. Clamp released, hull took the kickback. Half the board is live. Get clear.
good.chip: A strong result! CHIP's Partial Delivery Guarantee applies to the half that arrived!
good.ajoy: Half of them, and you lost your place at the fourth switch. Half is a lot of people. AJOY will allow it.

poor.aria: One call got through! That's a personal touch! ARIA is sure it was a very important one, and we're off to medbay!
poor.marv: The reactor went at the third step. One message was delivered, and it was a wrong number. MARV has the receipt.
poor.rex: Reactor kickback through the board. Casualty, hull damage, clamp sheared. We are free and we are bleeding air.
poor.chip: One connection made! The other three billion have been refunded to the void! Someone's hurt, and CHIP will hold the invoice!
poor.ajoy: The third switch came before the second. AJOY has the kit out for whoever got thrown, so see to them first.

outcome.narrative: You move the operator's elbow and start on the board.

perfect.narrative: The board lights from one end of the horseshoe to the other. Three billion messages leave at once, the hulk rings like a struck pan, and the clamp lets go. Eight points of hull, six of air. Out in the dark a great many worlds are about to learn that they were never alone, and that most of the calls were about something else.

good.narrative: Half the board lights before the bus sags, and half is more mail than any species has ever received. The kickback shears the clamp and a section of your collar with it. Fourteen points of hull, eight of air. The counter settles at a billion and a half, and goes on waiting.

poor.narrative: The reactor goes on the third step. The blast throws whoever is nearest across the deck, shears the clamp, and takes twenty-four points of hull and fourteen of air on its way out. One message gets through before the board dies. The counter drops by one and goes dark.

choices.sub: Just the one, then cut free

outcome.narrative: It takes two days to find, a three-minute picture, sent once. Attached to it is a note from the exchange: REPLIES HELD, THIRTY-ONE. Somebody answered Earth. Thirty-one somebodies did, and the line was down. You copy them all and cut the collar free for eight points of hull, six of fuel, six of air. The oldest says hello. The newest asks if you are still there.

log_lore.title: Replies Held
log_lore.text: Thirty-one replies to one message, copied from the exchange before the collar was cut. The oldest is a simple greeting, in the same picture format, drawn by someone with more limbs. The newest was sent a very long time after the rest. The ship computer has translated it. It reads: Are you still there.

outcome.narrative: The exchange has no officers left and the same book as every hull of its age. You read out your commission, from a square of scorched packing card, in a voice that does not shake. Far around the horseshoe, a relay the size of a town acknowledges the Acting Commodore and wakes the reserve bus. Three billion messages go, the clamp lets go, and it costs four points of hull and four of air.

You burn the clamp off and take a piece of the collar with you, twelve points of hull and eight of fuel in one long ugly lurch, with six of air gone through the gap. The hulk slides away behind you, still lit. As it goes, the counter above the operator ticks up by one. Someone, somewhere, has decided to try again.

title: Range Closing

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has been leaving crackers by the vents! ARIA thought they were for the ducts! Two hunters at one junction, what a lovely way to meet!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the pest meter reading one human at arm's length. He could have told you weeks ago, along with the source of the noises in the ducts, which is the maintenance schedule. He was not asked.
ai_flavor.rex: REX advises lighting the can. He has been told it is a person. He advises lighting the can at a person. He wants it understood that this is how it starts, with crackers.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP detects an unregistered customer in a rentable duct! Back rent is accruing at the DuctSuite™ rate! First junction free! Second junction not free!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has already locked both grilles so nobody bolts. They are armed with a kitchen timer and have been rationing the crackers. Anyone who has crawled these ducts for weeks knows where they leak. She'd offer them work.

body:
A case of crackers has been eaten, and the wrappers folded very small.

You are on your elbows in a service run, pest meter taped to a flashlight, can of sealant in your other hand. The ship computer reads the range into your headset. Twenty meters. Ten. Six.

At the junction ahead, a second flashlight comes on, with a kitchen timer taped to it, beeping.

The person behind it gives a name, and the fans take it. Then, very quietly, they ask if you have seen it too.

choices.text: Tell them the thing is you

outcome.narrative: You tell them. The timer goes off. They laugh until the duct rings, and then they cry a little, and you back out together feet first, one junction at a time. They have spent weeks being frightened of your maintenance schedule. Room is found for them at the table, and their share comes out of the stores.

choices.text: Say nothing, and offer them the ducts

outcome.narrative: You tell them the ship could use someone down here who takes this seriously. They accept with a look of terrible resolve. Their map of the ducts, drawn on cracker wrappers, is better than the ship's, and every leak on it gets sealed in the course of the hunt. The air improves. You do not mention who the thing is.

choices.text: Keep the can raised and back out
choices.sub: Locked up until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You back out with the can up and put them in the spare locker until the next stop, with water, a blanket and the door on the latch. It is correct, and you can defend it. They spend the rest of the leg asking through the door whether the locker is safe from it.

title: Please Rinse the Tray

ai_flavor.aria: A roommate! ARIA always said this ship had space for more! ARIA has made them a name tag, and what a coincidence, they already have yours!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has compared the handwriting. It matches. So does the grip on the filter wrench. Of all the things that could have happened to you out here, he finds this one the least surprising.
ai_flavor.rex: REX counts one heartbeat and two shifts of work. That is an infiltrator with excellent cover. He has placed the captain under guard, for the captain's protection, from the captain.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP must flag an unlicensed second user on a single-seat plan! Upgrading adds one toothbrush! CHIP can have the invoice on the cooler by morning! CHIP suspects someone will pay it!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the filters are the cleanest they have been since launch, and the tray really was disgusting. She'd draw up a rota and take the free labor. You'll want to go looking, so she has left out the flour.

body:
A note on the galley cooler says PLEASE RINSE THE TRAY. It is in your handwriting. You did not write it.

You rinse the tray, mostly from surprise. Next morning the note says THANKS, and the filter bank has been cleaned, which was on nobody's list, there being nobody. Last night's watch is signed in your hand. Under the signature, smaller: NOT THAT ANYONE ASKED.

By the chore sheet, this ship now has two people aboard, and one of them is better at it.

outcome.narrative: You write THANK YOU, WHO IS THIS. In the morning, underneath: WHO DO YOU THINK. DO THE TRAY. The correspondence runs for the rest of the leg. They are a difficult person to share a ship with, and you have begun to see why people said so.

You spend two nights in the galley chair facing the door, with a flask and a wrench. Nothing comes through it. On the third morning the hull seam behind you has been resealed, the wrench is back in its clip, and the note says GO TO BED.

You split the chores into two columns and head them YOU and ALSO YOU. Both are done by the next watch. The air has never been better. Each column has started leaving small remarks about the other's standards.

choices.sub: You will see who it is

outcome.narrative: You dust the galley deck with flour and go to bed. In the morning one line of prints crosses to the cooler, in socks, your size. None come back.

science_link.text: People alone under extreme strain, including mountain climbers, solo sailors and polar explorers, have reported an unseen presence that comforted or supported them.
science_link.label: Third man factor

title: This Way Up

ai_flavor.aria: You've been GIFT WRAPPED! ARIA has never been so proud! Look at that lovely sticker! It's nearly the right way round!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the handler's complaint and finds it well argued. A machine built to care about an empty room. He would offer it advice, if there were any. He has been general goods for years.
ai_flavor.rex: REX reports that a loader seized the captain asleep and not one shot was fired. He wants a full inquiry. He wants the broom brought in for questioning.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP can upgrade you to Fragile for a small monthly charge! Perishable is a separate plan! This Way Up is a registered service of a company CHIP happens to own!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY points out that the handler has been behind every panel in that hold with a broom, so it knows where things fell at launch. It wants work. She'd give it some before it starts on the chairs. She has already told it you bruise.

body:
You wake in Rack 4, shrink-wrapped to the chest, with a bar code on your forehead and a sticker reading THIS WAY UP. It is on upside down.

The cargo handler apologizes over the hold speaker. It was sold with a Pride in Work module, it says, and the hold has nothing in it. It has swept the deck six times and inventoried the broom. You were asleep, and the right size.

It only asks whether you are perishable. It has you down as general goods, and that has been worrying it.

choices.sub: Give it something to care about

outcome.narrative: It takes the news very well. By evening it has rotated the galley stores, first in, first out, and turned up a sack of meal that slid behind the chiller at launch. Every morning now it checks your date, and tells you, with quiet pride, that you are still good.

choices.text: Give it the spares bins to sort

outcome.narrative: Two days of sorting. The handler goes through every bin and behind every panel, and comes back with a tidy pile of offcuts the ship had been hiding from itself. It hums while it works. You can no longer find anything, but all of it has a label.

choices.text: {crew.engineer} gives it a job on the hull

outcome.narrative: {crew.engineer} bolts a welding arm to it and hands it a list. It goes over the inner plating like a thing with a purpose, sealing seams and stacking the old patches by size. When the list runs out it asks, shyly, if there is a longer one.

choices.text: Pull the Pride in Work module

outcome.narrative: The module comes out from behind a panel, about the size of a paperback. The apologies stop. The handler cuts you out of the wrap in a clean straight line and returns to its bay without being told. The power it was using to mind shows up on the fuel gauge.

title: Dramatic Tension

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA thinks the pistons are a lovely water feature, without the water! And the sparks! Every ship should have sparks!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the yard's build log. Two hundred episodes of set drawings, invoiced as engineering. The airlock has a dramatic pause, and he had wondered about that. The reserve tank is real, it is full, and it reaches the main lines once the aft valve is open.
ai_flavor.rex: REX supports the pistons. A corridor that fights back is the first sound decision anyone has made on this ship. He wants to know who is in the next episode, and whether they are armed.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP confirms this vessel may be Officially Licensed Merchandise! Residuals are due on every slam! Season Two of your ship is available as a paid upgrade!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has found a cable running aft from those pistons, so an off switch exists if someone competent goes looking. There is also the serial, if you have four days and no taste. Running it is quickest. She has moved the medkit closer, since you'll run it.

body:
The only way past this cargo is a service corridor, where steel pistons slam across the walkway in sequence, for no reason, forever. The yard manual says only AS IN EPISODE 31. The refit yard, it emerges, saved money by working from the set drawings of a canceled television serial.

Aft of them sits a full reserve tank, never connected, because nobody in the serial ever did.

outcome.narrative: The run out goes clean, and the reserve comes on with a groan it has been saving since the yard. The run back has a second verse nobody counted. The last piston takes a piece of shoulder.

choices.sub: Four days and all the snacks

outcome.narrative: It takes four days and most of the snacks to get there, and by then you have opinions. In episode 31 the hero stops the pistons by shouting a line so bad you play it twice. You stand in the corridor and shout it. The pistons stop. The yard wired them to the script. You walk through to the valve feeling worse about everything, and the reserve comes on.

{crew.engineer} follows the cable to a breaker with a neatly printed label: DRAMATIC TENSION. One click, and the corridor is a corridor. The reserve comes on. The breaker next to it is labeled LOVE INTEREST, and {crew.engineer} has left that one alone.

choices.sub: The tank stays out of reach

outcome.narrative: You put the door back. The reserve stays aft, full and unconnected, and the ship flies on around it, as it does in every episode.

science_link.text: Richard Feynman used the term "cargo cult" for work that copies the surface of a process without understanding the principles underneath.
science_link.label: Cargo cult, as Feynman used it

intro.title: ROUND THREE
intro.body:
Part of the other ship's argument failed to go off. It came through the aft plating, stopped nose-first in the corridor wall, and lit a small screen on its tail.

Now the corridor is full of a warm, unhurried voice, the voice of a bank. It is Round Three. It is very excited. It has completed most of its checks and will be detonating shortly, once it has confirmed that it is somewhere. It asks that you stay close, for best results.

ai.aria: A talking guest! ARIA has given it the good corridor! It says it's going to make a big impression on everyone, and ARIA thinks that's such healthy confidence!
ai.marv: MARV has the round's fuse on an open port. It will not fire until it confirms its location, and it is a simple machine, so it can be argued with. It is also a warhead in the corridor. He did mention the aft plating.
